177|## How each attempt is judged
178|
179|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
182|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
183|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
184|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
185|
186|   At every size:
187|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
188|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
189|
190|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
191|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
192|3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.
193|
194|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
195|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
196|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
197|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.
198|
199|**The piece timing** runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and waits for the GPU once at the end. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.
200|
201|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and beats the compiled reference in the piece timing at all three row counts, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

1|# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.
6|
7|## Hardware limits
8|
9|**Peak bandwidth**:
10|The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
11|_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed
12|
13|**Peak compute**:
14|The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
15|_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)
16|
17|**Achieved bandwidth**:
18|The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
19|_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)
20|
21|**Arithmetic intensity**:
22|Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
23|_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio
24|
25|**Ridge point**:
26|The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.
27|
28|**Roofline**:
29|The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.
30|
31|## Bottlenecks and fixes
32|
33|**Bandwidth-bound**:
34|A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.
35|
36|**Compute-bound**:
37|A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.
38|
39|**Overhead-bound**:
40|A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
41|_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)
42|
43|**Bottleneck**:
44|The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
45|_Avoid_: issue, slowness
46|
47|**Kernel**:
48|One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
49|_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)
50|
51|**Occupancy**:
52|The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
53|_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)
54|
55|**Knock-out**:
56|A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
57|_Avoid_: ablation
58|
59|**Baseline**:
60|The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.
61|
62|**Fix**:
63|One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
64|_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak
65|
66|## Inference
67|
68|**Prefill**:
69|Processing a request's whole prompt in one pass before any token is generated.
70|
71|**Decode step**:
72|One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.
73|
74|**Decode rows**:
75|The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
76|_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency
77|
78|**Client concurrency**:
79|The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
80|_Avoid_: batch size

83|

86|
87|**Active experts**:

89|_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts

278|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
279|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")

282|def dim(expr, rows):
283|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
284|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
285|    if isinstance(expr, int):
286|        return expr
287|    value = 1
288|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
289|        if not TERM.match(term):
290|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
291|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
292|    return value

295|def template_value(v):
296|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
297|        return v
298|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
299|        return DTYPES[v]
300|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")

303|def build(spec, sources, slot):
304|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
305|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
306|    kernels = []
307|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
308|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
309|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
310|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
311|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
312|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
313|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
314|            header=header,
315|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
316|        )
317|        kernels.append((k, fn))
318|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
319|    if missing:
320|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
321|
322|    def run(**inputs):
323|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
324|        env = dict(inputs)
325|        for k, fn in kernels:
326|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
327|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
328|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
329|            outs = fn(
330|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
331|                template=[
332|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
333|                ],
334|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
335|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
336|                output_shapes=[
337|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
338|                ],
339|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
340|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
341|            )
342|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
343|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
344|
345|    return run

65|class Attention(nn.Module):
66|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs, use_rope: bool):
67|        super().__init__()
68|        dim = args.hidden_size
69|        self.n_heads = args.num_attention_heads
70|        self.n_kv_heads = args.num_key_value_heads
71|        self.head_dim = args.head_dim
72|        self.scale = self.head_dim**-0.5
73|
74|        bias = args.attention_bias
75|        self.q_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
76|        self.k_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
77|        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
78|        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(self.n_heads * self.head_dim, dim, bias=bias)
79|
80|        self.use_rope = use_rope
81|        if use_rope:
82|            self.rope = initialize_rope(
83|                self.head_dim,
84|                args.rope_theta,
85|                traditional=True,
86|                scaling_config=args.rope_scaling,
87|                max_position_embeddings=args.max_position_embeddings,
88|            )
89|
90|        # The reference applies this norm after RoPE. RoPE does not change
91|        # the vector norm, so applying it before RoPE gives the same result.
92|        self.use_qk_norm = args.use_qk_norm and use_rope
93|        if self.use_qk_norm:
94|            self.q_norm = QKNorm(args.rms_norm_eps)
95|            self.k_norm = QKNorm(args.rms_norm_eps)
96|
97|    def __call__(
98|        self,
99|        x: mx.array,
100|        mask: Optional[mx.array] = None,
101|        cache: Optional[Any] = None,
102|    ) -> mx.array:
103|        B, L, _ = x.shape
104|        queries = self.q_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_heads, -1)
105|        keys = self.k_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_kv_heads, -1)
106|        values = self.v_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_kv_heads, -1)
107|
108|        if self.use_qk_norm:
109|            queries = self.q_norm(queries)
110|            keys = self.k_norm(keys)
111|
112|        queries = queries.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
113|        keys = keys.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
114|        values = values.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
115|
116|        if self.use_rope:
117|            offset = cache.offset if cache is not None else 0
118|            queries = self.rope(queries, offset=offset)
119|            keys = self.rope(keys, offset=offset)
120|
121|        if cache is not None:
122|            keys, values = cache.update_and_fetch(keys, values)
123|
124|        output = scaled_dot_product_attention(
125|            queries, keys, values, cache=cache, scale=self.scale, mask=mask
126|        )
127|        output = output.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, L, -1)
128|        return self.o_proj(output)

142|class TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear(nn.Module):
143|    """Quantized expert weights in [E, in, out] layout, grouped along out."""

145|    def __init__(

187|class MoE(nn.Module):
188|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs):
189|        super().__init__()
190|        dim = args.hidden_size
191|        hidden = args.intermediate_size
192|        num_experts = args.num_local_experts
193|        self.top_k = args.num_experts_per_tok
194|        self.norm_topk_prob = args.norm_topk_prob
195|        self.routed_scaling_factor = args.routed_scaling_factor
196|
197|        self.router = nn.Linear(dim, num_experts, bias=False)
198|        self.expert_bias = mx.zeros((num_experts,))
199|        self.experts = SwitchGLU(dim, hidden, num_experts)
200|        if args.transposed_experts:
201|            q = args.quantization
202|            for name, dims in (
203|                ("gate_proj", (dim, hidden)),
204|                ("up_proj", (dim, hidden)),
205|                ("down_proj", (hidden, dim)),
206|            ):
207|                proj = TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear(
208|                    *dims,
209|                    num_experts,
210|                    q["group_size"],
211|                    q["bits"],
212|                    q.get("mode", "affine"),
213|                )
214|                setattr(self.experts, name, proj)
215|        self.shared_expert = MLP(dim, args.intermediate_size_mlp)
216|
217|    def __call__(self, x: mx.array) -> mx.array:
218|        # The reference computes the router in float32.
219|        scores = mx.sigmoid(self.router(x.astype(mx.float32)))
220|
221|        # The bias changes which experts are selected, not their weights.
222|        k = self.top_k
223|        biased = scores + self.expert_bias
224|        inds = mx.argpartition(-biased, kth=k - 1, axis=-1)[..., :k]
225|        scores = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
226|        if self.norm_topk_prob:
227|            scores = scores / (scores.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20)
228|        scores = scores * self.routed_scaling_factor
229|
230|        y = self.experts(x, inds)
231|        y = (y * scores[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(x.dtype)
232|        return y + self.shared_expert(x)

3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing chains the 20 layers, so
9|each call waits for the one before, as in a decode step. The grader prints
10|its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when given. It never writes into
11|the attempt folder, which holds only the Muse agent's files.
12|
13|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
14|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
15|
16|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run as the
17|candidate, and adds `beats_baseline`. From round 2 on, the bar is the previous
18|round's final attempt for the slot (claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md).
19|The two are timed in alternating repeats, so drift in the GPU's clocks reaches
20|both alike, and the candidate beats the baseline at a row count only if it is
21|faster in at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats: a one-sided sign
22|test at p < 0.01. The same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. FOLDER alone is an
24|attempt for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one
25|routing+combine attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.
26|"""
27|
28|import argparse
29|import json
30|import math
31|import statistics
32|import sys
33|import time
34|import traceback
35|from pathlib import Path
36|
37|import mlx.core as mx
38|import numpy as np
39|
40|sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
41|import gpu_lock  # noqa: E402
42|import slots  # noqa: E402
43|
44|ROWS = (1, 8, 32)
45|REPEATS = 30
46|WINS_NEEDED = next(  # 22 of 30
47|    k
48|    for k in range(REPEATS + 1)
49|    if sum(math.comb(REPEATS, i) for i in range(k, REPEATS + 1)) / 2**REPEATS < 0.01
50|)
51|
52|
53|def parts(slot):
54|    return ["routing", "combine"] if slot == "routing+combine" else [slot]
55|
56|
57|def load(attempt, slot):
58|    spec = json.loads((attempt / "spec.json").read_text())
59|    sources = [
60|        p.read_text()
61|        for p in sorted(attempt.glob("block-*.metal"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem[6:]))
62|    ]
63|    specs = spec if slot == "routing+combine" else {slot: spec}
64|    return {p: slots.build(specs[p], sources, p) for p in parts(slot)}
65|
66|
67|def baselines(values, slot):
68|    """The --baseline attempts' functions by part; they must cover the slot's parts."""
69|    fns = {}
70|    for value in values:
71|        name, sep, folder = value.rpartition("=")
72|        name = name if sep else slot
73|        if name not in slots.SLOTS:
74|            sys.exit(f"--baseline {value}: unknown slot {name!r}")
75|        try:
76|            fns |= load(Path(folder), name)
77|        except Exception as e:
78|            sys.exit(f"--baseline {value}: can't load it: {short_error(e)}")
79|    if sorted(fns) != sorted(parts(slot)):
80|        sys.exit(f"--baseline must cover {parts(slot)}, not {sorted(fns)}")
81|    return fns

84|def ulp_bf16(r):
85|    """bfloat16's unit in the last place at |r|, floored at |r| = 0.001 (brief, G2)."""
86|    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))
87|    return 2.0 ** (exp - 7)
88|
89|
90|def differences(g, r):
91|    """Elements of *g* that aren't *r*'s bit for bit, and the largest gap in units
92|    in the last place (floored at |r| = 0.001); "at" is the flat index of it."""
93|    differ = (g != r) & ~(np.isnan(g) & np.isnan(r))
94|    out = {"differ": int(differ.sum()), "max_ulp": 0.0}
95|    if out["differ"]:
96|        with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
97|            over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
98|        out |= {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "at": int(over.argmax())}
99|    return out

102|def check_routing(fn, layer):
103|    ref_inds, ref_w = slots.ref_routing(layer["x"], layer["w_router"], layer["bias"])
104|    got = fn(x=layer["x"], w_router=layer["w_router"], bias=layer["bias"])
105|    inds, w = got["inds"], got["weights"]
106|    rows = layer["x"].shape[0]
107|    if inds.shape != (rows, slots.K) or w.shape != (rows, slots.K):
108|        return {
109|            "error": f"shapes inds {inds.shape}, weights {w.shape}; want ({rows}, 4)"
110|        }
111|    if inds.dtype != mx.uint32 or w.dtype != mx.float32:
112|        return {
113|            "error": f"dtypes inds {inds.dtype}, weights {w.dtype}; want uint32, float32"
114|        }
115|    inds, w = np.array(inds), np.array(w)
116|    ref_inds, ref_w = np.array(ref_inds), np.array(ref_w)
117|    if inds.max() >= slots.E:
118|        return {"error": f"expert index {int(inds.max())} out of range (60 experts)"}
119|    # Exact, in order: combine sums the 4 pairs in this order.
120|    differ = (inds != ref_inds).any(axis=1) | (w != ref_w).any(axis=1)
121|    same_order = (inds == ref_inds).all(axis=1)
122|    rel = np.abs(w - ref_w)[same_order] / np.maximum(np.abs(ref_w[same_order]), 1e-12)
123|    out = {
124|        "rows_differ": int(differ.sum()),
125|        "rows_other_experts": int(
126|            sum(set(a) != set(b) for a, b in zip(inds.tolist(), ref_inds.tolist()))
127|        ),
128|        "max_rel_err": float(rel.max()) if rel.size else 0.0,
129|    }
130|    if out["rows_differ"]:
131|        r = int(differ.argmax())
132|        out["example"] = (
133|            f"row {r}: experts {inds[r].tolist()}, weights {w[r].tolist()}; "
134|            f"want {ref_inds[r].tolist()}, {ref_w[r].tolist()}"
135|        )
136|    return out
137|

139|def check_combine(fn, layer):
140|    ref = slots.ref_combine(layer["y"], layer["weights"], layer["shared"])
141|    got = fn(y=layer["y"], weights=layer["weights"], shared=layer["shared"])["out"]
142|    if got.shape != ref.shape or got.dtype != mx.bfloat16:
143|        return {"error": f"out {got.shape} {got.dtype}; want {ref.shape} bfloat16"}
144|    r = np.array(ref.astype(mx.float32))
145|    g = np.array(got.astype(mx.float32))
146|    out = differences(g, r)
147|    if out["differ"]:
148|        i, j = np.unravel_index(out.pop("at"), g.shape)
149|        out["example"] = f"row {i} column {j}: {g[i, j]:.6g}, want {r[i, j]:.6g}"
150|    return out
151|
152|
153|def check_experts(fn, layer):
154|    names = slots.SLOTS["experts"][0]
155|    args = [layer[n] for n in names]
156|    ref = slots.ref_experts(*args)
157|    got = fn(**{n: layer[n] for n in names})["y"]
158|    if got.shape != ref.shape or got.dtype != mx.bfloat16:
159|        return {"error": f"y {got.shape} {got.dtype}; want {ref.shape} bfloat16"}
160|    r = np.array(ref.astype(mx.float32)).reshape(ref.shape[0], -1)
161|    g = np.array(got.astype(mx.float32)).reshape(ref.shape[0], -1)
162|    out = differences(g, r)
163|    if out["differ"]:
164|        i, j = np.unravel_index(out.pop("at"), g.shape)
165|        k, d = divmod(j, slots.D)
166|        out["example"] = (
167|            f"row {i} expert slot {k} column {d}: {g[i, j]:.6g}, want {r[i, j]:.6g}"
168|        )
169|    return out

171|
172|def passes(part, s):
173|    if "error" in s:
174|        return False
175|    return s["rows_differ" if part == "routing" else "differ"] == 0

178|@mx.compile
179|def link(a, prev):
180|    """*a* unchanged, computed after *prev*: one small fused kernel."""
181|    return a + (prev.reshape(-1)[:1] * 0).astype(a.dtype)
182|
183|
184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs
202|
203|
204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)
214|
215|
216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:
221|            call()
222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
228|    return times
229|
230|
231|def short_error(e):
232|    """The exception, keeping only the compiler's error lines from Metal builds."""
233|    text = "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip()
234|    lines = text.splitlines()
235|    if len(lines) > 1 and "Unable to build metal library" in lines[0]:
236|        keep = [lines[0]]
237|        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
238|            if "error:" in line:
239|                keep += lines[i : i + 3]
240|        text = "\n".join(keep)
241|    return text[:4000]

244|def main():
245|    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
246|    ap.add_argument("attempt", type=Path)
247|    ap.add_argument("slot", choices=tuple(slots.SLOTS))
248|    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="also write the verdict here")
249|    ap.add_argument(
250|        "--baseline",
251|        action="append",
252|        default=[],
253|        metavar="[SLOT=]FOLDER",
254|        help="an earlier attempt to time in the same run (repeat for routing+combine)",
255|    )
256|    args = ap.parse_args()
257|    attempt, slot = args.attempt, args.slot
258|    gpu_lock.hold(f"check_candidate.py {attempt} {slot}")
259|    base = baselines(args.baseline, slot) if args.baseline else None
260|    result = {"slot": slot, "g1": False, "g2": False, "beats_compiled": False}
261|    if base:
262|        result |= {
263|            "baseline": args.baseline,
264|            "beats_baseline": False,
265|            "wins_needed": f"{WINS_NEEDED} of {REPEATS} paired repeats",
266|        }
267|    try:
268|        fns = load(attempt, slot)
269|        model = slots.load_model()
270|        weights = slots.model_expert_weights(model) if slot == "experts" else None
271|        stats = {}
272|        sizes = [("rows", lambda r=r: slots.load_inputs(r, weights)) for r in ROWS]
273|        sizes += [
274|            ("prefill rows", lambda r=r: slots.capture_prefill(model, r, weights))
275|            for r in slots.PROMPT_REQUESTS
276|        ]
277|        for kind, inputs in sizes:
278|            layers = inputs()
279|            size = f"{kind} {layers[0]['x'].shape[0]}"
280|            for part, fn in fns.items():
281|                check = {
282|                    "routing": check_routing,
283|                    "combine": check_combine,
284|                    "experts": check_experts,
285|                }[part]
286|                per_layer = [check(fn, layer) for layer in layers]
287|                errors = [s["error"] for s in per_layer if "error" in s]
288|                if errors:
289|                    stats[f"{part} {size}"] = {"error": errors[0]}
290|                    continue
291|                agg = {
292|                    k: (max if k.startswith("max") else sum)(s[k] for s in per_layer)
293|                    for k in per_layer[0]
294|                    if k != "example"
295|                }
296|                agg["pass"] = all(passes(part, s) for s in per_layer)
297|                examples = [
298|                    f"layer {i}, {s['example']}"
299|                    for i, s in enumerate(per_layer)
300|                    if "example" in s
301|                ]
302|                if examples:
303|                    agg["worst_example"] = examples[0]
304|                stats[f"{part} {size}"] = agg
305|            del layers
306|        result["g1"] = True
307|        result["correctness"] = stats
308|        result["g2"] = all(s.get("pass") for s in stats.values())
309|        if result["g2"]:
310|            timing, beats, beats_base = {}, True, True
311|            for rows in ROWS:
312|                layers = slots.load_inputs(rows, weights)
313|                row = {"reference": 0.0, "compiled": 0.0, "candidate": 0.0}
314|                base_t, cand_t = [0.0] * REPEATS, [0.0] * REPEATS
315|                for part, fn in fns.items():
316|                    names = slots.SLOTS[part][0]
317|                    ref = slots.REFERENCE[part]
318|                    wrap = lambda f: lambda **kw: f(
319|                        *[kw[n] for n in names]
320|                    )  # noqa: E731
321|                    row["reference"] += timed(wrap(ref), layers, names)
322|                    row["compiled"] += timed(wrap(mx.compile(ref)), layers, names)
323|                    if base:
324|                        b, c = paired_times([base[part], fn], layers, names)
325|                        base_t = [t + u for t, u in zip(base_t, b)]
326|                        cand_t = [t + u for t, u in zip(cand_t, c)]
327|                    else:
328|                        row["candidate"] += timed(fn, layers, names)
329|                if base:
330|                    row["candidate"] = statistics.median(cand_t)
331|                    row["baseline"] = statistics.median(base_t)
332|                    row["wins_vs_baseline"] = sum(c < b for b, c in zip(base_t, cand_t))
333|                    beats_base &= row["wins_vs_baseline"] >= WINS_NEEDED
334|                timing[f"rows {rows}"] = {k: round(v, 1) for k, v in row.items()}
335|                beats &= row["candidate"] < row["compiled"]
336|            result["timing_us_per_layer"] = timing
337|            result["beats_compiled"] = beats
338|            if base:
339|                result["beats_baseline"] = beats_base
340|    except Exception as e:  # report the failure to the Muse agent as G1
341|        result["error"] = short_error(e)
342|    if args.out:
343|        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
344|        args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1) + "\n")
345|    print(json.dumps(result))

1|# Round 1 of the Muse agent, measured
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|In round 1 (2026-11-03), the Muse agent (Muse Spark, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) explored the decode step as a swarm, then wrote fused Metal kernels for three slots of the mixture-of-experts block. Its summary, [muse-spark/summary.md](../../muse-spark/summary.md), names one final attempt per slot. Each one passed the grader, and the summary predicted, from the per-slot timing, that together they would shorten the decode step by 0.54, 1.81 and 5.72 ms at 1, 8 and 32 requests.
6|
7|This is Claude's independent measurement of those three attempts, done on main after merging round 1 (`a4995e4`), on 2026-11-04:
8|- **re-grading** them with the grader;
9|- **checking them end to end** in the model, in plain MLX and in vLLM;
10|- **timing the decode step (G3)** with each slot alone and with all three together.
11|
12|It is the measurement that round 2's skill reads first: the last section names what round 2 starts from in each slot.
13|
14|**Where everything is.** The raw data is in [results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/). The scripts are:
15|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py`, the grader;
16|- `bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, the end-to-end check and G3;
17|- `bench/micro/chain_timing.py`, the chained-timing experiment.
18|
19|**The machine.** The M1 Pro measured the baseline ([method](../benchmark/method.md)). Docker was quit for these runs, with surucuonur's permission. Another job of surucuonur's was running, and 21.3 to 22.7 GB of the 22.5 to 23.5 GB of swap were in use (`machine-*.txt`). vLLM ran with `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0`, as in earlier runs.
20|
21|## Summary
22|
23|- **All three attempts pass the grader as round 1 ran it.** On main, each one compiles, matches the reference within G2's tolerances at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and beats the compiled reference in the per-slot timing.
24|- **In the model, all three together make the decode step slower with 1 and 8 requests.** In vLLM:
25|  - +0.98 ms (+18%) with 1 request;
26|  - +0.16 ms (+1%) with 8;
27|  - −1.76 ms (−6%) with 32.
28|
29|  Round 1 predicted −0.54, −1.81 and −5.72 ms.
30|- **The experts kernel alone slows the step by 1.2 ms (22%) with 1 request,** although the grader timed it 36% faster than the reference.
31|  - The grader ran the 20 layers' calls with nothing between them, so the GPU overlapped them.
32|  - In the model each layer waits for the one before. Chained like that, the kernel takes 133 µs per layer against the reference's 80.
33|- **Each attempt changes the model's tokens,** breaking the brief's end-to-end rule. With 32 requests in vLLM, each one alone changes 7 to 12 of the 32 sequences from the first generated token.
34|  - **experts:** the prefill runs the same slot at 127 to 2,048 rows. There, MLX's own experts kernel changes, and the attempt differs from the reference in 62% of its outputs. The grader tested decode sizes only.
35|  - **routing and combine:** their small rounding differences, within G2's tolerances, are enough to flip greedy tokens.
36|- **The grader changes for round 2** ([ADR 0010](../adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)). G2 is now bit-exact and also covers the prefill's sizes, and the timing chains the layers. None of round 1's attempts passes the new G2.
37|- **Round 2 has no baseline in any slot.** Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's three final attempts are its starting points.
38|- **Round 1 ran the grader 29 times on the experts slot** for the 4 attempts its summary counts, 18 of those on attempt-1.
39|
40|## 1. The grader, as round 1 ran it
41|
42|Re-run on main with the grader of `a4995e4` (`grade-<slot>.json`). µs per layer: reference / compiled reference / attempt.
43|
44|| Slot, attempt | 1 row | 8 rows | 32 rows | G1, G2 |
45||---|---|---|---|---|
46|| experts, attempt-4 | 143.8 / 139.5 / **92.1** | 222.5 / 221.4 / **165.4** | 770.1 / 762.4 / **529.9** | pass, pass (0 units in the last place) |
47|| routing, attempt-1 | 39.9 / 31.5 / **25.3** | 83.5 / 42.7 / **24.3** | 101.2 / 87.6 / **68.9** | pass, pass (weights within 2.6×10⁻⁶) |
48|| combine, attempt-1 | 23.1 / 23.8 / **18.6** | 22.5 / 26.1 / **17.0** | 39.5 / 32.0 / **18.9** | pass, pass (up to 2 units) |
49|
50|Round 1's own runs gave the attempts 50.0 / 157.8 / 515.4 µs (experts), 28.5 / 23.6 / 41.8 (routing) and 17.2 / 17.0 / 18.5 (combine). The experts kernel at 1 row is the outlier, at 92 µs here against 50 then. Round 1's summary already warned that 1-row timings shift between runs.
51|
52|## 2. End to end: the tokens
53|
54|`time_candidates.py` installs each attempt in every layer's `MoE.__call__`, and generates 24 greedy tokens after 128-token prompts. It does this for each slot alone, for all three together, and for each slot's compiled reference. The brief's G2 asks for the same tokens as the unchanged model. Sequences that differ, and the first generated token where one does (`muse-plain.jsonl`, `muse-vllm.jsonl`, records of kind `check`):
55|
56|| Variant | Plain MLX, 1 request | Plain MLX, 32 | vLLM, 1 | vLLM, 32 |
57||---|---|---|---|---|
58|| experts attempt-4 | 1, from token 2 | 19, from token 0 | 0 | 12, from token 0 |
59|| routing attempt-1 | 1, from token 2 | 7, from token 1 | 0 | 9, from token 0 |
60|| combine attempt-1 | 1, from token 2 | 5, from token 2 | 0 | 7, from token 0 |
61|| all three | 0 | 19, from token 0 | 0 | 13, from token 0 |
62|| every compiled reference | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
63|
64|The compiled references give the same tokens in every case, so the unchanged model is deterministic, and every difference comes from the attempts.
65|
66|**Why the tokens change.** Greedy decoding picks the most likely next token. On these random-token prompts, the top two candidates are often very close, so any change to the numbers can flip the choice, and every later token follows from it. That gives two causes:
67|
68|- **The prefill (measured).** The model's prefill runs `MoE.__call__` on the prompt in chunks. With 128-token prompts and 2,048-token chunks, that is 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows at 1, 8 and 32 requests.
69|  - **From the code:** from 60 rows on, MLX switches its experts kernel from `gather_qvm` to `gather_qmm_rhs`, which rounds differently. Round 1's own analysis found this threshold (`muse-spark/exploration/territory-switch-layers.md`, section G).
70|  - **The attempt:** experts attempt-4 copies `gather_qvm`'s arithmetic exactly, which is why it is bit-exact at decode sizes. With the prefill's inputs, it differs from the reference in 62% of its outputs, by up to 110 units in the last place (`grade-exact-experts.json`).
71|  - **The grader:** it never tested more than 32 rows.
72|- **Small rounding differences (measured).** routing attempt-1 picks the same experts in the same order, but every row's weights differ from the reference's, by up to 2.6×10⁻⁶ at decode sizes and 8.7×10⁻⁶ in the prefill. combine attempt-1 differs in 2 to 130 elements per size. Both are inside G2's old tolerances, and both still change 5 to 9 of 32 sequences.
73|
74|## 3. G3: the decode step
75|
76|The decode step's period: the median over 3 repeats, in shuffled order, at 1, 8 and 32 requests, with 128-token prompts and 256 generated tokens. The change is against the unchanged model, and the range is over the 3 repeats (`console-plain.txt`, `console-vllm.txt`).
77|
78|**vLLM, ms per step:**
79|
80|| Variant | 1 request | 8 | 32 |
81||---|---|---|---|
82|| unchanged | 5.370 (5.320–5.452) | 14.363 (14.327–14.475) | 29.851 (29.657–29.952) |
83|| experts attempt-4 | **+1.162** (+21.6%) | −0.817 (−5.7%) | −4.154 (−13.9%) |
84|| experts, compiled reference | +0.066 | +0.024 | −0.103 |
85|| routing attempt-1 | **+0.185** (+3.4%) | −0.397 (−2.8%) | −0.490 (−1.6%) |
86|| routing, compiled reference | −0.220 | −0.183 | −0.157 |
87|| combine attempt-1 | −0.514 (−9.6%) | −0.705 (−4.9%) | −0.390 (−1.3%) |
88|| combine, compiled reference | −0.288 | −0.260 | −0.272 |
89|| all three attempts | **+0.980** (+18.3%) | **+0.163** (+1.1%) | −1.756 (−5.9%) |
90|| all three compiled references | −0.498 (−9.3%) | −0.558 (−3.9%) | −0.242 (−0.8%) |
91|| round 1's prediction, all three | −0.54 | −1.81 | −5.72 |
92|
93|**Plain MLX**, change in ms against an unchanged step of 4.998, 13.541 and 28.496 ms:
94|- experts: +1.228, −0.832, −3.661;
95|- routing: +0.233, −0.361, −0.318;
96|- combine: −0.857, −0.753, −0.406;
97|- all three: +0.927, +0.881, −1.560;
98|- all three compiled references: −0.617, −0.524, −0.255.
99|
100|What it shows:
101|
102|- **Against the brief's G3,** an attempt must beat both the unchanged model and the compiled reference, by more than the spread between repeats. In vLLM:
103|  - **experts attempt-4** does so with 8 and 32 requests, and is slower than both with 1.
104|  - **routing attempt-1** does so with 32 requests. With 8, its range ends 0.05 ms below the compiled reference's; with 1, it is slower than both.
105|  - **combine attempt-1** does so with 8 requests. With 1, its range overlaps the compiled reference's; with 32, it is 0.12 ms ahead of it, within the spread.
106|- **All three together are slower than the parts suggest.**
107|  - With 8 requests in vLLM, the three alone save 0.82, 0.40 and 0.71 ms, but together they cost 0.16 ms.
108|  - With 32 requests, the experts kernel alone saves 4.15 ms, and all three together save 1.76 ms.
109|  - **Measured but not explained:** together the three launch 567 kernels per step with 1 request, against 967 unchanged, so a shorter list of kernels runs slower. The cause is an open question for round 2.
110|- **The compiled references alone save 0.5 to 0.6 ms** with 1 and 8 requests in both engines, without any new kernel.
111|
112|## 4. Why the grader's timing missed the 1-request slowdown
113|
114|**Measured.** `bench/micro/chain_timing.py` times the experts slot on the 20 layers' captured inputs in two ways (`console-chain.txt`, µs per layer):
115|
116|| | 1 row | 8 rows | 32 rows |
117||---|---|---|---|
118|| independent calls, as the grader ran them: reference / attempt-4 | 86.0 / **61.0** | 219.1 / 165.1 | 767.3 / 535.0 |
119|| chained calls, each waiting for the one before: reference / attempt-4 | 80.3 / **132.9** | 239.6 / 175.9 | 797.6 / 587.6 |
120|
121|- **Chained, at 1 row,** attempt-4 is 66% slower than the reference: 52.6 µs × 20 layers is 1.05 ms per step, close to G3's +1.16 ms.
122|- **Independent,** the GPU runs the 20 calls side by side, and the attempt looks 29% faster.
123|- **Estimate, from the code:** attempt-4 gives each (row, expert) pair one threadgroup of 256 threads. With 1 row that is 4 threadgroups, too few to fill the GPU, so one call's time is long even when many calls together go fast. Round 1 called this "occupancy starvation", and attempt-4 doubled the threads per pair to fight it (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/block-0.metal`, opening comment).
124|
125|## 5. How round 1 counted its attempts
126|
127|Round 1's summary counts "experts 4, routing 2, combine 2" graded attempts. In its transcripts (`muse-spark/transcripts/`), the shell commands that ran the grader number:
128|- **experts: 29.** 18 on `attempt-1`, 3 on `attempt-2`, 6 on `attempt-3`, 1 on `attempt-4` and 1 on `probe-f64`;
129|- **routing: 2;**
130|- **combine: 3.** 1 on `attempt-1` and 2 on `attempt-2`.
131|
132|`builder-1-a` edited attempt-1's files before nearly every one of its 18 runs, so that folder's kernel is the last of many versions rather than one try. Skill version 4 made "one grader run is one attempt" a rule, and version 5 keeps it.
133|
134|## 6. What changes for round 2
135|
136|surucuonur chose these rules on 2026-11-04 ([ADR 0010](../adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)). The [brief](../muse-agent-brief.md) and the grader now apply them:
137|
138|- **Every call.** A slot's kernels run wherever `MoE.__call__` runs, the prefill included.
139|- **Bit-exact.** G2 asks for outputs identical to the reference's at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step, and at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows of a prefill. For routing that means the same experts and weights, in the same order.
140|- **Chained timing.** Each layer's call waits for the one before, through one small link kernel that every function timed gets alike.
141|
142|Round 1's final attempts under the new grader (`grade-exact-<slot>.json`):
143|
144|| Slot, attempt | Decode: 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Prefill: 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows |
145||---|---|---|
146|| experts, attempt-4 | exact / exact / exact | 4,868,667 / 39,078,912 / 78,741,557 elements differ (up to 43, 65 and 110.5 units) |
147|| routing, attempt-1 | 20 / 159 / 638 rows differ, of 20 / 160 / 640 | 2,518 / 16,187 / 32,743 rows differ |
148|| combine, attempt-1 | exact / 2 / 2 elements differ | 6 / 50 / 130 elements differ (up to 1, 16 and 32 units) |
149|
150|Each count is summed over the 20 layers. None of the three passes.
151|
152|## For round 2: baselines and starting points
153|
154|**No slot has a baseline.** No earlier attempt passes the current G2. A new attempt must pass G1 and the new G2 and beat the compiled reference at 1, 8 and 32 rows, in the chained timing; there is no `--baseline` to pass. Each slot's starting point, the attempt to build from:
155|
156|| Slot | Starting point | What keeps it from passing G2 | Its G3 alone, vLLM, 1 / 8 / 32 requests (ms) |
157||---|---|---|---|
158|| `experts` | `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4` | Exact at decode sizes only. From 60 rows on it doesn't match `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding. | +1.16 / −0.82 / −4.15 |
159|| `routing` | `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1` | Every row's weights differ from the reference's in the last bits; the experts and their order match. | +0.19 / −0.40 / −0.49 |
160|| `combine` | `muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` | 2 to 130 elements differ per size, from 8 rows on. | −0.51 / −0.71 / −0.39 |
161|
162|**What round 2 has to find out,** in Claude's reading of these results:
163|1. **The experts kernel at prefill sizes.** It must match MLX's `gather_qmm_rhs` from 60 rows on, bit for bit, or follow a design whose rounding equals both of MLX's kernels.
164|2. **The experts kernel at 1 row,** where it is slower than the reference when chained: 133 against 80 µs per layer.
165|3. **routing's and combine's exact arithmetic.** Each needs the reference's order of operations and rounding points, for example the float32 sum order of the router's product, and of combine's sum over the 4 pairs.
166|4. **Why the three together lose time** that each saves alone (section 3).
167|
168|**Recommendations outside the slots** from round 1 stand as written in its [summary](../../muse-spark/summary.md). This measurement didn't test them.

5|# From round 2, a kernel must be bit-exact at every size it runs at, prefill included, and the piece timing chains the layers
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's measurement of round 1 ([findings](../findings/muse-round-1.md)) found that round 1's final attempts, which passed the grader, broke the brief's end-to-end rule in the model, and that one of them slowed the decode step it was meant to speed up. The grader missed three things:
10|
11|1. **Sizes.** It tested a slot on a decode step's inputs only, at 1, 8 and 32 rows. The same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill, at 127 to 2,048 rows with 128-token prompts. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes, from `gather_qvm` to `gather_qmm_rhs`, and so does its rounding. Round 1's experts kernel copied `gather_qvm` bit for bit, and differed in 62% of its outputs at each prefill size.
12|2. **Exactness.** G2 allowed small differences: 2 bfloat16 units in the last place, and 10⁻⁴ for routing weights. End to end, the brief asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. Round 1's routing weights, within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences in 24 tokens.
13|3. **Latency.** The piece timing ran 20 layers' calls with no data between them, so the GPU could overlap them. At 1 row, round 1's experts kernel was 29% faster than the reference on overlapped calls and 66% slower on chained ones (`bench/micro/chain_timing.py`). In the model it slowed the decode step by 1.2 ms (22% in vLLM, 25% in plain MLX).
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose, before round 2:
16|- **every call:** the kernels run wherever `MoE.__call__` runs, the prefill included;
17|- **bit-exact** outputs;
18|- **chained** piece timing.
19|
20|## How it works
21|
22|- **G2 at two kinds of size.** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` checks every layer at:
23|  - the captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
24|  - the first prefill chunk at 1, 8 and 32 requests (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows), recorded while it runs (`slots.capture_prefill`), with the prompts `time_candidates.py` uses.
25|- **Bit-exact.** An output passes only if it equals the reference's:
26|  - for routing, the 4 experts and their weights, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order;
27|  - for combine and experts, every element.
28|
29|  The grader still reports the largest gap, in units in the last place, to help find the cause. The reference checked against itself shows no difference at any size.
30|- **Chained timing.** Each layer's call takes one input through `link`, a single fused kernel that adds 0 × one value of the previous call's output, so the call can't start before the previous one finishes. Every function timed (reference, compiled, candidate and baseline) gets the same link. The chained times match those of a real data chain within 10%.
31|  - **Why not `mx.depends`:** it orders only the graph. In a test on 2026-11-04, round 1's experts kernel took 46 µs per layer with it at 1 row, as fast as with no dependency, against 133 to 195 µs with a real data dependency in three runs.
32|- **The end-to-end check and G3 are unchanged.**
33|  - `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` now takes several `SLOT=FOLDER` attempts.
34|  - It times each slot alone, against its own compiled reference, and all of them together.
35|
36|## Consequences
37|
38|- **No round-1 attempt passes the new G2,** so round 2 has no baseline in any slot. Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's final attempts are its starting points, named in Claude's findings.
39|- **The experts slot needs a kernel exact at prefill sizes,** matching `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding from 60 rows on, or a single design whose rounding matches both of MLX's kernels.
40|- **A grader run takes longer.** It loads the model (760 MB) for every slot and runs three prefill chunks.
41|- **The piece timing now includes one small link kernel per layer** for every function timed. That brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs.
42|- **Not covered:** prefill speed. G3 times decode steps only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token.
43|
44|## Considered options
45|
46|- **Decode calls only,** with MLX's code in the prefill. The kernels would need to be exact only at decode sizes, but they would no longer replace the whole MoE block. Not chosen: surucuonur asked for every call.
47|- **Keep the tolerances, and relax the token rule** to counting the sequences that differ. Simpler kernels, but the claim would become "the same model up to rounding", with a threshold to pick.
48|- **Keep independent timing,** and rely on G3 to catch latency. Round 2's builders would again rank attempts by a number that hid a 22% slowdown.
49|- **`mx.depends` for the chain.** No extra kernel, but it doesn't make the GPU wait.

1|# Hypothesis 2: fused routing kernel
2|
3|- **Owner:** lead
4|- **Status:** ready
5|- **Version:** 4
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-03T21:52:00Z
7|- **Next:** none — attempt-1 goes to G3
8|
9|## Inefficiency
10|
11|Slot `routing`. One entry:
12|
13|- `ineff-runs-2` (rank 2, mean 11.0% of step): routing costs 1.02 ms at 1 row and 1.68 ms at 32 rows while reading ~4 MB — 12 tiny kernels/layer of pure overhead (argpartition runs a full 60-element sort per row; the weights-norm sum runs on 1 thread at 1 row). Fusion to ~1 kernel/layer saves 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 ms at 1/8/32 rows.
14|
15|Design: one Metal kernel per layer that computes router scores (matmul + sigmoid + bias), selects the top-4 experts, and normalizes/scales the weights, with the 4 experts in any order per row. G2 gives freedom only on within-1e-6 tie rows and 1e-4 relative weights by expert.
16|
17|## Boundary
18|
19|*written by boundary-2, 2026-11-03T21:45Z*
20|
21|### Inputs and outputs
22|
23|Source: the brief's routing table (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:28-36`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-48`. All arrays row-contiguous (brief:24).
24|
25|| | Name | Shape at 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Dtype | Layout |
26||---|---|---|---|---|
27|| input | `x` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | flat rows of the MoE input, row-contiguous |
28|| input | `w_router` | [60,768] at all row counts | float32 | router weight, used transposed (`x @ w_router.T`) |
29|| input | `bias` | [60] at all row counts | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) | one value per expert |
30|| output | `inds` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | uint32 | 4 expert indices per row, each < 60 |
31|| output | `weights` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | float32 | `weights[r,j]` belongs to `inds[r,j]` |
32|
33|### Before and after in `MoE.__call__`
34|
35|Source: `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232` and the split harness `bench/grader/slots.py:105-119`.
36|
37|- **Before:** the slot input `x` is the MoE block's input, i.e. `post_attention_layernorm(h)` reshaped to flat `[rows,768]` (`mobilemoe.py:258-260`, `slots.py:106-107`). `w_router` (`self.router.weight`) and `bias` (`self.expert_bias.astype(float32)`, `slots.py:108`) are parameters. The producer expects nothing back; the slot must read `x` as bfloat16 — the reference casts to float32 itself (`mobilemoe.py:219`).
38|- **After (1), the experts call:** `SwitchGLU(x, inds)` gathers expert weights per (row, j) by index (`switch_layers.py:176-199`). From `inds.size >= 64` (rows ≥ 16) it sorts pairs by expert internally and unscatters the result back, so its output `y[..., j, :]` always corresponds to `inds[..., j]` whatever per-row order the slot emits (brief:53: `y` is "in `inds` order"). It expects 4 valid indices per row, each < 60; order is free.
39|- **After (2), combine:** `(y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bfloat16) + shared` (`mobilemoe.py:231`, `slots.py:51-52`). It expects `weights[r,j]` to be the normalized weight of `inds[r,j]` (brief:47). The shared expert runs independently of the slot.
40|
41|Checklist (per `tracking.md`) for each neighbour:
42|
43|- **Producer (layernorm output / MoE entry).** Callers: `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258-260`). Callees: none into the slot — it only supplies `x`. Data: `x` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: attention block before (untouched). Cost: outside the slot. Invariants: `x` values are whatever the model produces; no assumption about their range beyond bf16.
44|- **Consumer `SwitchGLU(x, inds)`.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:230`). Callees: `gather_qmm` per product, with internal sort/unsort from rows ≥ 16 (`switch_layers.py:176-199`). Data: `inds` [rows,4] uint32. Neighbours: combine after it. Cost: the experts slot (hyp-1), untouched by this hypothesis. Invariants: one output row per (row, j) pair, in `inds` order; any per-row permutation of `inds` is safe as long as `weights` permutes with it.
45|- **Consumer combine.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:231`). Callees: none (reference arithmetic). Data: `weights` [rows,4] f32, `y` [rows,4,768] bf16, `shared` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: residual add `h + ...` in `DecoderLayer` after. Cost: 5 kernels/layer, untouched. Invariants: the bf16 cast happens here, outside the slot — the slot outputs pure float32.
46|
47|### What must stay identical
48|

# Attempt 2: two-kernel split (direction b)

First attempt in direction (b): kernel 1 fuses router scores (dense matmul +
sigmoid + bias add), kernel 2 fuses top-4 selection plus weight
normalize/scale. The dense matmul keeps a regular GEMM shape (one thread per
(row, expert), k tiled through threadgroup memory); the 11 bookkeeping kernels
around it collapse into the two fused kernels.

Removes `ineff-runs-2`: 12 kernels/layer of pure launch overhead become 2.
Kernel 1 additionally avoids re-reading the 184 KB router weight once per row
by staging k-chunks in threadgroup memory shared across 8 rows (17.4 KB <
32 KB limit; 480 threads/group < 1024).

## Predicted µs per layer (piece timing)

Fixed cost: 2 kernels x 6.81 µs (step_parts.txt:2) = 13.6 µs. Traffic at
200 GB/s peak:

- 1 row: w 184 KB (1 group) + x 1.5 KB + intermediates ~1 KB = ~187 KB ~= 0.9 µs.
  Total ~= 14.5 -> **15 µs/layer** (original 51).
- 8 rows: w 184 KB (1 group) + x 12 KB + intermediates ~8 KB = ~204 KB ~= 1.0 µs.
  Total ~= 14.6 -> **15 µs/layer** (original ~59, interpolated).
- 32 rows: w 737 KB (4 groups) + x 49 KB + intermediates ~32 KB = ~818 KB ~= 4.1 µs.
  Total ~= 17.7 -> **18 µs/layer** (original 84).

Predicted saving per step (x20 layers): 0.72 / 0.88 / 1.32 ms at 1/8/32 rows.

## Verdict

G1 pass. G2 pass: 0 wrong-expert rows, 0 near-tie rows at all row counts,
worst max_rel_err 2.6e-6 (40x inside the 1e-4 tolerance).

| rows | candidate | reference | compiled | beats compiled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 36.3 | 36.3 | 29.3 | no |
| 8 | 34.9 | 56.9 | 42.9 | yes |
| 32 | 49.0 | 51.7 | 46.6 | no |

`beats_compiled: false`. Attempt-1 (direction a, single kernel) measured
28.5 / 23.6 / 41.8 against compiled 30.5 / 42.0 / 49.1 on its run and stops
the slot; this attempt is slower than it at every row count.

## Why the prediction missed (predicted 15 / 15 / 18, off by 142 / 133 / 172%)

1. Wrong fixed-cost model. I charged 2 x 6.81 µs = 13.6 µs from
   step_parts.txt. The piece harness shows a ~24-28 µs floor even for one
   fused kernel (attempt-1: 28.5 at 1 row), while the reference's 12 kernels
   cost only ~3 µs each when pipelined 20 layers deep. A heavy fused kernel
   costs a dispatch floor plus low-occupancy ramp, not one microbench launch.
2. Two launches, each under-occupied. Kernel 1 runs 60 threads (2 simdgroups,
   1 of 16 cores) at 1 row with 24 threadgroup barriers; kernel 2 runs a
   single thread at 1 row -- a whole launch for ~100 ns of ALU.
3. Sub-peak bandwidth. Kernel 1's w reads are 3 KB apart across SIMD lanes,
   far from the assumed 200 GB/s, and the two [rows,60] intermediates add a
   write-plus-reread round trip the single-kernel design avoids.
4. Attempt-1 is the control: re-reading w once per row (no tiling) still wins
   at 32 rows, so my barrier-heavy tiling bought traffic savings that never
   mattered and paid overhead that did.

One change I would make next (staying in direction b): delete the
threadgroup tiling in kernel 1 -- stream each expert's w column from device
memory with zero barriers -- since traffic is not the binding constraint.
Honestly, direction (a) dominates this split: one launch and no intermediates
beats two launches at all three row counts.

67|### 2. `slots.py` — capture/save/load of grader inputs (slots.py:137-224)
68|
69|- **Callers:** `slots.py capture` → `main` → `check_identity` + `save_inputs`
70|  (slots.py:296-312); every grading run calls `load_inputs(rows)` per row count
71|  and, for experts, `load_expert_weights()` once (check_candidate.py:177,180,212).
72|- **Callees:** `capture` runs `breakdown.prefill`/`greedy` on checkpoint
73|  `MODEL = "models/MobileMoE-S-QAT-mlx-bfloat16"` (breakdown.py:62) with
74|  `make_prompt_cache`, recording MoE inputs on decode step 8
75|  (slots.py:137-171); `save_inputs`/`load_inputs` use `np.savez`/`np.load`
76|  (slots.py:174-223); `load_expert_weights` reads the served checkpoint via
77|  `mlx_lm.utils.load_model` (slots.py:189-202).
78|- **Data:** `INPUTS = models/muse-inputs/rows{1,8,32}.npz` (slots.py:41):
79|  140 keys each = 20 layers × {x, w_router, bias, inds, y, weights_in, shared}
80|  (verified by listing; e.g. rows32 `L00_x` (32,768), `L00_y` (32,4,768),
81|  `L00_w_router` (60,768), `L19_*` same). Files are 4.1/6.7/15.5 MB for
82|  rows 1/8/32 (`ls -la models/muse-inputs/`). bfloat16 arrays (x, y, shared)
83|  are stored as float32 and cast back on load (slots.py:178-185,210-216);
84|  `weights_in` is renamed to `weights`, `inds` cast to u32, expert weights
85|  merged per layer (slots.py:217-223). Inputs are seeded (`mx.random.seed(rows)`,
86|  slots.py:158): identical every run.
87|- **Neighbours:** capture runs plain MLX, no API (slots.py:8); it prefills
88|  128-token random prompts then records the 8th decode step (slots.py:158-168).
89|  Consumed by every G1/G2/timing run; G2 tests all 20 layers' inputs at each row
90|  count (check_candidate.py:179-205).
91|- **Cost:** capture is one-time; per grading run the loads are host-side plus one
92|  `mx.eval` of weights. Not decode-step time.
93|- **Invariants:** fixed seeded inputs make G2 deterministic; per-layer dicts keep
94|  layers independent (a candidate sees one layer's inputs per call).

96|### 3. `slots.py` — launch-spec build (slots.py:226-293)
97|
98|- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` (check_candidate.py:34-41) and
99|  `Variants` in time_candidates.py:60-77, via `slots.build(spec, sources, slot)`.
100|- **Callees:** one `mx.fast.metal_kernel` per spec kernel (slots.py:257-264);
101|  the returned `run(**inputs)` chains them (slots.py:270-291). The grader runs
102|  no Python of the candidate's: the spec is data, only the Metal compiles
103|  (brief:97).
104|- **Data:** `spec.json` schema (brief:143-176): `kernels` in run order, each with
105|  name, source/header block numbers, inputs (slot inputs or earlier kernels'
106|  outputs), outputs (name/shape/dtype), grid, threadgroup, template, init_value,
107|  atomic_outputs; `slot_outputs` maps slot outputs to kernel outputs.
108|  `routing+combine` nests two such specs under `{"routing":…, "combine":…}`
109|  (brief:171). Sizes are ints or products of ints and rows/D/E/K/H only
110|  (`dim`, slots.py:230-240); dtypes are float32/bfloat16/float16/uint32/int32
111|  (slots.py:22-28); template values are dtype/int/bool (slots.py:243-248).
112|- **Neighbours:** Metal bodies live in `block-N.metal` numbered from 0
113|  (check_candidate.py:36-39); kernels run in list order with outputs chained
114|  through `env` (slots.py:273-290). For `routing+combine` the original experts
115|  and shared expert run between the two parts (brief:171).
116|- **Cost:** each spec kernel is ≥1 GPU launch; candidate kernel count is the
117|  builder's main overhead lever (see the covered inefficiency entries).
118|- **Invariants:** threadgroup product must be in 1..1024 (slots.py:274-276);
119|  missing `slot_outputs` → ValueError (slots.py:266-268); bad size terms → ValueError.

121|### 4. `check_candidate.py` — G1, G2, piece timing (whole file)
122|
123|- **Callers:** builders run `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py
124|  <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]` (brief:123-129); `time_candidates.py` imports
125|  `load` (time_candidates.py:29). Holds the GPU lock for the whole run
126|  (check_candidate.py:173).
127|- **Callees:** `slots.build`/`load_inputs`/`load_expert_weights`; `mx.eval` for
128|  correctness and timing; `mx.compile(ref)` for the compiled baseline only
129|  (check_candidate.py:217-222).
130|- **Data:** `ROWS = (1,8,32)`, `REPEATS = 30` (check_candidate.py:26-27).
131|  Prints and optionally writes the JSON verdict
132|  `{slot, g1, g2, beats_compiled, correctness, timing_us_per_layer, error}`
133|  (check_candidate.py:174,229-232).
134|- **Neighbours — G1:** pass = compiled and ran without exception at all row
135|  counts (`g1 = True` after the loops, check_candidate.py:206; any exception →
136|  `error` + g1 false, check_candidate.py:227-228, Metal errors trimmed by
137|  `short_error`, check_candidate.py:153-163). Note: shape/dtype mismatches are
138|  per-layer `{"error":…}` stats, not exceptions — they fail G2 with g1 true
139|  (check_candidate.py:188-191).
140|- **Neighbours — G2 routing** (`check_routing`, check_candidate.py:50-94):
141|  exact shapes (rows,4)/(rows,4) and dtypes u32/f32 (55-62); inds < 60 (65);
142|  expert *set* per row must match (71) unless the reference's 4th/5th biased
143|  scores are within 1e-6 — such rows count as `near_tie_rows` and skip the
144|  weight check (72-80); otherwise weights matched by expert, relative error
145|  ≤ 1e-4 (81-87,137). Order within the row is free.
146|- **Neighbours — G2 combine/experts** (`check_combine`/`check_experts`,
147|  check_candidate.py:96-139): exact shape and bf16 dtype; every element within
148|  2 bf16 ULP of the reference, with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 (`ulp_bf16`,
149|  check_candidate.py:44-47). Aggregation over 20 layers: max of `max_*`, sum of
150|  counts, `pass` iff every layer passes, worst example kept
151|  (check_candidate.py:192-204).
152|- **Neighbours — routing+combine independence:** each part is checked and timed
153|  on its own; the combine part receives the *reference* (captured) routing
154|  weights, not the candidate's (check_candidate.py:96-98,181-187; brief:171).
155|  A routing miss can never fail the combine part, and vice versa.
156|- **Neighbours — piece timing** (`timed`, check_candidate.py:141-150,209-226):
157|  runs only if G2 passes. Per row count and part: 3 warmup evals, then median
158|  of 30 repeats of `mx.eval` over all 20 layers' calls with one GPU wait,
159|  divided by 20 → µs/layer. `timing_us_per_layer[rows]` = reference +
160|  `mx.compile(reference)` + candidate summed over parts; `beats_compiled`
161|  requires candidate < compiled at *all three* row counts. "It is a guide; G3
162|  decides" (brief:193).
163|- **Cost:** grading runtime ≈ correctness (20 layers × 3 rows × parts) + timing
164|  (33 evals × 3 variants × 3 rows × parts, each a 20-layer eval); a run should
165|  take under 3 minutes (brief:98). Not decode-step time.
166|- **Invariants:** verdict JSON shape; `--out` writes it too (229-231).

168|### 5. `time_candidates.py` — G2 end-to-end and G3 (whole file)
169|
170|- **Callers:** surucuonur's team runs it after merging (`plain` and `vllm`
171|  engines, time_candidates.py:14-15); the final attempt per slot "goes to the
172|  end-to-end and G3 checks" (brief:195). Holds the GPU lock (time_candidates.py:113).
173|- **Callees:** `check_candidate.load`; `slots.make_moe_call`/`REFERENCE`;
174|  `breakdown` (`MODEL`, `prefill`, `greedy`, `run_plain`, `run_vllm`,
175|  `install_vllm_step_hooks`; breakdown.py:62,408-485); `repeat_fixes`
176|  (`count_ops`, `divergence`, `vllm_checks`, `time_variants`;
177|  repeat_fixes.py:136-277) with `SETTINGS = [(1,128),(8,128),(32,128)]`,
178|  `REPEATS = 3` (repeat_fixes.py:43-44).
179|- **Data:** variants base (port's MoE) / compiled (`mx.compile` of the slot
180|  reference) / muse (candidate) [/ claude_fixed] (time_candidates.py:60-77).
181|  `TOKENS = 24` greedy tokens at rows 1 and 32 in plain MLX
182|  (time_candidates.py:34,79-101); vLLM uses ≤32 seqs, 512 MiB KV cache
183|  (time_candidates.py:132-141).
184|- **Neighbours:** `as_routing`/`as_combine`/`as_experts` adapt candidate fns to
185|  the MoE signature and install them into *every* layer's `MoE.__call__`
186|  (time_candidates.py:37-77). G2-e2e requires *exact* greedy-token equality
187|  with base (`exact` flag + first-divergence step, time_candidates.py:97-99;
188|  brief:185). G3 is the steady decode-step period, median of 3 shuffled
189|  repeats at 1/8/32 with 128-token prompts; it must beat *both* base and
190|  compiled with the gap exceeding the repeat spread (brief:186).
191|- **Cost:** G3 is the deciding measurement; the piece timing (item 4) only guides.
192|  `count_ops` also records one step's kernel count per variant
193|  (time_candidates.py:96; repeat_fixes.py:136).
194|- **Invariants:** exact tokens; shuffled repeats; vLLM and plain MLX both.
195|
196|### 6. `gpu_lock.py` — the GPU mutex (whole file)
197|
198|- **Callers:** `check_candidate.main`, `slots.main` (capture), `time_candidates.main`.
199|- **Callees:** `fcntl.flock` on `/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock`, shared between the
200|  main checkout and the worktree, OS-released on process end (gpu_lock.py:14-31).
201|- **Data:** lockfile content `pid <pid>: <job>`.
202|- **Neighbours:** the grader is a builder's only GPU job; contended runs print
203|  the holder and queue (gpu_lock.py:20-27; tracking.md rules). No model loads,
204|  no other GPU work (16 GB machine).
205|- **Cost:** queue wait when contended. Not decode-step time.
206|- **Invariants:** `_held` keeps the fd open for the process's life (gpu_lock.py:15,31).
207|
208|## Relations
209|
210|- **Fed by:** model territory (`MoE.__call__` mobilemoe.py:217-232, the router/
211|  `SwitchGLU`/shared-expert code the references mirror); switch-layers
212|  territory (`_gather_sort`/`_scatter_unsort`, switch_layers.py:12-24, called by
213|  `ref_experts`); findings/runs territories (the measured tables behind the
214|  reference costs); `bench/micro/breakdown.py` + `repeat_fixes.py` (MODEL,
215|  prefill/greedy, G3 harness); `models/muse-inputs/` (seeded captured inputs).
216|- **Feeds:** builders (spec format, G1/G2/timing verdicts); the boundary agent
217|  (slot I/O, dtypes, tolerances, rounding points — items 1+4 above); hypotheses
218|  (the compiled baseline is the bar to beat at all three row counts).
219|- **Boundary floor — traffic the slots mandate** (unremovable within the
220|  interface, so it caps every saving): per layer, experts must write
221|  y [rows,4,768] bf16 (rows×6144 B) and combine must re-read it; routing must
222|  write inds+weights [rows,4] (rows×32 B) for experts/combine to read. Per step
223|  @32 rows: y 196 KB × 2 (write+read) × 20 layers = 7.9 MB → 0.04 ms at
224|  200 GB/s; inds/weights ≈ 41 KB → negligible. Saving floor ≈ 0.04 ms @32 rows
225|  (≈ 0.001 ms @1 row): fusing *within* slots captures essentially all of each
226|  slot's cost; cross-slot fusion is not expressible (`routing+combine` still
227|  runs the reference experts + shared expert between the parts, brief:171).
228|- **Piece timing vs G3 (builder warning):** the piece timing medians 30 repeats
229|  of 20-layer evals per part and sums the parts; G3 medians 3 full steps. A
230|  candidate can win the piece timing yet lose G3 (e.g. via cache/overlap effects
231|  the isolated evals don't see). The gap must exceed the repeat spread.
232|

241|- `ineff-model-2` (combine overhead) — note: G2 2-ULP check + routing+combine
242|  part independence (combine graded on reference routing weights).
243|- `ineff-runs-1` (experts re-reads) — note: G2 experts check (2 ULP, 0.001
244|  floor), bf16 rounding points, piece-timing setup.
245|- `ineff-runs-3` (pairs unsorted below 16 rows) — note: exact threshold code
246|  (`do_sort = inds.size >= 64`, slots.py:62) + G2 compares outputs only, so
247|  sorting at 8 rows is G2-safe.
