- **Next:** none — checklist filled, 3 inefficiencies posted, grader note folded

## What it does

The `experts` slot of one MoE layer: for each row `r` and slot `j`, with
`e = inds[r, j]`, compute
`y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]`
(`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:84-88`; reference `bench/grader/slots.py:55-82`).
The starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4` is now the code in
the slot: one fused per-pair Metal kernel
(`block-0.metal` + header `block-1.metal`, launched by `spec.json`) that
replicates MLX `affine_gather_qvm` bitwise. It is bit-exact at decode sizes
and fails the new G2 at every prefill size, and it loses chained at 1 row
while winning chained at 8/32 rows. Round 1 mapped the same code path in
`muse-spark/exploration/territory-switch-layers.md` and
`territory-quantized-kernels.md`; this entry cites them where they still
hold and writes only what is new: the starting point as slot code, the
chained-timing reversal at 1 row, and the prefill kernel switch.

## Checklist

### A. Starting point `block-0.metal` — fused per-pair kernel body

- **Callers:** `spec.json` kernel `fused_experts_perpair` (see §C), built by
  `bench/grader/slots.py:303-345` (`build`) into one `mx.fast.metal_kernel`
  call per layer invocation. In the model it replaces `SwitchGLU.__call__`
  via `slots.make_moe_call` (`slots.py:97-119`): `experts(flat, inds, ...)`
  with `flat` `[rows, 768]` bfloat16 and `inds` `[rows, 4]` uint32.
  Shapes: decode 1/8/32 rows → pairs `rows*4` = 4/32/128; prefill
  127/1,016/2,048 rows → pairs 508/4,064/8,192 (prefill sizes from
  `slots.py:214-254`, `capture_prefill`: 128-token prompts, 2,048-token
  chunks). The grader tests all six sizes for G2
  (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:272-276`) and chains the piece timing
  only at decode 1/8/32 (`check_candidate.py:309-337`).
- **Callees:** `qvm_block` (§B) for gate, up, down; no MLX op. Thread 0 of
  each simdgroup stores each 32-output block; silu-mul is inline
  (`block-0.metal:53-64`).
- **Data:** inputs `x` `[rows, 768]` bfloat16, `inds` `[rows, 4]` uint32,
  `gate_w`/`up_w` `[60, 768, 48]` uint32, `gate_scales`/`gate_biases`/
  `up_scales`/`up_biases` `[60, 768, 12]` bfloat16, `down_w` `[60, 384, 96]`
  uint32, `down_scales`/`down_biases` `[60, 384, 24]` bfloat16
  (`bench/grader/slots.py:33-36`; brief `experts` table:
  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:73-80`). Threadgroup: `tg_x[768]`,
  `tg_gate[384]`, `tg_up[384]`, `tg_h[384]` bfloat = 1,920 values = 3,840 B
  (`block-0.metal:13-16`). Output `y` `[rows, 4, 768]` bfloat16, positional:
  `y[pair * 768 + ...]` with `pair = threadgroup_position_in_grid.x`,
  `r = pair >> 2`, `e = inds[pair]` (`block-0.metal:6-11,68-75`).
- **Neighbours:** before: routing produces `inds` (any order, values in
  `[0, 60)`); after: combine consumes `y` positionally as
  `y[r, j]` paired with `weights[r, j]` (`slots.py:116`,
  `ref_combine` `slots.py:51-52`). The kernel must accept any `inds` order
  and duplicates; it does (`e = inds[pair]`, no sort, no threshold).
  Shared expert runs independently and is outside the slot.
- **Cost:** 1 kernel per layer call (vs reference 7 at 1 row, 13 at 32 rows;
  see §E). Grid `rows*1024` threads, threadgroup 256 → `rows*4`
  threadgroups, one per pair (`spec.json`; `block-0.metal:1-5`). At 1 row:
  4 threadgroups / 1,024 threads. Weight bytes per pair 552,960 B
  (gate/up/down: `60·768·48 = 60·384·96 = 2,211,840` words per projection;
  per expert per projection 36,864 words = 147,456 B, plus scales+biases
  `9,216 × 2 B × 2 = 36,864` B; total `3 × 184,320 = 552,960` B; cf.
  `attempt-4/notes.md:19` "553 KB", `hyp-1-fused-experts.md:39`). Per layer:
  2.21 MB at 1 row (4 pairs), 17.7 MB at 8 rows (32 pairs), 70.8 MB at
  32 rows (128 pairs). Measured chained (median µs/layer,
  `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/console-chain.txt` via
  `bench/micro/chain_timing.py`): candidate 132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6 vs
  reference 80.3 / 239.6 / 797.6 at 1/8/32 rows. Independent (overlapped)
  same run: candidate 61.0 / 165.1 / 535.0 vs reference 86.0 / 219.1 /
  767.3. At 200 GB/s peak (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:10`) the byte floors are
  11.1 / 88.4 / 353.9 µs/layer; the candidate's effective rates are
  16.6 / 100.6 / 120.5 GB/s chained (2.21/17.7/70.8 MB ÷ chained µs).
- **Invariants:** per-block numerics must stay bit-identical to the
  reference kernel that runs at that size (see §F): float32 accumulation,
  bfloat16 rounding after each of gate/up, after `silu(gate)*up`, and after
  down (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). `block-0` keeps all four: gate/up
  stored as `(bfloat)p[j]` (`:34,46`), hidden stored as bfloat (`:63`),
  down stored as `(bfloat)p[j]` (`:73`). Silu is computed entirely in
  bfloat16, rounding after every op (`:56-64`; found by search, see
  `attempt-4/notes.md:22-26` and `hyp-1-fused-experts.md:94-97`). No rows
  threshold in the kernel: valid for any `rows` (indices `r`, `inds[pair]`,
  `y[pair*768+...]` all scale with `rows`).

### B. Starting point `block-1.metal` — `qvm_block`, the `gather_qvm` replica

- **Callers:** `block-0.metal:31,43,70` (gate, up, down). Byte-identical to
  attempt-2 (`attempt-4/notes.md:6-9`; `hyp-1-fused-experts.md:302-306`).
- **Callees:** `simd_sum` reduction (`block-1.metal:37-40`). No other call.
- **Data:** per call one 32-output block: `W` uint32 stream, `S`/`B`
  bfloat16 scales/biases, `xv` threadgroup bfloat row (`K` = 768 gate/up,
  384 down), `G` groups (12 gate/up, 24 down), `Ww` words per row (48/96),
  block index `g`, word base `wb = b*4`, `lane` in `[0, 32)`. Output
  `p[32]` float32 per lane, reduced by `simd_sum` so lane 0 holds the block
  result (`block-1.metal:17-40`). Dequant on the fly in float32:
  `p[2i] += x * (s0 * q + bias)`, `p[2i+1] += x * (s1 * q + bias)` with
  `s0 = scale`, `s1 = scale/16` (`:24-25,33-34`), matching MLX `qouter`
  bits=4 path (round 1: `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §A,
  `quantized.h:452-553`, `:503-509`).
- **Neighbours:** reads `tg_x` (gate/up) or `tg_h` (down) after a barrier
  (`block-0.metal:21,65`); writes only via the caller's lane-0 store.
- **Cost:** per pair: gate/up 12 blocks, down 24 blocks, each block
  `K/32` = 24 (gate/up) or 12 (down) strided lane steps × 32 outputs.
  Included in §A totals; launches no kernel itself.
- **Invariants:** this is the exactness core. Each lane accumulates its
  strided `K` elements serially (`k = lane; k < K; k += 32`, `:20`), then a
  `simd_sum` tree reduces across lanes (`:38-39`) — the same order as MLX
  `qvm_impl` (`quantized.h:1275-1321` in the installed 0.32.4 headers;
  round 1 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §A). Round 1 proved any other
  summation order fails: down outputs near cancellation amplify a 1-ULP
  hidden flip (`hyp-1-fused-experts.md:103-108`,
  `ineff-switch-layers-2.md` builder note). The guard `b < 12` in gate/up
  wave 2 is simd-uniform (`v`, `simd` only), so participating simdgroups
  reduce uniformly and idle ones skip wholly (`hyp-1-fused-experts.md:324-330`).

### C. Starting point `spec.json` — launch spec

- **Callers:** grader `load` (`check_candidate.py:57-64`) → `slots.build`
  (`slots.py:303-345`). One kernel entry.
- **Callees:** `fused_experts_perpair`, `source_block 0`, `header_block 1`,
  inputs all 11 slot inputs, output `y` `[rows, 4, 768]` bfloat16, grid
  `["rows*1024", 1, 1]`, threadgroup `[256, 1, 1]`, no template, no
  atomics (`spec.json` single line). `slot_outputs: {"y": "y"}`.
- **Data:** grid counts threads (`slots.py:334`, brief:175): `rows*1024 ÷
  256 = rows*4` threadgroups at every row count, including prefill
  (8,192 threadgroups / 2,097,152 threads at 2,048 rows). Threadgroup
  limits: 256 ≤ 1,024 threads, 3,840 B ≤ 32 KB (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:98`).
- **Neighbours:** kernels run in list order (`slots.py:325`); with one
  kernel there is no inter-kernel ordering to keep. A prefill branch (see
  ineff-1) must fit this surface: grid expressions are only products of
  integers and `rows`/`D`/`E`/`K`/`H` (`slots.py:279-292`), so a size
  switch can only be a second listed kernel with an in-Metal early return,
  or a branch inside `block-0` on a shape the source uses
  (`x_shape` is available when used; brief:96).
- **Cost:** 1 launch per layer per call. Fixed cost per launch ~6.81 µs
  end-to-end (round 1: `muse-spark/exploration/README.md:22`, Claude's
  `step_parts.txt` unit) — the candidate pays it once where the reference
  pays it 7–13 times, before any byte time.
- **Invariants:** `y` shape/dtype checked exactly (`check_candidate.py:158-159`);
  threadgroup product ≤ 1,024 enforced (`slots.py:327-328`); 32 KB
  threadgroup memory not enforced by `build` — verified by hand above.

### D. Starting point `notes.md` — what attempt-4 changed and measured

- **Callers/Callees:** none (documentation). Records the single change on
  attempt-2: 256 threads/pair (8 simdgroups) instead of 128, gate/up 12
  blocks in 2 waves of 8 (4 simds idle in wave 2), down 24 blocks in 3
  waves, x/silu strided loops step 256 (`notes.md:3-9`). `block-1.metal`
  byte-identical to attempt-2.
- **Data/Cost (its own run, old independent timing):** predicted
  60/185/650 µs/layer at 1/8/32 rows; measured candidate 50.0/157.8/515.4
  vs original 64.3/218.6/765.7, compiled 65.3/217.4/760.2 (`notes.md:46-52`).
  G2 bit-exact `max_ulp 0.0` at all decode rows under the old grader.
  The 1-row baselines shift between runs (64.3/65.3 here vs 99.8/135.0 in
  attempt-2's run; `notes.md:54-57`) — within-run comparison is the valid
  one. Claude's re-grade on the same old grader gave candidate
  92.1/165.4/529.9 vs compiled 139.5/221.4/762.4
  (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-experts.json`), and the new
  chained timing reverses the 1-row verdict (§A, §E).
- **Invariants:** states the kept boundary explicitly: same per-block
  numerics, same float32 accumulation and bfloat16 rounding points,
  3,840 B threadgroup memory, valid for all rows (`notes.md:22-26`).

### E. Reference `ref_experts` + `SwitchGLU` — what the slot must match

- **Callers:** grader `REFERENCE["experts"]` (`slots.py:85`), called per
  layer on captured decode inputs and on `capture_prefill` inputs
  (`check_candidate.py:153-169,272-305`); in the model, `MoE.__call__`
  calls `self.experts(x, inds)` (`slots.py:110-114` installs the slot the
  same way).
- **Callees:** `ref_experts` (`slots.py:55-82`): `expand_dims`, optional
  `_gather_sort`/`_scatter_unsort` (`slots.py:62-65,80-81`), three
  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4,
  mode="affine", sorted_indices=do_sort)` (`slots.py:67-79`), and compiled
  `swiglu` between them (`slots.py:79`; `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:9`
  import, `activations.py` fused kernel). The port's twin is
  `SwitchGLU.__call__` (`switch_layers.py:176-199`): same sort threshold
  `indices.size >= 64` (`switch_layers.py:181`; `slots.py:62`), same three
  products via `QuantizedSwitchLinear` replaced by
  `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear` with `transpose=False` in the served
  model (round 1 `territory-switch-layers.md` §A, §D). Kernel inventory:
  7/layer at 1–8 rows (3×(Arange+GatherQMM) + silu-mul), 13/layer at
  32 rows (+ 6 sort glue) (round 1 `territory-switch-layers.md` §A;
  `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md:136-139`).
- **Data:** same shapes/dtypes as §A. Sorted path (rows ≥ 16): pairs
  flattened, `order`/`inv_order` [rows*4], x gathered to `[rows*4, 1, 768]`;
  products on sorted pairs, then unsorted back to positional `y`
  (`switch_layers.py:12-24`; `slots.py:64-65,81-82`). Output squeezed to
  `[rows, 4, 768]` (`slots.py:82`).
- **Neighbours:** identical slot edges as §A (routing before, combine
  after). The sort is internal to the reference: G2 compares only `y`
  (`check_candidate.py:153-169`), so a candidate may sort or not — but the
  sort flag changes which MLX kernel the reference dispatches (§F), and
  that changes the bits.
- **Cost:** knock-out 0.92 ms/step at 1 row, 14.67 ms at 32 rows of a
  28.19 ms step (round 1 `territory-switch-layers.md` §A;
  `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md:170,211`). Chained reference
  80.3/239.6/797.6 µs/layer (§A table). Reads 51 MB at 1 row, 908 MB at
  32 rows vs 443 MB distinct-expert must-read (GPU counters; round 1
  `ineff-runs-1.md`, `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md:26,32`).
- **Invariants:** two thresholds, often conflated. (1) Sort:
  `inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16 (`switch_layers.py:181`). (2) Kernel
  dispatch: `gather_qmm_rhs` needs `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ &&
  B/E>=4` with `B = rows*4`, `E = 60` ⇔ rows ≥ 60 (round 1
  `territory-switch-layers.md` §G, `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §A/§C;
  MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp:2005,2012,2073-2093`). Decode 1/8/32 rows
  (B/E ≤ 2.13) always run `gather_qvm` even when sorted; prefill
  127/1,016/2,048 rows (B/E = 8.5/67.7/136.5) run `gather_qmm_rhs`. Each
  product accumulates float32 and rounds to bfloat16; `silu(gate)*up` on
  bfloat16 values, rounded to bfloat16 before down
  (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). New G2: every element equal at all
  six sizes (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:22-27`).

### F. MLX dispatch — `affine_gather_qvm` (decode) vs `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill)

- **Callers:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp:1980-2094`;
  installed version 0.32.4). Decode call shape `M=1, N=384/768, K=768/384,
  B=rows*4` (round 1 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §A).
- **Callees (decode):** `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`
  installed headers) → `qvm_impl` (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid
  `(M, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of 64 threads (2 simdgroups); gate/up
  `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. At 1 row that is 24/24/48 threadgroups
  per product across the three sequential kernels. Each lane owns one
  strided `K` element per iteration and decodes 32 outputs via `qouter`;
  float32 accumulation, `simd_sum` at the end, bfloat16 store
  (`quantized.h:1317-1329`).
- **Callees (prefill):** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs`
  (`quantized.h:2580-2718` installed headers): `BM=16, BN=32, BK=32`
  tiles (round 1 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §C),
  `schedule_row_tile<BM>` (`utils.h:501-542` installed headers) maps each
  tile to a run of same-expert rows via per-expert `offsets`;
  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (`quantized.h:674-791`) dequantizes weight tiles
  into threadgroup memory, `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:451`,
  `AccumType=float` default) multiplies. Round 1 mapped this kernel as
  "never run in decode" and did not read its arithmetic
  (`territory-quantized-kernels.md` §C); the arithmetic below is new in
  this round, read from the installed 0.32.4 headers.
- **Data:** identical weight/scale/bias layouts both paths. Difference is
  precision placement: `qvm` keeps `scale*q + bias` in float32 registers

## What it does

In every decode step and every prefill chunk, each of the 20 layers runs
`MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:230-232`): the
routed experts produce `y` [rows,4,768] bf16 in `inds` order, routing produces
`weights` [rows,4] f32, the shared expert produces `shared` [rows,768] bf16,
and combine returns `out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bf16)
+ shared` [rows,768] bf16 (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`). This territory is
the starting point now occupying the `combine` slot —
`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (one fused kernel/layer) — the
reference behind it, and the MLX kernels the reference launches. Round 1
mapped the same chain as territory `other-kernels` checklist G and
`ineff-model-2` (confirmed); this entry writes only what is new under round
2's rules (bit-exact G2 at decode + prefill sizes, chained piece timing;
`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md`), citing round 1 by path.

## Checklist

### A. Starting point: `fused_combine` (`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1/`)

- **Callers:** the grader builds it from `spec.json` via `slots.build`
  (`bench/grader/slots.py:303-345`) and calls it per layer as
  `fn(y=…, weights=…, shared=…)` (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:139-141`);
  in the model it replaces the combine line of `MoE.__call__`
  (`mobilemoe.py:231-232`, split form `slots.py:116`). Shapes: decode
  1 / 8 / 32 rows and prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows (brief: rows is tokens
  in the step; prefill rows from `slots.capture_prefill`, `slots.py:214-254`).
- **Callees:** one `mx.fast.metal_kernel` launch per layer, 20 per step.
  `spec.json:1`: grid `rows*768` threads, threadgroup [256,1,1], inputs
  `y, weights, shared`, one bf16 output `out` [rows,768], no header block,
  no template, `atomic_outputs: false`. Body: `block-0.metal:12-25`.
- **Data:** `y` bf16 [rows,4,768] row-contiguous (6,144 B/row), `weights`
  f32 [rows,4] (16 B/row), `shared` bf16 [rows,768] (1,536 B/row) → `out`
  bf16 [rows,768] (1,536 B/row); 9,232 B/row touched in total. One thread
  per output element: `row = idx/768`, `d = idx - row*768`
  (`block-0.metal:12-14`); thread reads `y[row,0..3,d]` (strides of 768
  elements), `weights[row,0..3]`, `shared[row,d]`, computes
  `acc = Σ float(y_j)·weights_j` in f32 (`:20-23`), writes
  `bfloat(acc) + shared` (`:25`). No threadgroup memory, no barriers, no
  atomics; threads fully independent. Grid is always whole threadgroups
  (768 = 3×256), and the indexing is exact for every row count (prefill
  2,048 rows = 1,572,864 threads = 6,144 threadgroups), so its G2 failure
  is arithmetic only (round 1 boundary check, `muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md` *Boundary checks*).
- **Neighbours:** before: experts' `y` and routing's `weights` (positional
  pairing `weights[r,j] ↔ y[r,j,:]`, never re-sorted), shared expert's
  `shared` (outside the slots); after: residual add `h + feed_forward(…)`
  in `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258`), then the next layer.
  A replacement must keep shapes, dtypes, the f32 accumulation, and both
  bf16 rounding points (the astype, then the bf16 `+ shared`).
- **Cost:** 1 kernel/layer. Bytes ÷ peak (200 GB/s, brief): 9,232 /
  73,856 / 295,424 B per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows = **0.05 / 0.37 /
  1.48 µs**; compute ≈7 f32 ops per output element ≈0.03 µs/layer even at
  32 rows against 5.2 TFLOPS peak — both negligible. Measured (old
  independent piece timing): candidate **18.6 / 17.0 / 18.9 µs/layer**
  against compiled reference 23.8 / 26.1 / 32.0 and reference
  23.1 / 22.5 / 39.5 (Claude re-grade, `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`
  §1, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-combine.json`); round
  1's own run: 17.2 / 17.0 / 18.5 against compiled 22.9 / 26.2 / 28.0
  (`attempt-1/notes.md` *Verdict*). Flat in rows: time is the dispatch
  floor, not work — see `ineff-baseline-combine-2`. No chained timing
  exists yet for this slot: the round-2 grader times only after G2 passes
  (`check_candidate.py:308-337`), and this kernel fails G2.
- **Invariants:** round 2 G2 is bit-exact at all six sizes (brief *How each
  attempt is judged*; ADR 0010). Round 1's 2-ULP rule is gone. The kernel
  keeps both rounding points but contracts its mul+add chain to FMAs,
  which the reference never does — 2 elements differ at decode 8/32 rows,
  6 / 50 / 130 at prefill (`grade-exact-combine.json`); see
  `ineff-baseline-combine-1` and checklist C–D below.

### B. Reference: `ref_combine` (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`)

- **Callers:** `MoE.__call__` split form (`slots.py:97-119`, combine at
  `:116`); the grader's correctness check calls it directly per layer
  (`check_candidate.py:140`) — **the G2 reference is the eager MLX graph,
  not the compiled one**; `mx.compile(ref_combine)` appears only in timing
  (`check_candidate.py:322`). In a `routing+combine` candidate the combine
  part still receives the captured reference weights (brief; `slots.py`
  slot table `:29-40`).
- **Callees:** eagerly, 5 kernels/layer, 100/step (`results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md:140`:
  AsType 40, Multiply 20, Sum 20, Add 20 per step), mapped in round 1's
  `muse-spark/exploration/territory-other-kernels.md` checklist G:
  1. `y` bf16→f32: `copy_v` (`…/metal/kernels/copy.h`, `cast_to<U>` per
     element; exact — bf16 ⊂ f32), grid rows·4·768 threads;
  2. broadcast multiply by `weights[...,None]`: `binary_g`
     (`…/metal/kernels/binary.h`), `Multiply` op `x * y`
     (`…/metal/kernels/binary_ops.h`), f32 product rounded once to f32,
     grid rows·4·768;
  3. sum over axis −2 (size 4, stride 768): `col_reduce_small`
     (`…/metal/kernels/reduction/reduce_col.h`), threadgroup (32,4,1) =
     128 threads (strided-small dispatch; round 1 territory-other-kernels
     G, citing MLX v0.32.4 `reduce.cpp` — installed version confirmed
     0.32.4); `Sum` op `a + b`, init 0 (`…/reduction/ops.h`);
  4. f32→bf16: `copy_v` again — the single astype rounding (RNE);
  5. `+ shared`: `binary_vv` (`binary.h`), `Add` op `x + y` in bf16,
     grid rows·768.
  (Header paths under `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`.)
- **Data:** intermediates are f32 [rows,4,768] after steps 1–2 (12,288
  B/row written + read), f32 [rows,768] after the sum, bf16 after step 4.
  Kernel-touch bytes ≈1.3 / 11 / 43 MB/step at 1 / 8 / 32 rows, but the
  intermediates stay in GPU cache between dependent kernels; unique DRAM
  traffic is the 9,232 B/row above (round 1 territory-other-kernels G).
- **Neighbours:** identical to A — that identity is the boundary
  (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md` *Boundary*).
- **Cost:** knock-out 0.61 ms/step at 1 row, 0.33 ms at 32 rows
  (`tables.md:335`; per layer 30.5 / 16.5 µs — the knock-out and the piece
  harness disagree on standalone cost, round 1 `ineff-model-2`); piece
  timing as in A. `mx.compile` fuses the casts (Claude:
  `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`, via round 1 ineff-model-2) and
  saves 0.29 / 0.26 / 0.27 ms/step end to end alone
  (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §3), yet its piece timing
  (23.8–26.1–32.0 µs/layer) still trails the fused candidate at every
  row count.
- **Invariants:** the arithmetic contract a replacement must reproduce
  bit for bit: exact bf16→f32 casts; each product `p_j` rounded once to
  f32 by the multiply kernel; the 4-term sum folded by separate f32 adds
  (checklist C); one bf16 rounding of the sum; one bf16 add of `shared`.
  Because each step is its own kernel, **no mul+add contraction can occur
  in the reference** — that asymmetry is the whole G2 gap (checklist D).

### C. The reference sum's association (`col_reduce_small`, size-4 axis)

Per output element (fixed row, fixed column `d`), `reduce_col.h` runs:
`totals[i]` (4 column lanes per thread) start at `Sum::init = 0`; the loop
over the reduction (`r = lid.y; r < rows·4; r += lsize.y`, `lsize.y = 4`)
gives each `lid.y` lane exactly one product, so lane `j` holds
`0 + p_j = p_j` exactly; then, if `lsize.y > 1`, the threadgroup fold on
`lid.y == 0` computes `t = p_0; t = p_1 + t; t = p_2 + t; t = p_3 + t`,
each `op(a,b) = a + b` rounded once to f32. IEEE addition commutes, so the
reference association is exactly the left fold **((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃** with a
rounding after every add. That association does **not** change with rows:
the reduced axis is always size 4; more rows only add threadgroups /
non-column reductions. Round 1's boundary emulation already proved the
point from the candidate side: all 120 pure association trees of the four
products give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches to the grader
fingerprint, while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it exactly
(`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The 2.0-ULP touch*).

### D. The candidate's arithmetic (`block-0.metal:20-25`)

The source writes the same left fold, `p₀ + p₁ + p₂ + p₃` as one f32
expression, then `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]`. Compiled as a single
Metal kernel (MLX `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, `slots.py:309-316`; no compiler
flags are expressible in `spec.json`), the mul+adds are FP-contracted
into FMAs: `fma(y_j, w_j, partial)` keeps the product unrounded, so `acc`
can differ from the reference fold by ~1 f32 ULP. The bf16 rounding of
`acc` absorbs that almost always; it flips only when `acc` lies within
the delta of a bf16 rounding midpoint, yielding a 1-ULP-different sum,
which the bf16 `+ shared` then preserves — or magnifies in ULP terms
when `shared ≈ −sum` cancels toward zero (the grader floors the ULP at
`|r| = 0.001`, `check_candidate.py:84-99`, so near-zero results report
large ULP gaps from tiny absolute differences). Attempt-2's explicit
`acc += product` loop shows the identical fingerprint (0.0 / 2.0 / 1.0),
so loop form and staging are exonerated too: only suppressing
contraction (e.g. the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary named)
while keeping the ((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ fold can close it. Counts under the
new grader (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-combine.json`,
summed over 20 layers; totals = rows·768·20 elements):

| Size | Differ | Max ULP | Elements | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode 1 row | 0 | 0.0 | 15,360 | 0 |
| decode 8 rows | 2 | 2.0 | 122,880 | 16 ppm |
| decode 32 rows | 2 | 1.0 | 491,520 | 4 ppm |
| prefill 127 rows | 6 | 1.0 | 1,950,720 | 3 ppm |
| prefill 1,016 rows | 50 | 16.0 | 15,605,760 | 3 ppm |
| prefill 2,048 rows | 130 | 32.0 | 31,457,280 | 4 ppm |

The count grows with the element count at a roughly constant few-ppm
rate — more samples of the same rounding-boundary lottery, **not** a
kernel switch at prefill sizes (combine's MLX kernels are identical at
every row count; the 60-row `gather_qvm → gather_qmm_rhs` switch belongs
to the experts slot and cannot enter here, since the grader feeds
captured `y`). The larger max ULP at prefill is the tail of the same
lottery plus near-zero cancellation after `+ shared`. It fails G2 at
five of six sizes; in the model the round-1 kernel changed 7 of 32
vLLM sequences from token 0 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §2).
Folded in from explorer-grader's note below: the fix must hold at
2,048 rows, not only at decode sizes (the per-element sum is
row-count-independent, so a correct fix scales by construction, but
only the six graded sizes certify it), and a fix that is slower at
prefill sizes would be invisible to `beats_compiled`, which times
decode sizes only (`check_candidate.py:311`).

### E. Micro-path of the candidate body (bounded, not posted)

Each thread does one `idx/768` integer divide, 4 scalar bf16 loads
strided 768 elements apart (coalesced within each expert plane), the
same 4 weights re-loaded by all 768 threads of a row (cache-broadcast),
and scalar shared/out accesses. Round 1's attempt-2 (vectorized u64
loads, staged weights/shared, one barrier, 192-thread threadgroup/row)
measured 17.9 / 16.1 / 18.1 µs/layer (`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-2/notes.md`)
— the same floor and the same 8→32-row slope (+1.5–2 µs for 4× work,
against +1.1 µs predicted from traffic alone). Vectorizing or staging
therefore buys nothing measurable; the slope is memory latency at
growing grid size, and the divide/loads sit under the dispatch floor.
No entry: expected saving <1 µs/layer, inside run-to-run spread.

## Relations

- **Fed by:** `baseline-experts` (produces `y`; its prefill rounding

# From round 2, a kernel must be bit-exact at every size it runs at, prefill included, and the piece timing chains the layers

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*

**The change.** Claude's measurement of round 1 ([findings](../findings/muse-round-1.md)) found that round 1's final attempts, which passed the grader, broke the brief's end-to-end rule in the model, and that one of them slowed the decode step it was meant to speed up. The grader missed three things:

1. **Sizes.** It tested a slot on a decode step's inputs only, at 1, 8 and 32 rows. The same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill, at 127 to 2,048 rows with 128-token prompts. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes, from `gather_qvm` to `gather_qmm_rhs`, and so does its rounding. Round 1's experts kernel copied `gather_qvm` bit for bit, and differed in 62% of its outputs at each prefill size.
2. **Exactness.** G2 allowed small differences: 2 bfloat16 units in the last place, and 10⁻⁴ for routing weights. End to end, the brief asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. Round 1's routing weights, within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences in 24 tokens.
3. **Latency.** The piece timing ran 20 layers' calls with no data between them, so the GPU could overlap them. At 1 row, round 1's experts kernel was 29% faster than the reference on overlapped calls and 66% slower on chained ones (`bench/micro/chain_timing.py`). In the model it slowed the decode step by 1.2 ms (22% in vLLM, 25% in plain MLX).

On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose, before round 2:
- **every call:** the kernels run wherever `MoE.__call__` runs, the prefill included;
- **bit-exact** outputs;
- **chained** piece timing.

## How it works

- **G2 at two kinds of size.** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` checks every layer at:
  - the captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
  - the first prefill chunk at 1, 8 and 32 requests (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows), recorded while it runs (`slots.capture_prefill`), with the prompts `time_candidates.py` uses.
- **Bit-exact.** An output passes only if it equals the reference's:
  - for routing, the 4 experts and their weights, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order;
  - for combine and experts, every element.

  The grader still reports the largest gap, in units in the last place, to help find the cause. The reference checked against itself shows no difference at any size.
- **Chained timing.** Each layer's call takes one input through `link`, a single fused kernel that adds 0 × one value of the previous call's output, so the call can't start before the previous one finishes. Every function timed (reference, compiled, candidate and baseline) gets the same link. The chained times match those of a real data chain within 10%.
  - **Why not `mx.depends`:** it orders only the graph. In a test on 2026-11-04, round 1's experts kernel took 46 µs per layer with it at 1 row, as fast as with no dependency, against 133 to 195 µs with a real data dependency in three runs.
- **The end-to-end check and G3 are unchanged.**
  - `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` now takes several `SLOT=FOLDER` attempts.
  - It times each slot alone, against its own compiled reference, and all of them together.

## Consequences

- **No round-1 attempt passes the new G2,** so round 2 has no baseline in any slot. Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's final attempts are its starting points, named in Claude's findings.
- **The experts slot needs a kernel exact at prefill sizes,** matching `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding from 60 rows on, or a single design whose rounding matches both of MLX's kernels.
- **A grader run takes longer.** It loads the model (760 MB) for every slot and runs three prefill chunks.
- **The piece timing now includes one small link kernel per layer** for every function timed. That brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs.
- **Not covered:** prefill speed. G3 times decode steps only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token.

## Considered options

- **Decode calls only,** with MLX's code in the prefill. The kernels would need to be exact only at decode sizes, but they would no longer replace the whole MoE block. Not chosen: surucuonur asked for every call.
- **Keep the tolerances, and relax the token rule** to counting the sequences that differ. Simpler kernels, but the claim would become "the same model up to rounding", with a threshold to pick.
- **Keep independent timing,** and rely on G3 to catch latency. Round 2's builders would again rank attempts by a number that hid a 22% slowdown.
- **`mx.depends` for the chain.** No extra kernel, but it doesn't make the GPU wait.

# Inefficiency: the experts attempt is slower than the reference when the layers are chained, at 1 row

- **Owner:** explorer-g3
- **Status:** superseded by ineff-baseline-experts-2
- **Version:** 2
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:18:59Z
- **Next:** none — the same claim is carried kernel-side by `ineff-baseline-experts-2`; the G3-side arithmetic below is cited there by note

## Slot

`experts`. Kernel side owned by territory `baseline-experts` (starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4`); this entry carries the measurement side from territory `g3`, so the lead can settle it as one claim with that territory's entry when it lands.

## What happens

Attempt-4 is one fused kernel per layer with grid `rows*1024` threads in threadgroups of 256 — `rows*4` threadgroups, one per (row, expert-slot) pair (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/spec.json`). Timed the old grader's way, with the 20 layers' calls overlapping, it beats the reference (61.0 vs 86.0 µs/layer at 1 row). Timed chained — each call's `x` is the previous call's output, as in a decode step — it is slower than the reference at 1 row and faster at 8 and 32 rows. In the model, where layers are chained by construction, it slows the 1-request decode step by ~1.2 ms. Claude's estimate from the code: 4 threadgroups at 1 row cannot fill the 16-core GPU, so one call's latency is long even when many calls together go fast ([muse-round-1.md:123](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md)). That mechanism is an estimate; the timings below are measured.

## Cost

Chained vs independent piece timing, experts reference / attempt-4, µs per layer (`bench/micro/chain_timing.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/console-chain.txt`; [territory-g3.md](territory-g3.md) piece 3):

| Timing | 1 row | 8 rows | 32 rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| independent: reference / attempt | 86.0 / 61.0 | 219.1 / 165.1 | 767.3 / 535.0 |
| chained: reference / attempt | 80.3 / **132.9** | 239.6 / **175.9** | 797.6 / **587.6** |
| chained gap × 20 layers | **+1.052 ms/step** | −1.274 ms/step | −4.200 ms/step |

End to end, attempt-4 alone against the unchanged model (G3, median of 3 shuffled repeats): **+1.162 ms (+21.6%) at 1 request**, −0.817 at 8, −4.154 at 32 in vLLM (`console-vllm.txt`); +1.228 / −0.832 / −3.661 ms in plain MLX (`console-plain.txt`). The chained gap at 1 row (+1.052 ms/step) reproduces the end-to-end slowdown to within 0.11 ms (vLLM) / 0.18 ms (plain). Against the brief's G3 rule the attempt also loses to its compiled reference at 1 request (compiled-experts +0.066 ms, vLLM). Bytes per pair are unchanged by row count (553 KB per pair, `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/notes.md`): the 1-row cost is not bytes.

## Kind

Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): at 1 row the chained call leaves most of the GPU idle — few threadgroups, latency exposed — while reading the same weight bytes as the faster overlapped timing. At 8 and 32 rows the same kernel is bandwidth/efficiency-limited in the normal way and wins.

## Spans

`g3` (this measurement), `baseline-experts` (the kernel), `grader` (the round-1 timing that hid it; the new chained timing in `check_candidate.py` is the fixed instrument).

## Predicted saving

Removing the chained 1-row penalty — bringing the chained call to the reference's 80.3 µs/layer — saves (132.9 − 80.3) µs × 20 layers = **1.05 ms per decode step at 1 request**, with nothing claimed at 8 or 32 rows, where the attempt already saves 1.27 / 4.20 ms/step chained and the fix must not give that back. Measured against G3 instead of the piece timing, the same fix is worth up to 1.16 ms (vLLM) / 1.23 ms (plain) at 1 request: the amount by which the attempt currently slows the step it was meant to speed up.

## Verdict

- **Callees:** `Variants` ([time_candidates.py:72-96](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) installs, per slot, the attempt (`muse-<slot>`), the slot's reference under `mx.compile` (`compiled-<slot>`), and — with several slots given — `muse-all` and `compiled-all`, by replacing `MoE.__call__` in every layer via `slots.make_moe_call`. Token checks: `plain_checks` (24 greedy tokens after 128-token prompts, 1 and 32 requests, [time_candidates.py:98-120](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) and `rf.vllm_checks` ([repeat_fixes.py:174-224](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)). Timing: `rf.time_variants` ([repeat_fixes.py:276-343](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)) — settings (1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128) requests/prompts, 3 repeats shuffled per repeat (`random.Random(100+rep)`, [repeat_fixes.py:290-293](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)), 256 generated tokens per run (`--tokens` default 256, [time_candidates.py:135](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)), period = median decode-step period from `breakdown.py`'s recorder; the printed change is the median of the 3 repeat medians against `base`, with the repeats' range as the spread.
- **Data:** one `check` record and 27 `run` records (9 variants × 3 row counts × 3 repeats, per engine) in each `muse-*.jsonl`. Kernel counts come from `count_ops` ([repeat_fixes.py:136-143](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)): the exported graph of one decode step, view ops excluded — a count of graph ops, where each `mx.compile` region and each custom kernel counts once. It is not a launch trace.
- **Neighbours:** G3's rule (brief, *How each attempt is judged*): an attempt must beat both the unchanged model and its compiled reference, by more than the spread between repeats. `compiled-all` is the control that shows what `mx.compile` of the untouched references already saves with no new kernel.
- **Cost:** the harness itself is not in the step. Machine caveat for every absolute number below: another job of surucuonur's was running and 21.3–22.7 GB of swap were in use; Docker was quit; vLLM ran with `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` ([muse-round-1.md:19](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md)). Shuffled repeats make variant-vs-variant comparisons usable; absolutes carry that caveat.
- **Invariants:** prompts for the token check are random tokens (`mx.random.seed(rows)` + `randint(0, 100000, (rows, 128))` in plain, [time_candidates.py:107-108](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py); `random.Random(7)` + `randrange(1000, 100000)` in vLLM, [repeat_fixes.py:179-185](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)) — near-tie next-token margins are expected, which is why last-bit differences flip tokens (piece 7). Timing runs use their own seeds (`rows*10000+prompt`, [repeat_fixes.py:299](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)), so the timed sequences are not the checked sequences.

### 5. G3 alone and together — plain MLX (`console-plain.txt`, `muse-plain.jsonl`)

- **Callers:** `time_candidates.py plain` (piece 4).
- **Data:** base step 4.998 / 13.541 / 28.496 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 requests (`console-plain.txt` summary block; `muse-plain.jsonl` `run` records, median of 3 repeat medians). Changes against base: experts +1.228 / −0.832 / −3.661 ms; routing +0.233 / −0.361 / −0.318; combine −0.857 / −0.753 / −0.406; **muse-all +0.927 / +0.881 / −1.560**; compiled-all −0.617 / −0.524 / −0.255. Kernel counts at 1 request: base 866, muse-experts 746, muse-routing 666, muse-combine 786, muse-all 466 (`muse-plain.jsonl` `check` records, rows 1); at 32 requests: base 986, muse-all 466.
- **Cost / the additivity test:** the three alone sum to +0.604 / −1.946 / −4.385 ms; together measure +0.927 / +0.881 / −1.560 ms. The interaction (together − sum of alone) is **+0.323 / +2.827 / +2.825 ms**, i.e. +16.1 / +141.3 / +141.2 µs per layer. Adding routing+combine to experts-alone costs −0.301 / +1.713 / +2.101 ms (muse-all − muse-experts) where alone they promise +0.233−0.857 / −0.361−0.753 / −0.318−0.406 ms.
- **Invariants:** kernel-count reductions are exactly additive here: −120 (experts) −200 (routing) −80 (combine) = −400 = 866−466 at 1 request; −240 −200 −80 = −520 at 32 requests. The time is not additive while the count is — the fact any explanation must meet.

### 6. G3 alone and together — vLLM (`console-vllm.txt`, `muse-vllm.jsonl`)

- **Callers:** `time_candidates.py vllm` (piece 4).
- **Data:** base step 5.370 (5.320–5.452) / 14.363 (14.327–14.475) / 29.851 (29.657–29.952) ms (`console-vllm.txt` summary block). Changes: experts **+1.162 (+21.6%)** / −0.817 / −4.154; routing +0.185 / −0.397 / −0.490; combine −0.514 / −0.705 / −0.390; **muse-all +0.980 (+18.3%) / +0.163 (+1.1%) / −1.756 (−5.9%)**; compiled-all −0.498 / −0.558 / −0.242 — all against round 1's prediction of −0.54 / −1.81 / −5.72 ms ([muse-round-1.md:80-91](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md)). Kernel counts at 1 request: base 967, muse-experts 847, muse-routing 767, muse-combine 887, muse-all **567** (`muse-vllm.jsonl` `check` records, rows 1); at 32 requests: base 1087, muse-all 567.
- **Cost / the additivity test:** the three alone sum to +0.833 / −1.919 / −5.034 ms; together measure +0.980 / +0.163 / −1.756 ms. Interaction: **+0.147 / +2.082 / +3.278 ms** (+7.4 / +104.1 / +163.9 µs per layer). Adding routing+combine to experts-alone costs −0.182 / **+0.980** / **+2.398 ms**. The compiled references, the control, compose near-additively: their alone changes sum to −0.442 / −0.419 / −0.532 ms against compiled-all's measured −0.498 / −0.558 / −0.242 ms (interaction −0.056 / −0.139 / +0.290 ms) — so the non-additivity is a property of the three custom kernels together, not of replacing three slots at once. At 1 request the vLLM interaction (+0.147 ms) is the size of the base spread (5.320–5.452 = 0.132 ms); at 8 and 32 requests it is 15–25× the spread and repeats in plain MLX (piece 5), so it is not repeat noise.
- **Invariants:** same additive kernel counts as plain: −120 −200 −80 = −400 at 1 request, −240 −200 −80 = −520 at 32. The headline form: **567 kernels/step run slower than 967 at 1 and 8 requests** — kernel count is not the step's cost driver here.

### 7. Token divergence (`check` records, both engines)

- **Callers:** `plain_checks` / `vllm_checks` (piece 4): 24 greedy tokens, 128-token prompts; a sequence *differs* if any of its 24 tokens differs from base's, with `first_differ_step` the first such token ([repeat_fixes.py:227-234](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)).
- **Data:** sequences differing of 32 at 32 requests — plain MLX: experts 19 from token 0, routing 7 from token 1, combine 5 from token 2, muse-all 19 from token 0; vLLM: experts 12, routing 9, combine 7, muse-all 13, all from token 0 (`muse-plain.jsonl` / `muse-vllm.jsonl` `check` records rows 32; [muse-round-1.md:58-62](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md)). At 1 request plain MLX each single attempt differs in its 1 sequence from token 2 while muse-all is exact; vLLM at 1 request every variant is exact — the two engines use different check prompts (piece 4), so the 1-request outcomes are prompt-dependent near-tie flips, not a disagreement about the kernels. Every `compiled-*` variant is exact in both engines at both row counts: the unchanged model is deterministic, and every difference comes from the attempts.
- **Neighbours:** divergence has two measured causes, by slot: the experts attempt is bit-exact at decode sizes but differs in 62% of prefill outputs (piece 2), and the prefill (127–2,048 rows) runs before the first decode step, so its difference is present from token 0; routing's (≤8.7×10⁻⁶) and combine's (≤2 ULP at decode) last-bit differences flip near-tie greedy choices within a few tokens ([muse-round-1.md:66-72](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md)).
- **Cost:** divergence is a correctness verdict (the brief's end-to-end G2), not a timing input: the timed runs generate their own 256 tokens per variant (piece 4), and each slot's per-step cost is data-independent in shape (fixed grids in all three `spec.json` files; the experts attempt reads one expert's weights per (row, slot) pair whichever expert is chosen), so differing tokens do not by themselves change what a step costs. They cannot explain piece 5/6's interaction.
- **Invariants:** `first_differ_step` 0 at 32 requests for experts/muse-all in both engines is the prefill signature; routing/combine first differ at step ≥0 only where their decode/prefill rounding reaches the logits — the counts, not the step, are the stable part across engines.

## Where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why

Three separate gaps, in the order the measurement establishes them:

1. **Experts at 1 request: piece says faster, step says slower — explained.** Independent piece timing: attempt 29% faster than the reference (61.0 vs 86.0 µs/layer, piece 3) and 92.1 vs 139.5 µs against the compiled reference in the re-grade (piece 1), a promised −0.948 ms/step. G3: **+1.162 ms (vLLM) / +1.228 ms (plain)** against base — the "1.2 ms" slowdown. Chained piece timing reverses the piece sign: 132.9 vs 80.3 µs/layer, +1.052 ms/step, matching G3 to 0.11–0.18 ms. Cause (estimate from the code, [muse-round-1.md:123](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-1.md); kernel side owned by `baseline-experts`): the attempt launches `rows*4` threadgroups of 256 threads — 4 threadgroups at 1 row on a 16-core GPU — so one call's latency is long, and the old timing hid exactly that latency by overlapping the 20 layers' calls. Posted as [ineff-g3-2](ineff-g3-2.md).
2. **Per-slot piece-vs-step gaps at 1 request, routing and combine — measured as gaps, cause not yet timed.** Routing's piece promises −0.124 ms/step against the compiled reference (piece 1); in vLLM it measures +0.185 against base where the compiled reference measures −0.220, i.e. **0.405 ms/step slower than the compiled reference in-step**, a 0.529 ms/step swing from the piece figure. Combine goes the other way: piece −0.104 ms/step, in-step −0.514 against base vs −0.288 compiled (vLLM), over-delivering. No chained routing/combine timing exists in this data (piece 3), so neither gap has a measured cause; the new grader's chained timing (piece 2) is the instrument that will produce one. Noted for `baseline-routing` / `baseline-combine` below; no inefficiency posted from G3 alone.
3. **All three together: slower than each alone predicts — measured, not explained.** Kernel reductions add exactly (pieces 5/6); time does not. The interaction is +0.15 / **+2.08** / **+3.28 ms** (vLLM) and +0.32 / **+2.83** / **+2.83 ms** (plain) at 1 / 8 / 32 requests, while the compiled references together stay within ±0.29 ms of additive. Equivalently: bolting the routing+combine attempts onto the experts attempt *costs* 0.98 ms at 8 requests and 2.40 ms at 32 (vLLM) where those two alone *save* 1.10 and 0.88 ms. What the data rules out: kernel count (additive, and fewer), token divergence (cost is shape-fixed, piece 7), repeat noise (15–25× the spread at 8/32, both engines), and the compiled-reference path (additive). What remains consistent with the numbers, in order: (a) each fused custom kernel carries a serial per-call latency that the 20-layer overlapped piece timing hid and that only fully serialises when all three sit on the same layer chain — the experts instance of this *is* measured (gap 1), and routing shows the same sign at 1 request (gap 2); (b) an interaction between the three custom kernels' execution (occupancy, cache or dispatch behaviour) that no single-slot run excites. The measurement that separates (a) from (b) — pairwise G3 (`experts+routing`, `experts+combine`, `routing+combine`; `time_candidates.py` builds `muse-all` for any subset, [time_candidates.py:85-87](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) and chained piece timings for routing/combine under the new grader — has not been run; explorers do not run GPU jobs, so it is left as the entry's predicted test. Posted as [ineff-g3-1](ineff-g3-1.md) with the interaction itself as the cost.

13|## What happens

15|The starting point computes `scores[e] = 1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))`
16|(`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:35`): the fast
17|(non-`precise`) Metal `exp` of `-acc`, then one division, for all signs.
18|The reference's `mx.sigmoid` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`) is MLX's unary
19|`Sigmoid` (`mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`,
20|installed MLX 0.32.4):

22|```metal

24|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;

28|1 ULP: (a) `metal::precise::exp` vs `metal::exp`; (b) the exponent argument
29|is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0` the result is the subtraction
30|`1 - y` rather than a direct division. With 60 scores per row and 4 selected,
31|even a bit-exact matmul behind this sigmoid would still leave most rows
32|differing — this cause is independent of `ineff-baseline-routing-1`, and
33|both must be fixed for G2. (That the 4-term weight sum is *not* a third

13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point gives each row exactly one 32-thread threadgroup
16|(`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/spec.json`: grid `rows*32`,
17|threadgroup 32; `block-0.metal:10-11`). At 1 row that is a single simdgroup
18|on a 16-core GPU. Inside the group, threads 0-27 compute two experts and
19|threads 28-31 one (`block-0.metal:25-36`); then, after the second barrier,
20|thread 0 alone runs a 60-iteration serial insertion scan over the biased
21|scores while the other 31 threads idle (`block-0.metal:39-61`), and alone
22|writes the outputs. The reference, by contrast, covers the same work with
23|many-thread kernels even at 1 row (the GEMV dispatch alone uses 4
24|threadgroups × 128 threads at rows=1; territory section 3.1). Round 1's
25|builders measured the consequence as a fixed floor, not body cost: the fused
26|kernel sits at ~24-28 µs/layer in the piece harness while the reference's 12
27|kernels cost ~3 µs each pipelined (`kernels/routing/attempt-1/notes.md:47-59`,
28|`attempt-2/notes.md`), and 8 rows ran *faster* than 1 row (23.6 vs 28.5
29|µs/layer) — the signature of fixed cost amortising over threadgroups, i.e.
30|of the 1-row case having too little parallel work per launch.
31|

33|
34|At 1, 8 and 32 rows (decode): the kernel body itself is small — 92k FLOP/row
35|(2×60×768) on one simdgroup is on the order of 1 µs, and the serial scan is
36|60 short iterations — so most of the measured 25.3/24.3/68.9 µs/layer
37|(independent timing, `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:47`) is per-launch
38|fixed cost that a single-simdgroup launch amortises worst. The end-to-end
39|price is visible at 1 request: the starting point is +0.185 ms/step while the
40|compiled reference is −0.220 ms/step (`muse-round-1.md:85`), a ~0.41 ms/step
41|(≈20 µs/layer) deficit at exactly the row count where this entry's occupancy
42|is worst; at 8/32 requests the same kernel already beats the compiled

1|# Territory: baseline-routing — the routing slot's starting point under bit-exact G2
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-routing
4|- **Status:** exploring
5|- **Version:** 1

7|- **Next:** post ineff-baseline-routing-1..4, then fold any notes
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|In every decode step and every prefill chunk, each of the 20 layers runs
12|`MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`): cast the
13|layer input to float32, multiply by the router weight transposed, sigmoid, add the
14|expert bias only for selection, take the top-4 experts per row, gather their
15|*unbiased* scores, normalise them (divide by their sum + 1e-20) and scale by 2.5.
16|The slot outputs `inds` [rows,4] uint32 and `weights` [rows,4] float32; `inds`
17|feeds the experts slot, `weights` feeds combine, which sums the 4 (expert,
18|weight) pairs *in the emitted order* — which is why round 2's G2 requires the
19|same experts, the same weights and the same order, bit for bit
20|(`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:25-27`,
21|`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:119-121`).
22|
23|The starting point is round 1's `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1`: one fused
24|Metal kernel per layer (`block-0.metal`, 78 lines; `spec.json`: one kernel
25|`fused_routing`, grid `rows*32`, threadgroup 32). One threadgroup per row stages
26|`x[row]` (768 bfloat16→float32) in threadgroup memory, each of the 32 threads
27|computes 1–2 experts' 768-term dot products serially, writes
28|`sigmoid(acc)` to `scores[60]`, and thread 0 alone does a serial insertion
29|top-4 scan over the biased scores and writes `inds`/`weights`
30|(`block-0.metal:10-78`).
31|
32|## The headline finding (details in ineff-baseline-routing-1 and -2)
33|
34|Under the new grader the starting point fails G2 at **every** size while the
35|experts and their order always match (`rows_other_experts` 0 everywhere):
36|rows differing 20/159/638 at decode 1/8/32 rows (of 20/160/640 rows summed over
37|20 layers — 100% / 99.4% / 99.7% of rows) and 2,518/16,187/32,743 at prefill
38|127/1,016/2,048 rows (of 2,540/20,320/40,960 — 99.1% / 79.7% / 79.9%), max
39|relative error 2.6e-06 at decode and up to 8.7e-06 in the prefill
40|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`, quoted in
41|`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/README.md:39`). The experts match because
42|selection is insensitive to last-bit score differences (no captured row is a
43|near-tie at the 4th/5th place); the weights expose every last-bit difference
44|in the 4 selected scores. Section 3 below pins down, op by op, which of the
45|reference's operations the kernel reproduces exactly and which it does not:
46|**the divergence is in the scores — the router matmul's float32 accumulation
47|order (which changes with `rows`) and MLX's sigmoid formula — not in the
48|4-term weight sum, whose order the kernel already matches.**

151|### 3. Op-by-op: where the kernel's arithmetic matches the reference's, and where it does not
152|
153|#### 3.1 The router product `x.astype(f32) @ w_router.T` — DOES NOT MATCH (main cause)
154|
155|The kernel accumulates each expert's dot product **serially, in one thread,
156|in increasing `d` order**: `acc += xsh[d] * w_router[wbase + d]` for
157|`d = 0..767` (`block-0.metal:31-34`; the Metal compiler may contract each
158|mul+add to an FMA, but the grouping stays a 768-long left-to-right chain).
159|
160|The reference never does that. `Matmul::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4,
161|`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, fetched 2026-11-04) sees A = `x` [rows,768]
162|f32 (not transposed), B = `w_router.T` [768,60] (transposed view), so
163|`transpose_a=false, transpose_b=true`, M=rows, N=60, K=768:
164|
165|- **rows = 1 → GEMV.** `min(M,N)==1` routes to `gemv`
166|  (matmul.cpp, `Matmul::eval_gpu`); the `gemv_wide` shortcut is skipped
167|  because the output is float32 (`gemv_wide_config` requires float16/bfloat16
168|  out). Dispatch picks `GEMVKernel<float, BM=4, BN=1, SM=1, SN=32, TM=4,
169|  TN=4>`: each output is accumulated by one simdgroup whose 32 lanes each
170|  serially sum 24 products — lane `l` takes `d = i*128 + l*4 + (0..3)` for
171|  `i = 0..5` (`kernels/gemv.h:162-182`) — and the 32 partials are then combined
172|  by a shuffle tree, `result += simd_shuffle_down(result, sn)` for
173|  sn = 16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`). Grouping: 32 blocked partials + pairwise
174|  tree, not a serial chain.
175|- **rows = 8, 32, 127 → steel split-K GEMM.** In `steel_matmul_axpby` the
176|  split-K case fires when `_tm*_tn <= 2048` (this device's architecture string
177|  ends in `s`; brief:99 names it `applegpu_g13s`), `_tk = 768/16 = 48 >= 8`
178|  and `K >= max(M,N)` (matmul.cpp, Case 1). `steel_gemm_splitk_axpby` uses
179|  BM=16 (M<40) or 32, BN=32, BK=16, WM=WN=2 (steel/gemm split-K dispatch):
180|  partitions = min(max(2, next_pow2(48/(_tm*_tn))), 32) with
181|  `_tm=(M+31)/32, _tn=2` → **32 partitions at rows 8 and 32** (the last
182|  partition also absorbs the remaining 16 BK-iterations,
183|  `steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_splitk.h:140-155`), **8 partitions at rows
184|  127**. Each partition accumulates its K-slice with simdgroup 8×8 matrix
185|  multiply-accumulate over BK=16 chunks in order (GEMMKernel/mma in
186|  `steel/gemm/gemm.h`, `mma.h`), writes a float32 partial, and
187|  `gemm_splitk_accum` sums the partials sequentially in partition order
188|  (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`).
189|- **rows = 1,016, 2,048 → regular steel GEMM.** Split-K no longer fires
190|  (768 < M), so `steel_matmul_regular_axpby` runs with the device tile from
191|  `GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` (for an architecture ending in `s` the macro's fallback:
192|  BM=64, BN=64, BK=16, WM=2, WN=2): K is walked in BK=16 chunks staged through
193|  threadgroup memory, accumulated by simdgroup matrix ops chunk after chunk.
194|
195|So the reference has **three different float32 accumulation orders for the
196|same mathematical product, selected by `rows`** — and none of them is the
197|kernel's serial order. Every score therefore differs from the reference's in
198|the last bits with high probability, which is exactly the observed pattern:
199|~100% of decode rows and ~80–99% of prefill rows have at least one differing
200|weight, while no row picks different experts (the biased-score gaps at the
201|4th/5th place are far larger than 1-ULP score noise on these inputs).
202|The drop from ~100% (decode, GEMV/split-K regimes) to ~80% (1,016/2,048,
203|regular GEMM) is consistent with a per-regime last-bit flip rate; that last
204|step is an inference from the counts, not a measurement.
205|A scalar re-implementation cannot reproduce the steel regimes' rounding by
206|reordering a serial loop: within each 8×8 simdgroup matrix op the 8-product
207|accumulation is the hardware's. A bit-exact candidate must either reuse
208|`simdgroup_float8x8` multiply-accumulate with the same tiling/K-order per
209|regime (branching on `rows` inside the kernel, or one kernel per regime in
210|the spec), or find an accumulation that provably rounds identically — none
211|is known.
212|
213|#### 3.2 The sigmoid — DOES NOT MATCH (independent second cause)
214|
215|Kernel (`block-0.metal:35`): `1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))` — the fast
216|(non-`precise`) `exp`, applied to `-acc`, one division.
217|
218|Reference (`mx.sigmoid` → `Sigmoid` in
219|`mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`, installed headers):
220|
221|```metal
222|auto y = 1 / (1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(x)));
223|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;
224|```
225|
226|Three differences, each able to move the result by 1 ULP: (a) `precise::exp`
227|vs `metal::exp`; (b) the argument is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0`
228|the result is `1 - y` (a subtraction that rounds) instead of the direct
229|division the kernel computes for all signs. Even a kernel whose matmul
230|matched bit for bit would still fail G2 on sigmoid alone for a large share
231|of scores. The fix is free in time: copy this formula verbatim.
232|
233|#### 3.3 Selection, gather, and the weight normalisation — MATCH
234|
235|- `scores + bias`: one f32 add in both (`block-0.metal:45`;
236|  `binary_ops.h:10-15`).
237|- Selection: the kernel's strictly-greater insertion scan emits descending
238|  biased order, earliest index winning ties (`block-0.metal:44-61`). The
239|  reference's argpartition is a full sort of `-(scores+bias)`
240|  (round-1 note, `ineff-runs-2.md:94-98`); on all six graded sizes the emitted
241|  sets *and* order agree (`rows_other_experts` 0, and the grader's worst-row
242|  examples show identical expert lists, grade-exact-routing.json). This is
243|  the part of Claude's round-1 reading ("the reference's order of
244|  operations … differ", round-2 README:39) that does **not** need fixing —
245|  but a builder must preserve the exact tie behaviour, since G2 now also
246|  compares order (`check_candidate.py:120`).
247|- The 4-term sum: the reference's `w.sum(axis=-1)` on a [rows,4] f32 array
248|  takes `row_reduce_small` (row_size 4 <= 64, MLX v0.32.4
249|  `mlx/backend/metal/reduce.cpp`, `row_reduce_general_dispatch` Case 1) in its
250|  per-thread branch (`non_row_reductions=1 < 32 && row_size <= 8`,
251|  `row_reduce_small` dispatch), i.e. `thread_reduce` with `N_READS=4`
252|  (`defines.h:12`): `total = (((0 + w0) + w1) + w2) + w3` in memory order —
253|  and `w`'s memory order is the `inds` order from argpartition, the same
254|  sequence the kernel sums as `s0 + s1 + s2 + s3` (`block-0.metal:64-68`;
255|  `kernels/reduction/reduce_row.h:164-181`). The kernel then adds `1e-20f`
256|  inside the same expression (`denom = s0+s1+s2+s3 + 1e-20f`), the reference
257|  as a separate add after the reduction (`slots.py:48`) — same association,
258|  and in float32 `sum + 1e-20` equals `sum` for any sum above ~1e-27, so the
259|  epsilon cannot be the cause either. Division and ×2.5 are the same single
260|  ops (`binary_ops.h:43-48,208-213`; `block-0.metal:74-77`).
261|  **Conclusion:** once the 4 selected scores are bit-equal and in the same
262|  order, the weights are bit-equal. Builders should spend their effort on
263|  3.1 and 3.2, not on the normalisation — the opposite emphasis to round 2
264|  README:39's example list, which names "the float32 sum order of
265|  `x @ w_router.T` and of `w.sum(...)`" as co-equal suspects.
266|
267|### 4. `spec.json`, `notes.md`, and the round-1 hypothesis/boundary entries
268|
269|- **Callers/callees/data/neighbours:** `spec.json` declares the single kernel
270|  above; `slots.build` enforces threadgroup <= 1024 threads (32 here) and
271|  turns grid expressions into thread counts (`slots.py:326-341`). The
272|  round-1 boundary (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-2-fused-routing.md:47-52`)
273|  declared summation order "fine within tolerance" — true under round 1's
274|  1e-4 G2, false under bit-exact G2; that sentence is the one assumption
275|  round 2 must retire.
276|- **Cost:** the attempt's own verdict and miss analysis (`notes.md:30-68`):
277|  the piece harness's fixed floor is ~24 µs/layer, not one 6.81 µs launch;
278|  the reference's 12 kernels cost ~3 µs each when 20 layers are pipelined.

281|  `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-2/notes.md`) — direct evidence that at
282|  decode sizes dispatch/occupancy, not traffic, binds.

## What building taught

The analysis corrected by what the attempts showed (see `../implementation/README.md`):

1. **Fusion beats grouping in the experts slot.** The ranking put the grouped-read ideal first ([ineff-quantized-kernels-1.md](ineff-quantized-kernels-1.md), 8.6 ms at 32 rows), but the grouped designs lost: attempt-1 (full fused grouped, 15 versions) and attempt-3 (grouped two-kernel) beat compiled only at 32 rows, while attempt-2/4's per-pair fusion won at 1+8 rows and tied at 32. Grouping overhead (pair scan, chunking, barriers, phantom work; duty-cycle ceiling ~55 GB/s vs the 150 ideal) eats the byte savings in the piece harness. The realizable prize came from launch fusion + occupancy + memory-level parallelism, not from reading each expert once.
2. **The piece harness prices kernels differently from in-step knock-outs.** A fused kernel costs a ~24 µs/layer floor with barriers/serial tails (routing) and ~17 µs/layer streaming elementwise (combine) — not 6.81 µs per launch; the reference's 12 routing kernels cost ~3 µs each when pipelined 20 deep. Future predictions must use harness floors; G3 decides the in-step truth.
3. **Experts G2 numerics key** (for the next round's builders): MLX's compiled swiglu computes entirely in bf16 — replicate per-op rounding or fail G2 at ~7%; gate/up/hidden must match bitwise (qvm strided-lane + `simd_sum` order) because down outputs near cancellation amplify 1-ULP flips; the stable bfloat sigmoid is replicable bit-exactly. Start from attempt-4's inner loop.
4. **1-row piece baselines shift between runs** (experts eager 64–100, compiled 62–135 µs/layer across runs on the same machine) — cross-run absolute comparisons are unreliable; within-run vs-compiled is the valid comparison, and G3's spread check matters most at 1 row. The 8/32-row baselines are stable.
5. **Combine's 2-ULP touch is safe**: it is FMA contraction, max exactly 2.0 on realistic inputs with zero exceedances over 20M resampled elements; only adversarial `shared ≈ −acc` cancellation exceeds it. The G2-margin worry was theoretical.

  "output": "# Inefficiency: `gather_qmm_rhs` BM=16 row tiles dispatch empty tiles and compute zero-padded rows at prefill

- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
- **Status:** open
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:23:30Z
- **Next:** verifier to confirm grid arithmetic and padded fractions

## Slot

`experts`

## What happens

MLX's prefill kernel `affine_gather_qmm_rhs`
(`quantized.h:2570-2718`, installed 0.32.4 headers) tiles sorted
pairs into `BM=16`-row tiles. The host over-provisions the grid:
`grid_y = min(B, ceil(B/16) + E - 1)` with `E = 60`
([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1817-1819](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1817-L1819)),
i.e. up to 59 tiles beyond the all-in-one-expert minimum, because
any expert may contribute a partial tile. Each threadgroup then
runs `schedule_row_tile<16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) to find its
expert; threadgroups past the real tile count return false and
exit (`quantized.h:2637-2640`) — launched, scheduled, discarded.

Useful tiles are `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` over per-expert pair
counts `cnt_e`. Tiles that are real but partial
(`tgp_bm < 16`, `quantized.h:2636`) still run the full tile:
`BlockLoader::load_safe` zero-pads the missing `x` rows
(`steel/gemm/loader.h:83-128`), `BlockMMA::mma`
(`steel/gemm/mma.h:513-537`) multiplies them, and
`store_result_safe` discards them (`quantized.h:2687-2695`).
The weight tile is fully loaded and dequantized regardless
(`QuantizedBlockLoader`, `quantized.h:665-791`), so a partial
tile costs a full tile of load + MMA for a fraction of the rows.

This is distinct from the G2 failure itself
(`ineff-baseline-experts-1`): even a bit-exact replica of this
kernel inherits the waste; a replica that regroups rows
(different `BM`, or per-row accumulation with the same per-row
arithmetic — territory §C invariant) avoids it without
changing any valid output bit.

## Cost

Decode 1/8/32 rows: **0 kernels, 0 bytes** — this kernel never
runs there (`B/E ≤ 2.13 < 4`, territory §A table). All figures
below are per product per layer at the prefill sizes, balanced-expert
model (`cnt_e` near the uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are
random tokens, territory §C). `N` tiles: gate/up 12, down 24
(`BN=32`).

| prefill rows | B | dispatched `grid_y` | useful `T` | empty y-tiles | padded rows `T·16−B` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 127 | 508 | 91 | 60 | 31 (34.1%) | 452 / 960 (47.1%) |
| 1,016 | 4,064 | 313 | 300 | 13 (4.2%) | 736 / 4,800 (15.3%) |
| 2,048 | 8,192 | 571 | 540 | 31 (5.4%) | 448 / 8,640 (5.2%) |

Arithmetic: `grid_y` from the host formula; `T = 60·ceil((B/60)/16)`
in the balanced case (`ceil(8.47/16)=1`, `ceil(67.7/16)=5`,
`ceil(136.5/16)=9`). Empty threadgroups per gate/up call =
empty y-tiles × 12 (372 / 156 / 372), per down call × 24
(744 / 312 / 744), each 64 threads that only run the
`schedule_row_tile` scan over 60 experts (`utils.h:514-541`:
two 32-lane prefix iterations) and exit. Padded-row MMA work:
the kernel issues `2·T·16·K·N` flops for `2·B·K·N` useful
(`K·N = 294,912` for both products), so 47.1% / 15.3% / 5.2%
of issued row-work multiplies zero-padded rows. Weight bytes
are *not* wasted by padding (the tile's weights serve its valid
rows); the waste is issued MMA/load slots and threadgroup
occupancy. No measured prefill time exists: the grader times
decode only (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`), so
no µs figure is claimed from measurement.

## Kind

Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): at prefill the path is far
below both peaks, and the padded fraction is pure overhead —
issued work with no output. The empty-tile part is launch/
scheduling overhead; the padded-row part is wasted compute
inside otherwise useful threadgroups.

## Spans

`quantized-kernels` (host grid formula + `schedule_row_tile` +
`BlockMMA` partial-tile path) → slot `experts`. Neighbour:
`baseline-experts` (any grouped prefill branch of a candidate
chooses its own tiling; this entry prices MLX's).

## Predicted saving

0 µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows (kernel never runs
there). At prefill, removing both parts saves the padded
fraction of the main kernel's row work — up to ~47% at
127 rows, ~15% at 1,016, ~5% at 2,048 — plus the empty
threadgroups above, in time-to-first-token only. Prefill
speed is not gated (G3 times decode;
`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`), so this saving
is real but unbanked by the grader; it is worth taking only
if it comes free with the exact prefill branch (e.g. a
per-row `qmm_rhs`-arithmetic kernel has no tiles to pad).
In absolute terms the main kernel's useful MMA floors at
`2·B·K·N / 5.2 TFLOPS` ≈ 57.6 / 461.0 / 929.2 µs per
layer-product at peak (territory §E); issued MMA including
padding floors at 108.9 / 544.6 / 980.0 µs, so the padded
part alone floors at ≈51.3 / 83.5 / 50.8 µs per
layer-product *if* the kernel ran at peak compute — it
does not (two barriers per 32-K tile,
`quantized_utils.h:14-29`), so treat these as lower bounds
on the waste, not predictions.

  "output": "# Inefficiency: `gather_mm_offsets` recomputed identically for gate, up and down on every prefill call

- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
- **Status:** open
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:23:43Z
- **Next:** verifier to confirm launch counts and redundancy

## Slot

`experts`

## What happens

Every `gather_qmm_rhs` call builds its row-tile schedule from
scratch: `offsets = gather_mm_offsets(indices, E, M=B, ...)`
([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1795](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1795)),
one extra kernel launch per call that counts the sorted
`rhs_indices` into per-expert start rows
(host launch at
[matmul.cpp v0.32.4:2247-2265](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp#L2247-L2265):
`offsets` is `int32[60]`, dispatched as 60 threads in one
threadgroup). The offsets depend only on the sorted index
array and `E = 60`.

Within one MoE layer the three products (gate, up, down) are
called with the *same* sorted `idx`
(`bench/grader/slots.py:67-79`, `switch_layers.py:188-194`:
one `_gather_sort`, three `gather_qmm` calls sharing `idx`),
so the same 240-byte result is computed three times per
layer, plus a 240-byte allocation each time
(`offsets.set_data(allocator::malloc(...))`, matmul.cpp
host function). Nothing caches it: the primitive has no
cross-call state, and each `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` invocation
starts fresh (`quantized.cpp:1980-2094`).

## Cost

Decode 1/8/32 rows: **0 kernels** — the `qvm` path builds no
offsets (territory §A). Prefill, per 20-layer forward (one
prefill chunk at 127/1,016/2,048 rows; chunking in
`bench/grader/slots.py:242`):

- offsets kernels launched: 3 products × 20 layers = **60**,
  of which **40 are bit-identical recomputations** (only 20
  distinct results exist, one per layer).
- bytes: 60 × 240 B written = 14.4 KB total; the kernel reads
  the `B`-element sorted index array to count it
  (508 / 4,064 / 8,192 × 4 B = 2.0 / 16.3 / 32.8 KB read per
  call, 60 calls per forward). Byte time at 200 GB/s peak
  (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:10`) is < 0.2 µs per call — negligible;
  the cost is the fixed launch of a 60-thread kernel.
- fixed cost: no per-launch µs is measured for this kernel.
  Bounding with the decode step's small-kernel scale —
  routed experts 140 kernels / 0.92 ms ≈ 6.6 µs average
  including full `qvm` products (`claude/findings/step-breakdown.md:179-185`
  via round 1 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §A) — 40
  redundant launches cost **at most ≈0.26 ms per prefill
  forward** (40 × 6.6 µs), and less when launches pipeline
  behind the main kernels; MLX's own `// TODO: Tune 16 and 4`
  (`quantized.cpp:2011`) flags this dispatch as untuned.
  At 127 rows the main kernels are smallest, so the fixed
  part is largest *relative* there; at 2,048 rows it is
  noise against ≈929 µs of useful MMA per layer-product
  (territory §E).

Kernels × fixed cost is the whole cost; there is no
bandwidth or compute component worth modelling.

## Kind

Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): a 60-element counting
kernel whose runtime is its launch, repeated identically.
Far below both bandwidth and compute limits.

## Spans

`quantized-kernels` (`gather_qmm_rhs` host wrapper +
`gather_mm_offsets`) → slot `experts`. The three-call
structure that makes it redundant lives in switch-layers
(`SwitchGLU.__call__`), but the recomputation is inside
this territory's host function.

## Predicted saving

0 µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows (path never runs).
At prefill: at most ≈0.26 ms per 20-layer chunk forward
(40 redundant launches × ≤6.6 µs, upper bound above;
pipelined reality smaller), in time-to-first-token only —
prefill speed is not gated (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`).
For a candidate kernel this entry costs nothing to avoid:
a fused experts kernel computes its own grouping (or none,
territory §C invariant) and never needs MLX's offsets at
all. Recorded so the reference's prefill overhead is fully
accounted; not worth a fix on its own.

145|- **Callers:** §B only. Instantiated for this model as
146|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs<bfloat16, group_size=32, bits=4, BM=16,
147|  BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2, transpose=false>`

149|- **Callees:** `schedule_row_tile<BM=16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) maps
150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive
159|  `BlockMMA::mma` over `K_it = K/BK` tiles (24 gate/up, 12 down),

163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =
164|  40`, `quantized.h:2596-2597, 2623-2624`; padding is the usual
165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows
170|  `y_row .. y_row+tgp_bm-1` of the already-gathered `[B, K]` matrix;
171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).
175|- **Neighbours:** consumes the sorter's output order directly; this
176|  is the only gather kernel whose addressing depends on pair order
177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,
179|  so `_scatter_unsort` after the down product is load-bearing for
180|  position, not for bits.
181|- **Cost (arithmetic):** balanced-expert model (counts near the
182|  uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are random tokens, so this is
183|  the expected case, not a bound): useful row tiles
184|  `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` ≈ 60 / 300 / 540 at B = 508 / 4,064 /
185|  8,192, against dispatched `grid_y` 91 / 313 / 571 (§B). Weight
186|  bytes read per product per layer = `T × 184,320 B` (per-expert
187|  147,456 B weights + 36,864 B scales/biases; §F) = 11.06 / 55.30 /
188|  99.53 MB, i.e. 1× / 5× / 9× the 11.06 MB distinct-expert floor —
189|  each extra row tile of an expert re-reads and re-dequantizes its
190|  full weights. The per-pair `qvm` path at the same `B` would read
191|  `B × 184,320 B` = 93.6 MB / 749 MB / 1.51 GB per product, so `rhs`
192|  is 8.5× / 13.5× / 15.2× leaner on weight traffic — grouping works;
193|  its waste is the tile quantization in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`,
194|  not the grouping idea.
195|- **Invariants:** correctness rests on sorted `rhs_indices` +
196|  exact `offsets`; an unsorted input silently computes tiles from
197|  mixed experts (dispatch trusts `right_sorted_`, §A). `BM=16`
198|  grouping changes only which rows share a weight-tile load — never
199|  a valid row's arithmetic (§E) — so a bit-exact replacement may
200|  regroup rows freely, including not grouping at all, as long as
201|  each row's own accumulation matches §D+§E.
