*(to be written by boundary-1)*","replace":"## Boundary

(written by boundary-1; delta only — every line carries its source)

**Cited boundary, checked line by line.** Round 1's boundary for this slot is
[`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md`](../../implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md)
*Boundary* (inputs/outputs table, neighbours A/B, identical-math, grader,
GPU limits). I checked each line against the starting point
`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4` (`block-0.metal`, `block-1.metal`,
`spec.json`) and against the current G2
(`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:179,182-188`; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:22-29`;
`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:90-99,153-169,172-175,272-308`).
Still holding, not rewritten below: input/output names, dtypes, layouts and
weight shapes/bytes; `y[r,j]` positional in `inds` order; neighbour
contracts; the four bfloat16 rounding points in kind; launch-spec surface;
GPU limits. Baseline is `none` — no earlier attempt passes the current G2
(this entry, *Inefficiency*; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:38`).
Only what changed follows.

### Inputs and outputs — changed: prefill row counts added

Unchanged shapes now also run at prefill sizes. `rows` is still read from
the first slot input's `shape[0]` (`bench/grader/slots.py:323`); the grader
adds prefill `127 / 1,016 / 2,048` rows (1/8/32 requests × 128-token
prompts, first chunk; `bench/grader/slots.py:211,214-220,240-254`;
`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:272-276`):

| Name | Shape at 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows | Dtype |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | [127,768] / [1016,768] / [2048,768] | bfloat16 (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:74`) |
| `inds` | [127,4] / [1016,4] / [2048,4] | uint32 (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:75`) |
| `gate_w`, `up_w`, `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases`, `down_w`, `down_scales`, `down_biases` | rows-independent, as round 1 | as round 1 (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:76-79`; `bench/grader/slots.py:33-36`) |
| `y` (output) | [127,4,768] / [1016,4,768] / [2048,4,768] | bfloat16 (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:80`) |

Pairs `rows*4` are therefore 508 / 4,064 / 8,192 at prefill (arithmetic
from `rows` above), against 4 / 32 / 128 at decode 1/8/32 rows (round-1
boundary). A decode step can still have any 1–32 rows and a prefill chunk
other sizes again (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:24`); the kernel must be
valid at every `rows`, not only the six tested ones (see *can't see*).

### Before and after — changed: same neighbours, now also in prefill

Neighbour code is unchanged: post-attention layernorm → `x`; router →
`inds`, `weights`; `experts(x, inds)` → `y`; `shared_expert(x)` independent;
combine pairs `y[r,j]` with `weights[r,j]` positionally → residual
(`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`;
`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119,105-118`). What changed is the invocation
domain: the same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill first chunk, so the slot
is now called at the prefill row counts above with the same expectations —
`inds` any order, values in [0,60); `y` exact shape/dtype, positional
(`bench/grader/slots.py:217-218,231-254`;
`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:16`).

### What must stay identical — changed: bit-exact, with two arithmetics

- **Tolerance removed.** Round 1 allowed every element within 2 bfloat16
  ULP; now every element must equal the reference bit for bit
  (`differ == 0` in every layer at all six sizes;
  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:186-188`;
  `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:90-99,153-169,172-175,308`).
  `max_ulp` is diagnostic only (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`).
- **Summation order and dequantization are no longer free.** Round 1
  allowed any fp32 summation/dequantization order; that line is superseded.
  The reference itself changes kernel at `rows >= 60` — dispatch
  `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4` with `B = rows*4`, `E = 60`,
  i.e. `B >= 240` (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`
  §A; `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:22-32`).
  Sorting from `inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16 is a distinct, earlier
  threshold and does not switch the kernel: decode 32 rows is sorted and
  still `gather_qvm` (`bench/grader/slots.py:62`;
  `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:181`).

  | Rows | Reference kernel | Weight value | K accumulation |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | < 60 (all decode) | `gather_qvm` | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 through the product (`qouter`) | strided lanes `k≡lane (mod 32)` serial, then `simd_sum` tree |
  | ≥ 60 (all tested prefill) | `gather_qmm_rhs` | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup `Ws` before the multiply (`dequantize`: `static_cast<bfloat16>(s·q+b)`) | contiguous 8-wide frag dots, sequential over `BK=32` tiles (`BlockMMA`, `AccumType=float`) |

  Sources: `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`
  §D (dequant rounding), §E (MMA order), §F (side-by-side table);
  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md` §F.
  Either difference alone breaks bit-equality (down outputs near
  cancellation amplify a 1-ULP hidden flip, round-1 boundary builders'
  notes; measured 62.4–62.6% differ, max 43/65/110.5 ULP at prefill,
  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:62-71`).
  A size branch is therefore required — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic at/above — branched on `rows >= 60` from the
  dispatch source, not on the grader's bracketing sizes 32/127; rows
  33–59 in the real model still run `qvm`
  (`territory-quantized-kernels.md` §F conclusion). Row *grouping* inside
  the prefill branch is free (padded rows occupy separate accumulators
  and are discarded); per-row K order is not
  (`territory-quantized-kernels.md` §C invariant, §E invariant).
- **Unchanged in kind, now exact:** each gate/up/down product still
  accumulates in float32 and rounds once to bfloat16; `silu(gate)*up` is
  still computed on those bfloat16 values and rounded to bfloat16 before
  down (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`; `bench/grader/slots.py:67-79`).
  The compiled `swiglu` (full-bfloat16 per-op silu) is shared by both
  reference paths, so it is not the divergence
  (`ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:56-58`). At prefill the gate/up values
  arriving at `swiglu` already differ by the two rows above.
- **Tie rule and pair order — unchanged, restated because G2 is exact:**
  this slot makes no 4th/5th-expert tie choice; it inherits routing's
  output as given and must accept any 4 valid ids per row in any order,
  including either side of a near-tie. The order of the 4 pairs is not
  free: `y[r,j]` must stay the output of expert `inds[r,j]`, because
  combine sums `y[...,j,:] * weights[...,j]` positionally
  (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52,116`;
  `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:230-232`). Routing's own
  ordered tie-exactness is the `routing` slot's contract
  (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:187`), not this slot's.
- **Starting point against this boundary:** attempt-4 replicates only
  `gather_qvm` — strided-lane `qvm_block` + `simd_sum`, float32 dequant
  `x·(s·q+bias)` (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/block-1.metal:20-40`),
  full-bfloat16 silu (`block-0.metal:53-64`), one kernel with grid
  `rows*4` groups at every row count (`spec.json`; `block-0.metal:6`).
  Decode 1/8/32 therefore passes bit-exact and every prefill size fails
  (`ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:62-71`); closing that gap without losing
  the decode bits is this hypothesis's correctness work.

### What the grader checks, and what it can't see — changed

Checks (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): G1 is true only after the
whole six-size correctness loop completes without exception (`:306`);
per-layer shape/dtype faults fail G2 with G1 true (`:158-159,288-304`).
G2 for `experts` requires exact shape/dtype and `differ == 0` in all 20
layers at decode 1/8/32 and prefill 127/1,016/2,048 (`:153-169,272-308`).
Piece timing runs only if G2 passes, only at decode 1/8/32, now chained
through the `link` kernel so each layer waits for the previous one
(`:178-213,309-337`); `beats_compiled` needs chained candidate <
compiled at all three decode sizes (`:334-335`). Prefill speed is not
timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first
token (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`). No `--baseline` bar
exists this round (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md` §5).
What it still can't see (checked by hand later — *check an attempt*):
row counts between the six tested ones (2–7, 9–31, 33–126, 128–1,015,
1,017–2,047, >2,048), with both thresholds (sort 16, kernel switch 60)
only bracketed by tested sizes; prefill beyond the first chunk of seeded
128-token random prompts (later chunks, other lengths/distributions);
reads of unwritten threadgroup memory, thread-timing dependence, and
the 32 KB limit below; NaN-vs-NaN counts as equal (`:93`)
(`territory-grader.md`, *What the grader still cannot see* 1–6).

### The GPU limits — unchanged

At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup (count enforced,
`bench/grader/slots.py:327-328`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:98`) and
32 KB of threadgroup memory (not enforced by `build` — verify by hand
from the Metal source; `territory-grader.md` §3). Starting point for
scale: 256 threads/group and 3,840 B threadgroup memory
(`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/spec.json`;
`block-0.metal:13-16`), valid at every row count including 8,192
threadgroups at 2,048 rows
(`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md` §C).
Any prefill branch must stay inside both limits at all six sizes."}

1|"""The parts of MobileMoE-S's MoE block that a Muse Spark kernel may replace.
2|
3|Each slot has a reference (the port's own code, split as in breakdown.py),
4|named inputs and outputs (claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and a way to install
5|an implementation into MoE.__call__ for every layer. build() turns a launch
6|spec (data, never code) into mx.fast.metal_kernel calls.
7|
8|Record the grader's inputs from a real decode step (plain MLX, no API):
9|
10|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/slots.py capture
11|"""

13|import re
14|from pathlib import Path

16|import mlx.core as mx
17|import numpy as np
18|
19|D, E, K, H = 768, 60, 4, 384
20|SCALE = 2.5  # routed_scaling_factor; norm_topk_prob is true
21|NAMES = {"D": D, "E": E, "K": K, "H": H}
22|DTYPES = {
23|    "float32": mx.float32,
24|    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
25|    "float16": mx.float16,
26|    "uint32": mx.uint32,
27|    "int32": mx.int32,
28|}
29|SLOTS = {
30|    "routing": (["x", "w_router", "bias"], ["inds", "weights"]),
31|    "combine": (["y", "weights", "shared"], ["out"]),
32|}
33|EXPERT_WEIGHTS = [
34|    f"{p}_{t}" for p in ("gate", "up", "down") for t in ("w", "scales", "biases")
35|]
36|SLOTS["experts"] = (["x", "inds"] + EXPERT_WEIGHTS, ["y"])
37|SLOTS["routing+combine"] = (
38|    SLOTS["routing"][0] + ["y", "shared"],
39|    ["inds", "weights", "out"],

41|INPUTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "models" / "muse-inputs"

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE
49|
50|
51|def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
53|
54|
55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)
83|
84|
85|REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}

88|def expert_weights(experts):
89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
94|    }

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
103|    """
104|
105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
110|        if experts is None:
111|            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
112|        else:
113|            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
114|            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
115|        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
117|        return out.reshape(*lead, D)
118|
119|    return moe_call

122|def check_identity(model):
123|    """The split MoE with reference slots equals the port's, at 1, 8, 32 rows."""
124|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe

131|            if not mx.array_equal(original(moe, x), split(moe, x)).item():
132|                raise AssertionError(
133|                    f"split MoE differs from the port's at {rows} rows"
134|                )

138|    """Every layer's slot inputs and reference outputs in one real decode step."""
139|    import sys

146|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__

149|    def recording_routing(x, w_router, bias):
150|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)

214|def capture_prefill(model, requests, with_weights=None):
215|    """Every layer's slot inputs in the first chunk of a prefill, as load_inputs.
216|
217|    The same MoE.__call__ runs the prefill. With 128-token prompts and
218|    breakdown.py's 2,048-token chunks, 1, 8 and 32 requests give the slots
219|    127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes
220|    (gather_qmm_rhs). The prompts are time_candidates.py's.
221|    """
222|    import sys
223|
224|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
225|    import breakdown as bd
226|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
227|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache

229|    seen = []
230|
231|    def routing(x, w_router, bias):
232|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
233|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})

236|    def combine(y, weights, shared):
237|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights=weights, shared=shared)

240|    mx.random.seed(requests)

249|    for i, layer in enumerate(seen):

257|def load_inputs(rows, with_weights=None):
258|    """[{name: mx.array}] per layer, with bfloat16 restored where the model had it.
259|
260|    *with_weights*, from load_expert_weights or model_expert_weights, adds each layer's expert weights.
261|    """
262|    data = np.load(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz")
263|    bf16 = {"x", "y", "shared"}
264|    layers = {}
265|    for key in data.files:
266|        i, name = int(key[1:3]), key[4:]
267|        a = mx.array(data[key])
268|        layers.setdefault(i, {})[name] = a.astype(mx.bfloat16) if name in bf16 else a
269|    for i, layer in layers.items():
270|        layer["weights"] = layer.pop("weights_in")
271|        if "inds" in layer:
272|            layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
273|        if with_weights is not None:
274|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
275|    return [layers[i] for i in sorted(layers)]

278|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
279|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")
280|
281|
282|def dim(expr, rows):
283|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
284|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
285|    if isinstance(expr, int):
286|        return expr
287|    value = 1
288|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
289|        if not TERM.match(term):
290|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
291|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
292|    return value
293|
294|
295|def template_value(v):
296|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
297|        return v
298|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
299|        return DTYPES[v]
300|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")
301|
302|
303|def build(spec, sources, slot):
304|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
305|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
306|    kernels = []
307|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
308|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
309|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
310|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
311|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
312|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
313|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
314|            header=header,
315|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
316|        )
317|        kernels.append((k, fn))
318|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
319|    if missing:
320|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
321|
322|    def run(**inputs):
323|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
324|        env = dict(inputs)
325|        for k, fn in kernels:
326|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
327|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
328|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
329|            outs = fn(
330|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
331|                template=[
332|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
333|                ],
334|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
335|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
336|                output_shapes=[
337|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
338|                ],
339|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
340|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
341|            )
342|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
343|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
344|
345|    return run
346|

348|def main():
349|    import sys
350|
351|    if sys.argv[1:] != ["capture"]:
352|        raise SystemExit("usage: slots.py capture")
353|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))

361|    mx.eval(model.parameters())
362|    check_identity(model)
363|    print("split MoE with reference slots: bit-identical to the port's")
364|    save_inputs(model)
365|

367|if __name__ == "__main__":
368|    main()

66|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs, use_rope: bool):

77|        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
78|        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(self.n_heads * self.head_dim, dim, bias=bias)

# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write a faster MobileMoE-S decode kernel

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

## The task

Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.

1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.

**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.

## The slots

Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.

The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.

### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights

| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |

Reference:

```python
scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
```

The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.

### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert

| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |

Reference:

```python
out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
```

Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.

### `routing+combine`

Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.

### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products

| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |

Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.

Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:

```python
y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
```

As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.

Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.

## How each attempt is judged

The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only.

1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.

   At every size:
   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.

   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.

**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.

**The piece timing** runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and waits for the GPU once at the end. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.

**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and beats the compiled reference in the piece timing at all three row counts, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

84|def ulp_bf16(r):
85|    """bfloat16's unit in the last place at |r|, floored at |r| = 0.001 (brief, G2)."""
86|    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))
87|    return 2.0 ** (exp - 7)

90|def differences(g, r):
91|    """Elements of *g* that aren't *r*'s bit for bit, and the largest gap in units
92|    in the last place (floored at |r| = 0.001); "at" is the flat index of it."""
93|    differ = (g != r) & ~(np.isnan(g) & np.isnan(r))
94|    out = {"differ": int(differ.sum()), "max_ulp": 0.0}
95|    if out["differ"]:
96|        with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
97|            over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
98|        out |= {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "at": int(over.argmax())}
99|    return out

104|    got = fn(x=layer["x"], w_router=layer["w_router"], bias=layer["bias"])

113|            "error": f"dtypes inds {inds.dtype}, weights {w.dtype}; want uint32, float32"

184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs

204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:
221|            call()
222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
228|    return times

9|## What it does
10|
11|In every decode step and every prefill chunk, each of the 20 layers runs
12|`MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`): cast the
13|layer input to float32, multiply by the router weight transposed, sigmoid, add the
14|expert bias only for selection, take the top-4 experts per row, gather their
15|*unbiased* scores, normalise them (divide by their sum + 1e-20) and scale by 2.5.
16|The slot outputs `inds` [rows,4] uint32 and `weights` [rows,4] float32; `inds`
17|feeds the experts slot, `weights` feeds combine, which sums the 4 (expert,
18|weight) pairs *in the emitted order* — which is why round 2's G2 requires the
19|same experts, the same weights and the same order, bit for bit
20|(`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:25-27`,
21|`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:119-121`).
22|
23|The starting point is round 1's `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1`: one fused
24|Metal kernel per layer (`block-0.metal`, 78 lines; `spec.json`: one kernel
25|`fused_routing`, grid `rows*32`, threadgroup 32). One threadgroup per row stages
26|`x[row]` (768 bfloat16→float32) in threadgroup memory, each of the 32 threads
27|computes 1–2 experts' 768-term dot products serially, writes
28|`sigmoid(acc)` to `scores[60]`, and thread 0 alone does a serial insertion
29|top-4 scan over the biased scores and writes `inds`/`weights`
30|(`block-0.metal:10-78`).
31|
32|## The headline finding (details in ineff-baseline-routing-1 and -2)
33|
34|Under the new grader the starting point fails G2 at **every** size while the
35|experts and their order always match (`rows_other_experts` 0 everywhere):
36|rows differing 20/159/638 at decode 1/8/32 rows (of 20/160/640 rows summed over
37|20 layers — 100% / 99.4% / 99.7% of rows) and 2,518/16,187/32,743 at prefill
38|127/1,016/2,048 rows (of 2,540/20,320/40,960 — 99.1% / 79.7% / 79.9%), max
39|relative error 2.6e-06 at decode and up to 8.7e-06 in the prefill
40|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`, quoted in
41|`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/README.md:39`). The experts match because
42|selection is insensitive to last-bit score differences (no captured row is a
43|near-tie at the 4th/5th place); the weights expose every last-bit difference
44|in the 4 selected scores. Section 3 below pins down, op by op, which of the
45|reference's operations the kernel reproduces exactly and which it does not:
46|**the divergence is in the scores — the router matmul's float32 accumulation
47|order (which changes with `rows`) and MLX's sigmoid formula — not in the
48|4-term weight sum, whose order the kernel already matches.**

151|### 3. Op-by-op: where the kernel's arithmetic matches the reference's, and where it does not
152|
153|#### 3.1 The router product `x.astype(f32) @ w_router.T` — DOES NOT MATCH (main cause)
154|
155|The kernel accumulates each expert's dot product **serially, in one thread,
156|in increasing `d` order**: `acc += xsh[d] * w_router[wbase + d]` for
157|`d = 0..767` (`block-0.metal:31-34`; the Metal compiler may contract each
158|mul+add to an FMA, but the grouping stays a 768-long left-to-right chain).
159|
160|The reference never does that. `Matmul::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4,
161|`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, fetched 2026-11-04) sees A = `x` [rows,768]
162|f32 (not transposed), B = `w_router.T` [768,60] (transposed view), so
163|`transpose_a=false, transpose_b=true`, M=rows, N=60, K=768:
164|
165|- **rows = 1 → GEMV.** `min(M,N)==1` routes to `gemv`
166|  (matmul.cpp, `Matmul::eval_gpu`); the `gemv_wide` shortcut is skipped
167|  because the output is float32 (`gemv_wide_config` requires float16/bfloat16
168|  out). Dispatch picks `GEMVKernel<float, BM=4, BN=1, SM=1, SN=32, TM=4,
169|  TN=4>`: each output is accumulated by one simdgroup whose 32 lanes each
170|  serially sum 24 products — lane `l` takes `d = i*128 + l*4 + (0..3)` for
171|  `i = 0..5` (`kernels/gemv.h:162-182`) — and the 32 partials are then combined
172|  by a shuffle tree, `result += simd_shuffle_down(result, sn)` for
173|  sn = 16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`). Grouping: 32 blocked partials + pairwise
174|  tree, not a serial chain.
175|- **rows = 8, 32, 127 → steel split-K GEMM.** In `steel_matmul_axpby` the
176|  split-K case fires when `_tm*_tn <= 2048` (this device's architecture string
177|  ends in `s`; brief:99 names it `applegpu_g13s`), `_tk = 768/16 = 48 >= 8`
178|  and `K >= max(M,N)` (matmul.cpp, Case 1). `steel_gemm_splitk_axpby` uses
179|  BM=16 (M<40) or 32, BN=32, BK=16, WM=WN=2 (steel/gemm split-K dispatch):
180|  partitions = min(max(2, next_pow2(48/(_tm*_tn))), 32) with
181|  `_tm=(M+31)/32, _tn=2` → **32 partitions at rows 8 and 32** (the last
182|  partition also absorbs the remaining 16 BK-iterations,
183|  `steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_splitk.h:140-155`), **8 partitions at rows
184|  127**. Each partition accumulates its K-slice with simdgroup 8×8 matrix
185|  multiply-accumulate over BK=16 chunks in order (GEMMKernel/mma in
186|  `steel/gemm/gemm.h`, `mma.h`), writes a float32 partial, and
187|  `gemm_splitk_accum` sums the partials sequentially in partition order
188|  (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`).
189|- **rows = 1,016, 2,048 → regular steel GEMM.** Split-K no longer fires
190|  (768 < M), so `steel_matmul_regular_axpby` runs with the device tile from
191|  `GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` (for an architecture ending in `s` the macro's fallback:
192|  BM=64, BN=64, BK=16, WM=2, WN=2): K is walked in BK=16 chunks staged through
193|  threadgroup memory, accumulated by simdgroup matrix ops chunk after chunk.
194|
195|So the reference has **three different float32 accumulation orders for the
196|same mathematical product, selected by `rows`** — and none of them is the
197|kernel's serial order. Every score therefore differs from the reference's in
198|the last bits with high probability, which is exactly the observed pattern:
199|~100% of decode rows and ~80–99% of prefill rows have at least one differing
200|weight, while no row picks different experts (the biased-score gaps at the
201|4th/5th place are far larger than 1-ULP score noise on these inputs).
202|The drop from ~100% (decode, GEMV/split-K regimes) to ~80% (1,016/2,048,
203|regular GEMM) is consistent with a per-regime last-bit flip rate; that last
204|step is an inference from the counts, not a measurement.
205|A scalar re-implementation cannot reproduce the steel regimes' rounding by
206|reordering a serial loop: within each 8×8 simdgroup matrix op the 8-product
207|accumulation is the hardware's. A bit-exact candidate must either reuse
208|`simdgroup_float8x8` multiply-accumulate with the same tiling/K-order per
209|regime (branching on `rows` inside the kernel, or one kernel per regime in
210|the spec), or find an accumulation that provably rounds identically — none
211|is known.
212|
213|#### 3.2 The sigmoid — DOES NOT MATCH (independent second cause)
214|
215|Kernel (`block-0.metal:35`): `1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))` — the fast
216|(non-`precise`) `exp`, applied to `-acc`, one division.
217|
218|Reference (`mx.sigmoid` → `Sigmoid` in
219|`mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`, installed headers):
220|
221|```metal
222|auto y = 1 / (1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(x)));
223|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;
224|```
225|
226|Three differences, each able to move the result by 1 ULP: (a) `precise::exp`
227|vs `metal::exp`; (b) the argument is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0`
228|the result is `1 - y` (a subtraction that rounds) instead of the direct
229|division the kernel computes for all signs. Even a kernel whose matmul
230|matched bit for bit would still fail G2 on sigmoid alone for a large share
231|of scores. The fix is free in time: copy this formula verbatim.
232|
233|#### 3.3 Selection, gather, and the weight normalisation — MATCH
234|
235|- `scores + bias`: one f32 add in both (`block-0.metal:45`;
236|  `binary_ops.h:10-15`).
237|- Selection: the kernel's strictly-greater insertion scan emits descending
238|  biased order, earliest index winning ties (`block-0.metal:44-61`). The
239|  reference's argpartition is a full sort of `-(scores+bias)`
240|  (round-1 note, `ineff-runs-2.md:94-98`); on all six graded sizes the emitted
241|  sets *and* order agree (`rows_other_experts` 0, and the grader's worst-row
242|  examples show identical expert lists, grade-exact-routing.json). This is
243|  the part of Claude's round-1 reading ("the reference's order of
244|  operations … differ", round-2 README:39) that does **not** need fixing —
245|  but a builder must preserve the exact tie behaviour, since G2 now also
246|  compares order (`check_candidate.py:120`).
247|- The 4-term sum: the reference's `w.sum(axis=-1)` on a [rows,4] f32 array
248|  takes `row_reduce_small` (row_size 4 <= 64, MLX v0.32.4
249|  `mlx/backend/metal/reduce.cpp`, `row_reduce_general_dispatch` Case 1) in its
250|  per-thread branch (`non_row_reductions=1 < 32 && row_size <= 8`,
251|  `row_reduce_small` dispatch), i.e. `thread_reduce` with `N_READS=4`
252|  (`defines.h:12`): `total = (((0 + w0) + w1) + w2) + w3` in memory order —
253|  and `w`'s memory order is the `inds` order from argpartition, the same
254|  sequence the kernel sums as `s0 + s1 + s2 + s3` (`block-0.metal:64-68`;
255|  `kernels/reduction/reduce_row.h:164-181`). The kernel then adds `1e-20f`
256|  inside the same expression (`denom = s0+s1+s2+s3 + 1e-20f`), the reference
257|  as a separate add after the reduction (`slots.py:48`) — same association,
258|  and in float32 `sum + 1e-20` equals `sum` for any sum above ~1e-27, so the
259|  epsilon cannot be the cause either. Division and ×2.5 are the same single
260|  ops (`binary_ops.h:43-48,208-213`; `block-0.metal:74-77`).
261|  **Conclusion:** once the 4 selected scores are bit-equal and in the same
262|  order, the weights are bit-equal. Builders should spend their effort on
263|  3.1 and 3.2, not on the normalisation — the opposite emphasis to round 2
264|  README:39's example list, which names "the float32 sum order of
265|  `x @ w_router.T` and of `w.sum(...)`" as co-equal suspects.

13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:31-34`)
16|computes each of the 60 router scores as one thread's serial float32 chain,
17|`acc += xsh[d] * w_router[e*768 + d]` for d = 0..767 (compiler FMA contraction
18|does not change the left-to-right grouping). The reference,
19|`mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`),
20|never accumulates that way. In MLX 0.32.4's `Matmul::eval_gpu`
21|(`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, tag v0.32.4) with M=rows, N=60, K=768,
22|A not transposed, B transposed, the accumulation order is chosen by `rows`:
23|
24|| rows | MLX kernel | float32 accumulation order |
25||---|---|---|
26|| 1 | GEMV `gemv_float32_bm4_bn1_sm1_sn32_tm4_tn4` (`min(M,N)==1` → `gemv`; `gemv_wide` skipped, f32 out) | 32 lanes × serial 24 products (lane l: d = i*128 + l*4 + 0..3, i=0..5, `kernels/gemv.h:162-182`), then shuffle tree sn=16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`) |
27|| 8, 32, 127 | steel split-K GEMM (Case 1: `_tm*_tn <= 2048` on this `…s` device, `_tk=48 >= 8`, `K >= max(M,N)`) | 32 K-partitions (8/32 rows) or 8 (127 rows); each partition: simdgroup 8×8 MMA over BK=16 chunks (BM=16/32, BN=32); partials summed sequentially in partition order (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`); last partition absorbs the remainder iterations (`splitk.h:140-155`) |
28|| 1,016, 2,048 | regular steel GEMM (split-K off: 768 < M) | BM=64/BN=64/BK=16 tiles (`GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` fallback for `…s`), K walked in BK=16 chunks, simdgroup MMA accumulation chunk after chunk |
29|
30|A serial scalar loop cannot reproduce the two MMA regimes' rounding by
31|reordering: the 8-product accumulation inside each `simdgroup_float8x8`
32|multiply-accumulate is the hardware's. Bit-exactness therefore needs either
33|the same simdgroup matrix ops with the same tiling and K-order per regime
34|(branch on `rows`, or separate spec kernels), or a proof that another order
35|rounds identically (none known). Full derivation:
36|`territory-baseline-routing.md` section 3.1.

17|(non-`precise`) Metal `exp` of `-acc`, then one division, for all signs.
18|The reference's `mx.sigmoid` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`) is MLX's unary

30|`1 - y` rather than a direct division. With 60 scores per row and 4 selected,
31|even a bit-exact matmul behind this sigmoid would still leave most rows
32|differing — this cause is independent of `ineff-baseline-routing-1`, and

17|threadgroup 32; `block-0.metal:10-11`). At 1 row that is a single simdgroup
18|on a 16-core GPU. Inside the group, threads 0-27 compute two experts and
19|threads 28-31 one (`block-0.metal:25-36`); then, after the second barrier,

28|`attempt-2/notes.md`), and 8 rows ran *faster* than 1 row (23.6 vs 28.5
29|µs/layer) — the signature of fixed cost amortising over threadgroups, i.e.
30|of the 1-row case having too little parallel work per launch.

5|# From round 2, a kernel must be bit-exact at every size it runs at, prefill included, and the piece timing chains the layers
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's measurement of round 1 ([findings](../findings/muse-round-1.md)) found that round 1's final attempts, which passed the grader, broke the brief's end-to-end rule in the model, and that one of them slowed the decode step it was meant to speed up. The grader missed three things:
10|
11|1. **Sizes.** It tested a slot on a decode step's inputs only, at 1, 8 and 32 rows. The same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill, at 127 to 2,048 rows with 128-token prompts. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes, from `gather_qvm` to `gather_qmm_rhs`, and so does its rounding. Round 1's experts kernel copied `gather_qvm` bit for bit, and differed in 62% of its outputs at each prefill size.
12|2. **Exactness.** G2 allowed small differences: 2 bfloat16 units in the last place, and 10⁻⁴ for routing weights. End to end, the brief asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. Round 1's routing weights, within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences in 24 tokens.
13|3. **Latency.** The piece timing ran 20 layers' calls with no data between them, so the GPU could overlap them. At 1 row, round 1's experts kernel was 29% faster than the reference on overlapped calls and 66% slower on chained ones (`bench/micro/chain_timing.py`). In the model it slowed the decode step by 1.2 ms (22% in vLLM, 25% in plain MLX).
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose, before round 2:
16|- **every call:** the kernels run wherever `MoE.__call__` runs, the prefill included;
17|- **bit-exact** outputs;
18|- **chained** piece timing.
19|
20|## How it works
21|
22|- **G2 at two kinds of size.** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` checks every layer at:
23|  - the captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
24|  - the first prefill chunk at 1, 8 and 32 requests (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows), recorded while it runs (`slots.capture_prefill`), with the prompts `time_candidates.py` uses.
25|- **Bit-exact.** An output passes only if it equals the reference's:
26|  - for routing, the 4 experts and their weights, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order;
27|  - for combine and experts, every element.
28|
29|  The grader still reports the largest gap, in units in the last place, to help find the cause. The reference checked against itself shows no difference at any size.
30|- **Chained timing.** Each layer's call takes one input through `link`, a single fused kernel that adds 0 × one value of the previous call's output, so the call can't start before the previous one finishes. Every function timed (reference, compiled, candidate and baseline) gets the same link. The chained times match those of a real data chain within 10%.
31|  - **Why not `mx.depends`:** it orders only the graph. In a test on 2026-11-04, round 1's experts kernel took 46 µs per layer with it at 1 row, as fast as with no dependency, against 133 to 195 µs with a real data dependency in three runs.
32|- **The end-to-end check and G3 are unchanged.**
33|  - `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` now takes several `SLOT=FOLDER` attempts.
34|  - It times each slot alone, against its own compiled reference, and all of them together.
35|
36|## Consequences
37|
38|- **No round-1 attempt passes the new G2,** so round 2 has no baseline in any slot. Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's final attempts are its starting points, named in Claude's findings.
39|- **The experts slot needs a kernel exact at prefill sizes,** matching `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding from 60 rows on, or a single design whose rounding matches both of MLX's kernels.
40|- **A grader run takes longer.** It loads the model (760 MB) for every slot and runs three prefill chunks.
41|- **The piece timing now includes one small link kernel per layer** for every function timed. That brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs.
42|- **Not covered:** prefill speed. G3 times decode steps only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token.
43|
44|## Considered options
45|
46|- **Decode calls only,** with MLX's code in the prefill. The kernels would need to be exact only at decode sizes, but they would no longer replace the whole MoE block. Not chosen: surucuonur asked for every call.
47|- **Keep the tolerances, and relax the token rule** to counting the sequences that differ. Simpler kernels, but the claim would become "the same model up to rounding", with a threshold to pick.

# Rounds build on each other: each in its own folder, finished rounds frozen, the best attempt so far is the bar

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*

**The change.** On 2026-11-03, before round 2, surucuonur asked that round 1's files stay the same, and that round 2 "can see the round 1 and its results" and "do different plan considering that". Under the round skill's version 3, round 2 would have done neither:
- it would have continued round 1's documents in place, with `## Round 2` sections in its entries, and its README versions, logs and summary carried on;
- it would have judged attempts only against the original MLX code and its compiled version, a bar round 1 already passed.

Skill version 4 ([.agents/skills/muse-round/](../../.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md)) changes both.

## How it works

- **A folder per round.** Round 1 stays at the top of `muse-spark/`. Round N writes in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`: `exploration/`, `implementation/`, `kernels/` and `summary.md`. Transcripts stay in `muse-spark/transcripts/`, one file per session.
- **Finished rounds are frozen.** Claude tags a round's last commit `muse-round-<N>` once its transcripts are committed. Round 1's tag is `muse-round-1`, on `60308aa`, and freezes its 71 files. From a tag on:
  - the pre-commit hook on `muse-agent` refuses any change to, or deletion of, a file the tag holds in `muse-spark/`. It also refuses a new file anywhere but the current round's folder and `muse-spark/transcripts/`;
  - the audit, `tools/provenance_check.py`, re-checks every commit after each tag, so a commit made around the hook is caught;
  - the transcript exporter skips sessions it has already exported, so running it again never rewrites a frozen transcript.
- **The starting point.** From round 2 on, the lead first writes a plan from:
  - the previous rounds' final documents;
  - the notes of each slot's best attempt;
  - Claude's report on the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`.

  The plan covers, per slot, the best attempt so far (the **baseline**) and its G3 effect against its prediction. It also covers what is left to build, and which territories to explore again. The round stops if Claude's report is missing.
- **Targeted exploration.** Explorers map:
  - the baselines' kernels, now the code in the slots;
  - where Claude's G3 differed from the piece timing;
  - only those round-1 territories the plan reopens.

  Earlier entries are cited, never rewritten.
- **The baseline is the bar.** Claude's report names each slot's baseline. A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run, with `bench/grader/check_candidate.py --baseline`.
  - **The test.** The two are timed in alternating repeats, so drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. The candidate must be faster in at least 22 of the 30 paired repeats at each row count: a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01.
  - **Why a sign test.** In a test on 2026-11-03, round 1's combine attempt, timed separately against itself, differed by up to 5% between medians. In paired repeats it won only 15 to 19 of 30 against itself. Round 1's final experts attempt won 30 of 30 against its first. Comparing medians would have passed on noise.
- **A slot that nothing beats keeps its baseline** for G3.

## Consequences

- Round 1's files can't change, and every path in round 1's documents stays valid.
- Attempt numbers restart in each round's folder, and each round's summary counts attempts per round and over all rounds.
- The lead reads more at the start of a round, and the explorers repeat less.
- The grader's verdict gains `baseline`, `beats_baseline`, `wins_needed` and, per row count, `wins_vs_baseline`. Without `--baseline` it is unchanged.
- Claude's G3 for round 2 compares round 2's attempts with round 1's.

## Considered options

- **Carry on in round 1's folders** with `## Round N` sections, as version 3 did. Round 1's files would change, and only git history would keep their round-1 state.
- **Freeze by the skill's word alone,** with no hook. A slip would change round 1's files, unnoticed until the next audit.
- **Compare against round 1's recorded timings.** Timings drift between runs: in round 1 the compiled reference varied by up to 2 times at 1 row. The comparison has to happen in one run.
- **Compare medians within one run.** The 5% noise measured above would let an equal kernel pass.

28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.

50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```

72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |

86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]

151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from

153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then

157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive

163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =

169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows

203|### D. Dequantization — `QuantizedBlockLoader` + `dequantize` (rounding point 1)
204|
205|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` with
206|  `QuantizedBlockLoader<T=bfloat16, BROWS=BK=32, BCOLS=BN=32,
207|  dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=0, tgp_size=64, group_size=32, bits=4>`
208|  (`quantized.h:2613-2621`); same loader family as `qmm_n`/`qmm_t`
209|  (§G).
210|- **Callees:** `load_unsafe`/`load_safe` (`quantized.h:736-770`) call
211|  `dequantize<T, pack_factor=2, bits=4>` (`quantized.h:557-663`,
212|  bits=4 at `:617-623`) per packed byte: with `s = float(scale)`,
213|  `b = float(bias)` it writes
214|  `w_local[2i] = (bfloat16)(s * (w[i] & 0x0f) + b)` and
215|  `w_local[2i+1] = (bfloat16)((s/16) * (w[i] & 0xf0) + b)` into
216|  threadgroup `Ws`. Scales: one `scale`/`bias` pair per thread from
217|  `scales + bi * N/32` (`:733-734`); `group_steps = 32/32 = 1`, so
218|  `next()` advances `scales/biases` by `32*N/32 = N` per K tile
219|  (`:772-790`) — exactly one scale group per `BN=32` output tile and
220|  per `BK=32` row of `K`, matching the `[E, K, N/32]` layout.
221|- **Data:** packed uint32 weights are viewed as bytes (`(device
222|  uint8_t*)w`); each byte yields 2 outputs (low/high nibble), each
223|  `BK×BN = 1,024`-element weight tile dequantized once per
224|  (row tile, K tile) visit into `Ws`, then read by the MMA (§E).
225|  `x` tiles by contrast are copied verbatim (bfloat16 → bfloat16,
226|  exact) by `BlockLoader` (`steel/gemm/loader.h:74-80`).
227|- **Neighbours:** this is the first of the two divergence points
228|  vs `qvm` (§F): the dequantized weight is **rounded to bfloat16
229|  before any multiply**. In `qvm` the same `scale*q + bias` value
230|  stays in float32 registers through the product.
231|- **Cost:** dequant element-ops per product per layer =
232|  `T × K × N` = `T × 294,912` (both products have `K·N = 294,912`):
233|  17.7M / 88.5M / 159.2M at the three prefill sizes (balanced `T`
234|  from §C), each a float mul+add, a float→bfloat round, and a
235|  threadgroup store+reload. This recompute-per-row-tile is the
236|  loader's design (no dequantized-weight cache exists; the full
237|  dequantized expert is 294,912 × 2 B = 590 KB, far above the
238|  32 KB threadgroup limit, so cross-tile reuse would need a device
239|  buffer and an extra kernel — not a free fix).
240|- **Invariants:** `scale`/`bias` themselves are bfloat16 values
241|  upcast to float exactly (bfloat→float is exact), identical to
242|  `qvm`'s inputs; the *only* added rounding is
243|  `static_cast<bfloat16>(s*q + b)`. Relative error up to half a
244|  bfloat ULP (≈2⁻⁹ ≈ 0.2%) per weight element, deterministic per
245|  `(expert, k, n)` — the same rounded weight is reused for all
246|  ≤16 rows of the tile, so errors are correlated across rows
247|  sharing an expert, unlike per-pair float weights.

249|### E. Accumulation — `BlockLoader` + `BlockMMA` (rounding point 2)
250|
251|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` instantiates
252|  `BlockMMA<bfloat16, bfloat16, BM=16, BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2,
253|  false, transpose=false, ...>` (`quantized.h:2599-2610`) and
254|  `BlockLoader<bfloat16, BM=16, BK=32, dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=1,
255|  tgp_size=64>` for `x` (`:2611-2612`).
256|- **Callees:** `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:439-537`) with
257|  `AccumType = float` by default (`mma.h:451`): accumulator
258|  fragments `Ctile` are `float` 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` tiles
259|  (`TM = 16/(8·1) = 2`, `TN = 32/(8·2) = 2` frags per simdgroup).
260|  `mma()` (`mma.h:513-537`) steps `kk` over `BK` in 8-wide frags
261|  (4 steps per tile), each `tile_matmad` issuing
262|  `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` (`mma.h:181-206, 406-427`).
263|  Operand fragments are loaded from threadgroup bfloat16 and
264|  widened to float (`BaseMMAFrag::load` casts, `mma.h:57-67`), so
265|  the multiply is float×float with float accumulate — but the
266|  weight operand is the already-bfloat-rounded value of §D, and
267|  the 8-term dot inside each frag is the hardware's tree order,
268|  not a serial FMA chain. `gemm_loop_*` then adds tile results
269|  sequentially over the 24/12 K tiles. Store:
270|  `store_result`/`store_result_safe` cast float → bfloat16 once

304|### F. Comparator — `qvm_impl` + `qouter` (what decode runs; delta only)
305|
306|Round 1 §A mapped this kernel fully; only the contrast is new.
307|
308|- **Callers/Callees:** `gather_qvm` host (`quantized.cpp:1462-1529`)
309|  → `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`) → `qvm_impl`
310|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid `(1, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of
311|  64 threads; gate/up `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. Each lane owns
312|  one strided `K` element per 32-step (`x += block_size` with
313|  `block_size = 32`, `:1275-1287`) and accumulates 32 outputs in
314|  float registers via `qouter` (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 at
315|  `:503-509`): `result += x * (scale*q + bias)` with
316|  `scale`/`bias`/`x` all float, **no bfloat16 rounding of the
317|  weight**, serial per-lane adds in strided-K order
318|  (`k = lane, lane+32, ...`), then one `simd_sum` tree over the 32
319|  lane partials (`:1317-1321`) and a single float→bfloat16 store
320|  (`:1324-1329`).
321|- **The two divergences, side by side:**
322|
323|  | aspect | `gather_qvm` (decode, rows < 60) | `gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill, rows ≥ 60) |
324|  |---|---|---|
325|  | weight value | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup (§D) |
326|  | K grouping | strided lanes: lane `l` sums `k≡l (mod 32)` serially, then `simd_sum` tree | contiguous: 8-wide frag dots, sequential over BK=32 tiles (§E) |
327|  | rows sharing work | none: one grid slice per pair | ≤16 sorted rows share each weight tile |
328|  | final rounding | float → bfloat16 once after `simd_sum` | float → bfloat16 once after MMA — identical point |
329|
330|  Either divergence alone breaks bit-equality (measured: 62.4–62.6%
331|  of experts outputs differ at all three prefill sizes, max
332|  43/65/110.5 ULP, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-experts.json`;
333|  full statement in `ineff-baseline-experts-1`). A single arithmetic
334|  cannot match both kernels on generic inputs: pick any weight with
335|  `float(scale·q+bias)` not representable in bfloat16 and any
336|  `x ≠ 0` — the two references already disagree on that product
337|  before accumulation even starts. **Conclusion for builders: a
338|  size branch is required** — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
339|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic (bfloat-rounded dequant tiles + 8-wide frag
340|  accumulation) at/above 60 rows — or a proof of coincidence that
341|  the 62% differ rate rules out empirically. The branch threshold
342|  must be the dispatch rule `rows >= 60` (pairs `>= 240`, `E=60`),
343|  not the grader's nearest tested sizes 32/127: rows 33–59 in the
344|  real model still run `qvm` (§A). Row *grouping* inside the
345|  prefill branch is free (§C invariant); per-row accumulation is
346|  not.

348|  (`muse-spark/exploration/ineff-quantized-kernels-1`, confirmed;
349|  round-2 restatement `ineff-baseline-experts-3`): 51 MB read in
350|  0.92 ms at 1 row (55 GB/s), 908 MB in 14.67 ms at 32 rows
351|  (62 GB/s, 31% of peak). Not re-posted here.

353|  bfloat16 exactly once per product; `silu(gate)·up` is computed on
354|  those bfloat16 values and rounded again before down (brief:
355|  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). Any candidate must keep all

357|  final `y` rounding is insufficient, since 1-ULP hidden flips
358|  amplify through down (round 1

13|## What happens

15|Attempt-4 launches one threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair:
16|grid `rows*1024` threads ÷ 256 = `rows*4` threadgroups
17|(`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/spec.json`;

19|is 4 threadgroups / 1,024 threads on a 16-core GPU

21|serialized by barriers into waves (`block-0.metal`): load `tg_x` +
22|barrier (`:18-21`); gate 12 blocks in 2 waves of 8 simdgroups (`:28-38`)
23|— wave 2 uses 4 of 8 simdgroups, 4 idle under the simd-uniform

25|strided loop (`:56-64`); barrier (`:65`); down 24 blocks in 3 waves of 8

27|their waves; 8 of 56 slots across all three products) to wave
28|quantization, and no phase overlaps another.

35|independent the GPU overlaps calls and hides one call's latency; when

# attempt-2: fused per-pair experts (direction b)

First in direction (b): fusion first, keeping per-pair reads. One Metal kernel,
one 128-thread threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair. Gate/up share one
i-loop over an on-chip x row; gate/up/hidden intermediates stay in threadgroup
memory (1920 bf16 = 3840 B, under the 32 KB limit); each expert's weights are
read once per pair with no cross-pair batching and no sort.

does NOT remove `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (per-pair re-reads of weights) or
`ineff-runs-1` (465 MB excess) — those are directions (a)/(c).

# Attempt 3: two-kernel grouped experts split (builder-1-c, direction c)

First in direction (c): kernel 1 fuses gate+up+silu-mul with grouped
same-expert reads; kernel 2 runs the down product with grouped reads. One
threadgroup per expert finds its pairs by scanning `inds`, streams each
weight tile once per chunk from DRAM, reuses it across the chunk. A `hidden`
[rows,4,384] bf16 buffer passes between the kernels in DRAM.

## What it removes, and how

- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`: per-pair qvm grids re-read each expert's
  weights once per pair (908 MB/step at 32 rows for 443 MB distinct). Here
  each appearing expert's weights stream ~once per call (34 MB/layer at 32
  rows vs 71 MB per-pair); tile loads are coalesced.
- `ineff-switch-layers-2`: gate/up/activation fused (one hidden round-trip);
  no sort/unsort glue (`ineff-switch-layers-1`), valid at every 1-32 rows.
- `ineff-runs-1`: the same grouping removes the excess re-reads.

Final structure (v7): 192/384 threads per group, 2 outputs per thread (an
even pair shares one weight word + one scale/bias), chunks of 2 pairs with
scalar accumulators, branchless inner loop (short chunks pad with pair 0's x,
phantom stores skipped), K unrolled x2 with even/odd accumulators.

Threadgroup memory by hand (grader does not check 32 KB): k1 = 12 KB weight
tiles + 3 KB scales/biases + 128 B x tile + ~1 KB pair lists ≈ 16.1 KB; k2
likewise ≈ 16.1 KB. Threadgroups 192/384. All indexing valid for rows 1-32
(P = rows*4 ≤ 128; guarded plist reads); barriers uniform; each (pair,
output) written once, no atomics.

282|def dim(expr, rows):
283|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
284|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
285|    if isinstance(expr, int):
286|        return expr
287|    value = 1
288|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
289|        if not TERM.match(term):
290|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
291|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)

303|def build(spec, sources, slot):
304|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
305|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
306|    kernels = []
307|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
308|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
309|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
310|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
311|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
312|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
313|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
314|            header=header,
315|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
316|        )
317|        kernels.append((k, fn))
318|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
319|    if missing:
320|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
321|
322|    def run(**inputs):
323|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
324|        env = dict(inputs)
325|        for k, fn in kernels:
326|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
327|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
328|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
329|            outs = fn(
330|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
331|                template=[
332|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
333|                ],
334|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
335|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
336|                output_shapes=[
337|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
338|                ],
339|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
340|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
341|            )
342|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
343|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
344|
345|    return run

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing chains the 20 layers, so
9|each call waits for the one before, as in a decode step. The grader prints
10|its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when given. It never writes into
11|the attempt folder, which holds only the Muse agent's files.
12|
13|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
14|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
15|
16|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run as the
17|candidate, and adds `beats_baseline`. From round 2 on, the bar is the previous
18|round's final attempt for the slot (claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md).
19|The two are timed in alternating repeats, so drift in the GPU's clocks reaches
20|both alike, and the candidate beats the baseline at a row count only if it is
21|faster in at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats: a one-sided sign
22|test at p < 0.01. The same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. FOLDER alone is an
24|attempt for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one
25|routing+combine attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.
26|"""

84|def ulp_bf16(r):

184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs

204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:
221|            call()
222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
228|    return times

22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.

28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.

70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

4|256 threads per threadgroup (8 simdgroups) instead of 128 (4 simdgroups).
5|Grid goes from `rows*512` to `rows*1024` threads = still `rows*4` groups,
6|one per (row, expert-slot) pair. `block-1.metal` (qvm_block) is byte-identical
7|to attempt-2; only the wave structure in `block-0.metal` changed: gate/up 12
8|blocks in 2 waves of 8 (4 simds idle in wave 2, guarded by simd-uniform
9|`b < 12`), down 24 blocks in 3 waves of 8, x/silu strided loops step 256.
10|
11|Removes the 1-row half of attempt-2's occupancy finding (its notes.md miss
12|analysis): at 1 row, 4 pairs x 128 threads = 512 threads on a 16-core GPU
13|streams at only ~20 GB/s effective (2.21 MB in 107.3 us), regressing 7.5%
14|vs eager (99.8 us). Doubling threads per pair doubles each group's in-flight
15|memory parallelism while keeping the proven-correct numerics untouched: same
16|qvm strided-lane accumulation + `simd_sum` per 32-output block (guard is
17|uniform inside each simd, so the reduction stays uniform), same full-bf16
18|silu lowering, same fp32 accumulation and bf16 rounding points. Gate/up/down
19|weight bytes per pair are unchanged (553 KB), so 8/32 rows — already
20|streaming at ~94-109 GB/s — should be unaffected.

23|four bf16 rounding points, positional `y[r,j]`, any `inds` order, valid for
24|all 1-32 rows (grid is `rows*4` groups, no rows-dependent indexing),
25|256 threads/group <= 1024, threadgroup memory unchanged at 3840 B (~12% of
26|32 KB).

1|# Territory: quantized-kernels (round 2 — prefill path)
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:24:31Z
7|- **Next:** none — prefill checklist filled (§A–§H), 2 inefficiencies posted, note left on `territory-baseline-experts`
