9|## What it does
10|
11|This territory is MLX's `mx.gather_qmm` Metal kernels behind the `experts`
12|slot (`quantized.h`, `quantized_utils.h`, `utils.h` in the installed
13|0.32.4 headers, dispatch in MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp`). Round 1 mapped
14|it as decode-only: `affine_gather_qvm` runs at every decode size and
15|`affine_gather_qmm_rhs` was listed as never run
16|([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`](../../exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md)
17|§A/§C, frozen). Round 2 reopens it because the new G2 is bit-exact at
18|prefill sizes too: from 60 rows the reference switches to
19|`gather_qmm_rhs`, whose rounding is now on the correctness path at
20|prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows. This entry writes only what is new: the
21|prefill dispatch, the `qmm_rhs` arithmetic, and exactly how it diverges
22|from `qvm`. Decode facts that still hold are cited, not rewritten.
23|
24|## The checklist
25|
26|### A. Dispatch — `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` (which kernel runs at each size)
27|
28|- **Callers:** `ref_experts` (`bench/grader/slots.py:55-82`) and the
29|  served twin `SwitchGLU.__call__`
30|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:176-199`) both call
31|  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4,
32|  mode="affine", sorted_indices=do_sort)` three times per layer (gate,
33|  up, down), with `do_sort = inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16
34|  (`slots.py:62`, `switch_layers.py:181`). MLX is 0.32.4
35|  (`.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; print(mx.__version__)"`).
36|  Served weights are `[E, in, out]` via `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear`
37|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:142-184`), hence
38|  `transpose=False`; the `transpose=True` twin in `switch_layers.py:75-90`
39|  is not the served path.
40|- **Callees:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu`
41|  ([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1980-2094](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1980-L2094)).
42|  It shapes `K = x.shape(-1)`, `M = x.shape(-2)`,
43|  `N = out.shape(-1)`, `B = out.size()/M/N`,
44|  `E = w.size()/w.shape(-1)/w.shape(-2) = 60`,
45|  `vector_limit = 4` for `transpose=False` (`:2000-2005`). Branch order:
46|  (1) rhs fast path iff `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4`
47|  (`:2012-2031`); (2) else `gather_qmm` iff `M >= vector_limit`
48|  (`:2034-2054`); (3) else `gather_qmv` iff `transpose_` (`:2056-2075`);
49|  (4) else `gather_qvm` (`:2077-2094`). With `M=1` always (below),
50|  branch (2) never fires in this model.
51|- **Data / shapes at every grader size.** `x` reaching `gather_qmm` is
52|  `[B, 1, K]` with `B = rows*4`: `xx = expand_dims(x, (-2,-3))` then,
53|  when sorting, `_gather_sort` gathers to one row per pair
54|  (`slots.py:61-65`, `switch_layers.py:12-17`); hence `M = 1` and the
55|  `M` argument later passed to `gather_qmm_rhs` is `x.size()/K = B`
56|  (`:2013-2027`). Gate/up: `K=768, N=384`; down (input is the
57|  bfloat16 `silu*up` hidden): `K=384, N=768`.
58|
59|  | rows | B = rows·4 | B/E | sorted (`inds.size≥64`) | MLX kernel |
60|  |---|---|---|---|---|
61|  | 1 (decode) | 4 | 0.07 | no | `gather_qvm` |
62|  | 8 (decode) | 32 | 0.53 | no | `gather_qvm` |
63|  | 32 (decode) | 128 | 2.13 | yes | `gather_qvm` (sorted, still `B/E<4`) |
64|  | 127 (prefill) | 508 | 8.47 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
65|  | 1,016 (prefill) | 4,064 | 67.73 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
66|  | 2,048 (prefill) | 8,192 | 136.53 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
67|
68|  The switch is `rows >= 60` (`B >= 240 ⇔ B/E >= 4`; `B>=16` already
69|  holds from 4 rows). Two thresholds must not be conflated: sorting
70|  starts at 16 rows, the kernel switch at 60. The grader tests 32 and
71|  127, only bracketing 60; the exact threshold comes from this source,
72|  not from grader probing (cf. `territory-grader.md` *What the grader
73|  still cannot see* §1).
74|- **Neighbours:** before: router `inds` + `_gather_sort` (switch-layers
75|  territory); the sort is what sets `right_sorted_`. Between gate/up
76|  and down: compiled `swiglu` on bfloat16 values (other-kernels).
77|  After: `_scatter_unsort` back to positional `[rows, 4, 768]`, then
78|  combine. A replacement slot kernel sees only positional `inds`
79|  (any order, duplicates allowed) — the reference's sort is internal
80|  and invisible in `y` except through the bits.
81|- **Cost:** the dispatch itself launches nothing. Kernel counts and
82|  times per branch are in §C/§F. Prefill sizes are correctness-only in
83|  the grader (no timing; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`),
84|  so every prefill cost below is arithmetic, not a measured time.
85|- **Invariants:** `right_sorted_` is the Python `sorted_indices`
86|  argument trusted as-is; `gather_qmm_rhs` (§C) is only correct if
87|  `rhs_indices` really is sorted ascending by expert. `M` in the rhs
88|  call means total pairs `B`, not the `M=1` matrix height — the rhs
89|  kernel re-derives row tiles from `offsets` (§D).

91|### B. Host wrapper — `gather_qmm_rhs` (legacy path, the one this GPU runs)
92|
93|- **Callers:** only §A branch (1) (and the `GatherQQMM` twin at
94|  `quantized.cpp:2233-2251`, not this model).
95|- **Callees:** [gather_qmm_rhs v0.32.4:1676-1830](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1676-L1830).
96|  First gate: `is_nax_available() && (enable_tf32 || dtype != float32)`
97|  diverts to `gather_qmm_rhs_nax` (`:1692-1714`). On this machine that
98|  is false: device is Apple M1 Pro `applegpu_g13s`
99|  (`mx.device_info()`), architecture generation 13 < 17, and NAX also
100|  needs macOS 26.2
101|  ([device.cpp v0.32.4:978-995](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp#L978-L995)).
102|  So the legacy tiling below is the prefill path here; the NAX variant
103|  (`bm=32/64, bn=bk=64` in the same function, NAX MMA in
104|  `quantized_nax.h`) never runs on the grader GPU. Legacy tiles
105|  (`:1748-1749`): `bm=16, bn=32, bk=32`, `wm=1, wn=2`;
106|  `align_N = (N%32==0)`, `align_K = (K%32==0)` — both true for

108|  `offsets = gather_mm_offsets(indices, E, M=B, ...)` (`:1795`), one
109|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` launch with
110|  `group_dims = (32, wn, wm) = 64` threads and
111|  `grid_dims = ((N+31)/32, min(B, ceil(B/16)+E-1), 1)` (`:1817-1819`).
112|- **Data:** `broadcast_with_indices` (`:1721-1733`) copies `x` to
113|  `[B, 1, K]` only if `x.size()/x.shape(-2)/x.shape(-1) != B`; on the
114|  sorted path `x` already has `B` rows (the sort gathered it), so this
115|  is a no-op apart from `ensure_row_contiguous` flag checks, as are
116|  the `w`/`scales`/`biases` normalisations (already contiguous).
117|  `offsets` is `int32[E=60]` (240 B), the per-expert start rows in
118|  sorted order, built by one tiny kernel launch
119|  (`gather_mm_offsets`, host side at
120|  [matmul.cpp v0.32.4:2247-2265](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp#L2247-L2265):
121|  `dispatch_threads(60)`, one threadgroup). Inputs to the Metal kernel,
122|  in buffer order: `x` bfloat16 `[B, K]`, `w` uint32, `scales`/
123|  `biases` bfloat16, `offsets` int32, out `y` bfloat16 `[B, N]`, then
124|  `M=B, N, K, num_groups=60` as constants (`:1821-1835`).
125|- **Neighbours:** same slot edges as §A. The three products in one
126|  layer share the same sorted `idx`, hence the same `offsets` — yet
127|  each of the three calls recomputes it (see
128|  `ineff-quantized-kernels-2`).
129|- **Cost (arithmetic, per layer):** 3 offsets kernels + 3 main kernels
130|  per prefill layer-call (60 + 60 per 20-layer prefill forward),
131|  against 0 + 3 on the decode `qvm` path. Main-kernel dispatched
132|  threadgroups (64 threads each): gate/up `12 × grid_y`, down
133|  `24 × grid_y` with `grid_y = min(B, ceil(B/16)+59)` = 91 / 313 / 571
134|  at B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192 → gate/up 1,092 / 3,756 / 6,852 and down

136|  fewer (§C, `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).

138|  `ceil(B/16) + E - 1` is the worst case (every expert contributing a
139|  partial tile). Threadgroups whose tile index exceeds the real tile
140|  count return early inside the kernel (§C) — they are launched,
141|  scheduled, and discarded, never incorrect.

143|### C. Metal kernel — `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` + `schedule_row_tile`
144|
145|- **Callers:** §B only. Instantiated for this model as
146|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs<bfloat16, group_size=32, bits=4, BM=16,
147|  BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2, transpose=false>`
148|  (`quantized.h:2570-2593`).
149|- **Callees:** `schedule_row_tile<BM=16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) maps
150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive
159|  `BlockMMA::mma` over `K_it = K/BK` tiles (24 gate/up, 12 down),
160|  with an extra `gemm_loop_finalize` only when `!align_K` — never
161|  here, since `K % 32 == 0` (`quantized.h:2631, 2676-2717`).
162|- **Data:** threadgroup memory `Xs[16 × 40]` + `Ws[32 × 40]` bfloat16
163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =
164|  40`, `quantized.h:2596-2597, 2623-2624`; padding is the usual
165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows
170|  `y_row .. y_row+tgp_bm-1` of the already-gathered `[B, K]` matrix;
171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).
175|- **Neighbours:** consumes the sorter's output order directly; this
176|  is the only gather kernel whose addressing depends on pair order
177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,
179|  so `_scatter_unsort` after the down product is load-bearing for
180|  position, not for bits.
181|- **Cost (arithmetic):** balanced-expert model (counts near the
182|  uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are random tokens, so this is
183|  the expected case, not a bound): useful row tiles
184|  `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` ≈ 60 / 300 / 540 at B = 508 / 4,064 /
185|  8,192, against dispatched `grid_y` 91 / 313 / 571 (§B). Weight
186|  bytes read per product per layer = `T × 184,320 B` (per-expert
187|  147,456 B weights + 36,864 B scales/biases; §F) = 11.06 / 55.30 /
188|  99.53 MB, i.e. 1× / 5× / 9× the 11.06 MB distinct-expert floor —
189|  each extra row tile of an expert re-reads and re-dequantizes its
190|  full weights. The per-pair `qvm` path at the same `B` would read
191|  `B × 184,320 B` = 93.6 MB / 749 MB / 1.51 GB per product, so `rhs`
192|  is 8.5× / 13.5× / 15.2× leaner on weight traffic — grouping works;
193|  its waste is the tile quantization in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`,
194|  not the grouping idea.
195|- **Invariants:** correctness rests on sorted `rhs_indices` +
196|  exact `offsets`; an unsorted input silently computes tiles from
197|  mixed experts (dispatch trusts `right_sorted_`, §A). `BM=16`
198|  grouping changes only which rows share a weight-tile load — never
199|  a valid row's arithmetic (§E) — so a bit-exact replacement may
200|  regroup rows freely, including not grouping at all, as long as
201|  each row's own accumulation matches §D+§E.

208|  (`quantized.h:2613-2621`); same loader family as `qmm_n`/`qmm_t`
209|  (§G).
210|- **Callees:** `load_unsafe`/`load_safe` (`quantized.h:736-770`) call
211|  `dequantize<T, pack_factor=2, bits=4>` (`quantized.h:557-663`,
212|  bits=4 at `:617-623`) per packed byte: with `s = float(scale)`,
213|  `b = float(bias)` it writes
214|  `w_local[2i] = (bfloat16)(s * (w[i] & 0x0f) + b)` and
215|  `w_local[2i+1] = (bfloat16)((s/16) * (w[i] & 0xf0) + b)` into
216|  threadgroup `Ws`. Scales: one `scale`/`bias` pair per thread from
217|  `scales + bi * N/32` (`:733-734`); `group_steps = 32/32 = 1`, so
218|  `next()` advances `scales/biases` by `32*N/32 = N` per K tile
219|  (`:772-790`) — exactly one scale group per `BN=32` output tile and
220|  per `BK=32` row of `K`, matching the `[E, K, N/32]` layout.
221|- **Data:** packed uint32 weights are viewed as bytes (`(device
222|  uint8_t*)w`); each byte yields 2 outputs (low/high nibble), each
223|  `BK×BN = 1,024`-element weight tile dequantized once per
224|  (row tile, K tile) visit into `Ws`, then read by the MMA (§E).
225|  `x` tiles by contrast are copied verbatim (bfloat16 → bfloat16,
226|  exact) by `BlockLoader` (`steel/gemm/loader.h:74-80`).
227|- **Neighbours:** this is the first of the two divergence points
228|  vs `qvm` (§F): the dequantized weight is **rounded to bfloat16
229|  before any multiply**. In `qvm` the same `scale*q + bias` value
230|  stays in float32 registers through the product.
231|- **Cost:** dequant element-ops per product per layer =
232|  `T × K × N` = `T × 294,912` (both products have `K·N = 294,912`):
233|  17.7M / 88.5M / 159.2M at the three prefill sizes (balanced `T`
234|  from §C), each a float mul+add, a float→bfloat round, and a
235|  threadgroup store+reload. This recompute-per-row-tile is the
236|  loader's design (no dequantized-weight cache exists; the full
237|  dequantized expert is 294,912 × 2 B = 590 KB, far above the
238|  32 KB threadgroup limit, so cross-tile reuse would need a device
239|  buffer and an extra kernel — not a free fix).
240|- **Invariants:** `scale`/`bias` themselves are bfloat16 values
241|  upcast to float exactly (bfloat→float is exact), identical to
242|  `qvm`'s inputs; the *only* added rounding is
243|  `static_cast<bfloat16>(s*q + b)`. Relative error up to half a
244|  bfloat ULP (≈2⁻⁹ ≈ 0.2%) per weight element, deterministic per
245|  `(expert, k, n)` — the same rounded weight is reused for all
246|  ≤16 rows of the tile, so errors are correlated across rows
247|  sharing an expert, unlike per-pair float weights.
248|
249|### E. Accumulation — `BlockLoader` + `BlockMMA` (rounding point 2)
250|
251|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` instantiates
252|  `BlockMMA<bfloat16, bfloat16, BM=16, BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2,
253|  false, transpose=false, ...>` (`quantized.h:2599-2610`) and
254|  `BlockLoader<bfloat16, BM=16, BK=32, dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=1,
255|  tgp_size=64>` for `x` (`:2611-2612`).
256|- **Callees:** `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:439-537`) with
257|  `AccumType = float` by default (`mma.h:451`): accumulator
258|  fragments `Ctile` are `float` 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` tiles
259|  (`TM = 16/(8·1) = 2`, `TN = 32/(8·2) = 2` frags per simdgroup).
260|  `mma()` (`mma.h:513-537`) steps `kk` over `BK` in 8-wide frags
261|  (4 steps per tile), each `tile_matmad` issuing
262|  `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` (`mma.h:181-206, 406-427`).
263|  Operand fragments are loaded from threadgroup bfloat16 and
264|  widened to float (`BaseMMAFrag::load` casts, `mma.h:57-67`), so
265|  the multiply is float×float with float accumulate — but the
266|  weight operand is the already-bfloat-rounded value of §D, and
267|  the 8-term dot inside each frag is the hardware's tree order,
268|  not a serial FMA chain. `gemm_loop_*` then adds tile results
269|  sequentially over the 24/12 K tiles. Store:
270|  `store_result`/`store_result_safe` cast float → bfloat16 once
271|  (`mma.h:100-112, 540-592`; `quantized.h:2683, 2694`) — the same
272|  single final rounding as `qvm`.
273|- **Data:** `Xs` holds `16×32` bfloat16 activations per K tile
274|  (rows zero-padded by `load_safe` when `tgp_bm < 16`,
275|  `loader.h:83-128`); `Ws` holds the §D dequantized tile. Partial-row
276|  tiles take the `gemm_loop_unaligned<false, true, ...>` branch
277|  (`quantized.h:2687-2695`) — full MMA work on padded rows, results
278|  discarded.
279|- **Neighbours:** identical bfloat16 store boundary as `qvm`, so
280|  the downstream `swiglu` (gate/up) and down product see the same
281|  *kind* of rounding point — only the float value arriving at the
282|  cast differs.
283|- **Cost:** per product, MMA flops are `2·B_padded·K·N` with
284|  `B_padded = T·16` = 960 / 4,800 / 8,640 vs useful `B` = 508 /
285|  4,064 / 8,192 (padded fractions in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
286|  At 5.2 TFLOPS peak (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:14`) the useful MMA
287|  floors at `2·B·K·N/5.2 TFLOPS` = 57.6 / 461.0 / 929.2 µs per
288|  layer-product (B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192) if it ran at peak — it
289|  cannot, at `BM=16` tiles with two barriers per 32-K step
290|  (`quantized_utils.h:14-29`), so the path is
291|  overhead/latency-bound, not compute-bound; no measured prefill
292|  time exists to check this against (§A).
293|- **Invariants:** per-output accumulation grouping is
294|  **[contiguous 8-wide frag dots] sequentially over BK=32 tiles**,
295|  in increasing K. This is the second divergence from `qvm` (§F):
296|  even with bit-identical weight operands, regrouping a 768-term
297|  float sum this way rounds differently on generic data. Reproducing
298|  it with scalar FMAs is not bit-safe; reproducing it requires the
299|  same 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` fragmentation (same `BK`, same
300|  frag step order) or a proof the hardware order coincides — none
301|  exists in the sources. Warp tiling `WM/WN` only partitions frags
302|  across simdgroups; it does not change a single output's add order.
303|
304|### F. Comparator — `qvm_impl` + `qouter` (what decode runs; delta only)
305|
306|Round 1 §A mapped this kernel fully; only the contrast is new.
307|
308|- **Callers/Callees:** `gather_qvm` host (`quantized.cpp:1462-1529`)
309|  → `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`) → `qvm_impl`
310|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid `(1, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of
311|  64 threads; gate/up `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. Each lane owns
312|  one strided `K` element per 32-step (`x += block_size` with
313|  `block_size = 32`, `:1275-1287`) and accumulates 32 outputs in
314|  float registers via `qouter` (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 at
315|  `:503-509`): `result += x * (scale*q + bias)` with
316|  `scale`/`bias`/`x` all float, **no bfloat16 rounding of the
317|  weight**, serial per-lane adds in strided-K order
318|  (`k = lane, lane+32, ...`), then one `simd_sum` tree over the 32
319|  lane partials (`:1317-1321`) and a single float→bfloat16 store
320|  (`:1324-1329`).
321|- **The two divergences, side by side:**
322|
323|  | aspect | `gather_qvm` (decode, rows < 60) | `gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill, rows ≥ 60) |
324|  |---|---|---|
325|  | weight value | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup (§D) |
326|  | K grouping | strided lanes: lane `l` sums `k≡l (mod 32)` serially, then `simd_sum` tree | contiguous: 8-wide frag dots, sequential over BK=32 tiles (§E) |
327|  | rows sharing work | none: one grid slice per pair | ≤16 sorted rows share each weight tile |
328|  | final rounding | float → bfloat16 once after `simd_sum` | float → bfloat16 once after MMA — identical point |
329|
330|  Either divergence alone breaks bit-equality (measured: 62.4–62.6%
331|  of experts outputs differ at all three prefill sizes, max
332|  43/65/110.5 ULP, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-experts.json`;
333|  full statement in `ineff-baseline-experts-1`). A single arithmetic
334|  cannot match both kernels on generic inputs: pick any weight with
335|  `float(scale·q+bias)` not representable in bfloat16 and any
336|  `x ≠ 0` — the two references already disagree on that product
337|  before accumulation even starts. **Conclusion for builders: a
338|  size branch is required** — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
339|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic (bfloat-rounded dequant tiles + 8-wide frag
340|  accumulation) at/above 60 rows — or a proof of coincidence that
341|  the 62% differ rate rules out empirically. The branch threshold
342|  must be the dispatch rule `rows >= 60` (pairs `>= 240`, `E=60`),
343|  not the grader's nearest tested sizes 32/127: rows 33–59 in the
344|  real model still run `qvm` (§A). Row *grouping* inside the
345|  prefill branch is free (§C invariant); per-row accumulation is
346|  not.
347|- **Cost:** decode cost is round 1's confirmed entry
348|  (`muse-spark/exploration/ineff-quantized-kernels-1`, confirmed;
349|  round-2 restatement `ineff-baseline-experts-3`): 51 MB read in
350|  0.92 ms at 1 row (55 GB/s), 908 MB in 14.67 ms at 32 rows
351|  (62 GB/s, 31% of peak). Not re-posted here.
352|- **Invariants:** both paths accumulate in float32 and round to
353|  bfloat16 exactly once per product; `silu(gate)·up` is computed on
354|  those bfloat16 values and rounded again before down (brief:
355|  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). Any candidate must keep all
356|  four bfloat16 points (gate, up, hidden, down) — matching only the
357|  final `y` rounding is insufficient, since 1-ULP hidden flips
358|  amplify through down (round 1
359|  `muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md:103-108`).
360|
361|### G. Never-run neighbours — `gather_qmm` / `qmm_n_impl` / `qmm_t_impl`
362|
363|- **Callers:** §A branch (2) needs `M >= 4`; MobileMoE always has
364|  `M=1`, so `affine_gather_qmm_n`/`_t` (`quantized.h:2418-2568`)
365|  with `qmm_n_impl` (`:1468-1595`) / `qmm_t_impl` (`:1341-1459`),
366|  all `BM=BN=BK=32, WM=WN=2`, never run in this model at any size.
367|  Documented so no one chases them for the prefill failure: the
368|  prefill kernel is `qmm_rhs` (§C), not these.
369|- **Callees/Data/Invariants:** they share §D's loader (bfloat-rounded
370|  weights) and §E's `BlockMMA` accumulation, so their per-output
371|  arithmetic would match `qmm_rhs`'s rounding family — but their
372|  grid is per `(N tile, M tile, pair-batch B)` via
373|  `adjust_matrix_offsets`, not offset tiles. Zero cost here; the
374|  only use is as evidence that MLX's matrix family consistently
375|  dequantizes to the element type before multiplying, while its
376|  vector family (`qvm`/`qmv`) does not.
377|
378|### H. NAX variant — `gather_qmm_rhs_nax` (not on this GPU)
379|
380|- **Callers:** §B's first gate only; false on the M1 Pro grader
381|  machine (§B). Tiles there are `bm=32` (or 64 when `M/E >= 64`),
382|  `bn=bk=64` with NAX matrix ops (`quantized_nax.h`). If the grader
383|  ever moved to an M3-class GPU, the prefill reference's frag size
384|  and K blocking would change with it, and a hard-coded `BK=32`
385|  replica would fail G2 there. On the current hardware this is a
386|  portability note, not a cost.
387|

TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")


def dim(expr, rows):
    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
    if isinstance(expr, int):
        return expr
    value = 1
    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
        if not TERM.match(term):
            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
    return value


def template_value(v):

        return v
    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:

    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")

"""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np

D, E, K, H = 768, 60, 4, 384
SCALE = 2.5  # routed_scaling_factor; norm_topk_prob is true
NAMES = {"D": D, "E": E, "K": K, "H": H}
DTYPES = {
    "float32": mx.float32,
    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
    "float16": mx.float16,
    "uint32": mx.uint32,
    "int32": mx.int32,
}
SLOTS = {
    "routing": (["x", "w_router", "bias"], ["inds", "weights"]),
    "combine": (["y", "weights", "shared"], ["out"]),
}
EXPERT_WEIGHTS = [
    f"{p}_{t}" for p in ("gate", "up", "down") for t in ("w", "scales", "biases")
]
SLOTS["experts"] = (["x", "inds"] + EXPERT_WEIGHTS, ["y"])
SLOTS["routing+combine"] = (
    SLOTS["routing"][0] + ["y", "shared"],
    ["inds", "weights", "out"],
)
INPUTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "models" / "muse-inputs"


def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE


def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared


def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort

    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
    idx, inv = inds, None
    if do_sort:
        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)

    def qmm(a, w):
        return mx.gather_qmm(
            a,
            *w,
            rhs_indices=idx,
            transpose=False,
            group_size=32,
            bits=4,
            mode="affine",
            sorted_indices=do_sort,
        )

    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
    if do_sort:
        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
    return y.squeeze(-2)


REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}


def expert_weights(experts):
    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
    return {
        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
    }


def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.

    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
    """

    def moe_call(self, x):
        lead = x.shape[:-1]
        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
        if experts is None:
            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
        else:
            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
        return out.reshape(*lead, D)

    return moe_call

def main():

    ap.add_argument("attempt", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("slot", choices=tuple(slots.SLOTS))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="also write the verdict here")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",

        default=[],
        metavar="[SLOT=]FOLDER",
        help="an earlier attempt to time in the same run (repeat for routing+combine)",
    )

    attempt, slot = args.attempt, args.slot
    gpu_lock.hold(f"check_candidate.py {attempt} {slot}")
    base = baselines(args.baseline, slot) if args.baseline else None
    result = {"slot": slot, "g1": False, "g2": False, "beats_compiled": False}
    if base:
        result |= {
            "baseline": args.baseline,
            "beats_baseline": False,
            "wins_needed": f"{WINS_NEEDED} of {REPEATS} paired repeats",
        }
    try:
        fns = load(attempt, slot)
        model = slots.load_model()
        weights = slots.model_expert_weights(model) if slot == "experts" else None
        stats = {}
        sizes = [("rows", lambda r=r: slots.load_inputs(r, weights)) for r in ROWS]
        sizes += [
            ("prefill rows", lambda r=r: slots.capture_prefill(model, r, weights))
            for r in slots.PROMPT_REQUESTS
        ]
        for kind, inputs in sizes:
            layers = inputs()
            size = f"{kind} {layers[0]['x'].shape[0]}"
            for part, fn in fns.items():
                check = {
                    "routing": check_routing,
                    "combine": check_combine,
                    "experts": check_experts,
                }[part]
                per_layer = [check(fn, layer) for layer in layers]
                errors = [s["error"] for s in per_layer if "error" in s]
                if errors:
                    stats[f"{part} {size}"] = {"error": errors[0]}
                    continue
                agg = {
                    k: (max if k.startswith("max") else sum)(s[k] for s in per_layer)
                    for k in per_layer[0]

                examples = [

        result["correctness"] = stats
        result["g2"] = all(s.get("pass") for s in stats.values())

            for rows in ROWS:

                row = {"reference": 0.0, "compiled": 0.0, "candidate": 0.0}
                base_t, cand_t = [0.0] * REPEATS, [0.0] * REPEATS
                for part, fn in fns.items():

                    wrap = lambda f: lambda **kw: f(

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write a faster MobileMoE-S decode kernel
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
12|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
13|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
14|
15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|
94|## Tools and limits
95|
96|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
97|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
98|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes; stop one that hangs.
99|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
100|
101|## Rules of this session
102|
103|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
104|
105|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
106|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
107|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
108|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
109|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
110|
111|## Your files
112|
113|```
114|muse-spark/
115|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
116|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
117|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
118|    spec.json                                the launch spec
119|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
120|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
121|```
122|
123|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
124|
125|```bash
126|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
127|```
128|
129|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
130|
131|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
132|
133|```json
134|{
135|  "targets": [
136|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
137|  ]
138|}
139|```
140|
141|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
142|
143|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
144|
145|```json
146|{
147|  "kernels": [
148|    {
149|      "name": "fused_routing",
150|      "source_block": 0,
151|      "header_block": null,
152|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
153|      "outputs": [
154|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
155|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
156|      ],
157|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
158|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
159|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
160|      "init_value": null,
161|      "atomic_outputs": false
162|    }
163|  ],
164|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
165|}
166|```
167|
168|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
169|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
170|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
171|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
172|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
173|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
174|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
175|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
176|
177|## How each attempt is judged
178|
179|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
182|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
183|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
184|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
185|
186|   At every size:
187|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
188|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
189|
190|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
191|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
192|3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.
193|
194|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
195|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
196|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
197|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.
198|
199|**The piece timing** runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and waits for the GPU once at the end. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.
200|
201|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and beats the compiled reference in the piece timing at all three row counts, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

1|# Attempt 1 — builder-2-a, single fused kernel (direction a)
2|
3|First attempt in this direction: one Metal kernel per layer fusing router
4|scores (matmul + sigmoid + bias), top-4 selection, and weight normalize/scale.
5|One threadgroup (32 threads) per row; thread t computes experts t and t+32;
6|thread 0 does the serial top-4 scan and writes the outputs.
7|
8|## Inefficiency removed
9|
10|`ineff-runs-2`: routing costs 1.02 ms/step at 1 row for ~4 MB of traffic —
11|12 tiny kernels/layer of pure launch overhead (argpartition full-sorts 60
12|elements/row; the weights-norm sum runs on 1 thread at 1 row). This attempt
13|replaces all 12 with 1 launch/layer, keeping the same traffic floor
14|(w_router 60*768 f32 = 184 KB/layer/row, read once per row).
15|
16|## Prediction (µs per layer)
17|
18|Fixed cost per tiny kernel 6.81 µs
19|(`results/runs/2026-10-30-micro/step_parts.txt:2`); peak bandwidth 200 GB/s
20|(brief:9). One launch ≈ 6.8 µs plus traffic rows*184 KB at 200 GB/s:
21|
22|- 1 row: 6.8 + 184 KB / 200 GB/s (0.9) ≈ **8 µs**
23|- 8 rows: 6.8 + 1.47 MB / 200 GB/s (7.4) ≈ **14 µs**
24|- 32 rows: 6.8 + 5.9 MB / 200 GB/s (29.5) ≈ **36 µs**
25|
26|Compute (2*60*768 = 92k FLOP/row) and the 60-element serial scan are
27|negligible. Original reference per layer ≈ 1.02 ms/20 = 51 µs at 1 row
28|(ineff-runs-2 ÷ 20 layers).
29|
30|## Verdict
31|
32|G1 pass, G2 pass, beats `mx.compile(ref_routing)` at all three row counts.
33|Grader output (µs per layer, reference / compiled / candidate):
34|
35|- 1 row: 36.1 / 30.5 / **28.5** (predicted 8)
36|- 8 rows: 48.0 / 42.0 / **23.6** (predicted 14)
37|- 32 rows: 65.4 / 49.1 / **41.8** (predicted 36)
38|
39|Correctness: 0 wrong-expert rows, 0 near-tie rows, max rel err 2.6e-6 at all
40|row counts (limit 1e-4) — the f32 dot + sigmoid + exact-op-order weights match
41|the reference with ~40x margin, and no selection flip occurred on any of the
42|41 captured rows × 20 layers.
43|
44|Per the brief's stop rule (first attempt beating compiled at all three row
45|counts), this attempt stops the slot; G3/end-to-end are the team's call.
46|
47|## Why the 1/8-row predictions missed (>20%)
48|
49|The traffic model held (32 rows: 41.8 vs 36 predicted, +16%), but the fixed
50|cost is ~24 µs, not one 6.81 µs launch. The verdict itself proves it: the
51|reference's 12 kernels measure 36.1 µs/layer at 1 row, i.e. ~3 µs each in
52|this harness — far below the 6.81 µs whole-step figure from
53|`step_parts.txt:2` that I used. So per-launch cost in the piece-timing
54|harness (20 calls enqueued, one GPU wait, ÷20) is small, and my single
55|kernel's 28.5 µs is dominated by fixed per-harness cost: one wavefront on a
56|16-core GPU (single threadgroup at 1 row), MLX `metal_kernel` dispatch +
57|command encoding per call, and the amortized eval/wait. Consistent with this,
58|8 rows (23.6 µs) is *faster* than 1 row (28.5 µs): more threadgroups amortize
59|the fixed cost better, the opposite of a traffic model.
60|
61|Consequence for the saving: piece-timing saving vs the reference at 1 row is
62|(36.1−28.5)×20 = 0.15 ms/step, not the 0.9 ms the knock-out scaling
63|predicted — the knock-out (1.02 ms) and the piece harness (0.72 ms) disagree
64|on the slot's standalone cost, and G3 decides which one the fused kernel
65|actually cashes. The compute itself (92k FLOP/row, 60-element scan) is
66|negligible either way; further work on this slot should attack the ~24 µs
67|fixed floor (e.g. fewer, larger dispatches across layers is out of scope for
68|the slot — so nothing left here), not the kernel body.

1|# Territory: baseline-routing — the routing slot's starting point under bit-exact G2
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-routing
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:20:20Z
7|- **Next:** none — checklist filled for all pieces, ineff-baseline-routing-1..4 posted, grader and g3 notes folded
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|In every decode step and every prefill chunk, each of the 20 layers runs
12|`MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`): cast the
13|layer input to float32, multiply by the router weight transposed, sigmoid, add the
14|expert bias only for selection, take the top-4 experts per row, gather their
15|*unbiased* scores, normalise them (divide by their sum + 1e-20) and scale by 2.5.
16|The slot outputs `inds` [rows,4] uint32 and `weights` [rows,4] float32; `inds`
17|feeds the experts slot, `weights` feeds combine, which sums the 4 (expert,
18|weight) pairs *in the emitted order* — which is why round 2's G2 requires the
19|same experts, the same weights and the same order, bit for bit
20|(`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:25-27`,
21|`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:119-121`).
22|
23|The starting point is round 1's `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1`: one fused
24|Metal kernel per layer (`block-0.metal`, 78 lines; `spec.json`: one kernel
25|`fused_routing`, grid `rows*32`, threadgroup 32). One threadgroup per row stages
26|`x[row]` (768 bfloat16→float32) in threadgroup memory, each of the 32 threads
27|computes 1–2 experts' 768-term dot products serially, writes
28|`sigmoid(acc)` to `scores[60]`, and thread 0 alone does a serial insertion
29|top-4 scan over the biased scores and writes `inds`/`weights`
30|(`block-0.metal:10-78`).

32|## The headline finding (details in ineff-baseline-routing-1 and -2)
33|
34|Under the new grader the starting point fails G2 at **every** size while the
35|experts and their order always match (`rows_other_experts` 0 everywhere):
36|rows differing 20/159/638 at decode 1/8/32 rows (of 20/160/640 rows summed over
37|20 layers — 100% / 99.4% / 99.7% of rows) and 2,518/16,187/32,743 at prefill
38|127/1,016/2,048 rows (of 2,540/20,320/40,960 — 99.1% / 79.7% / 79.9%), max
39|relative error 2.6e-06 at decode and up to 8.7e-06 in the prefill
40|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`, quoted in
41|`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/README.md:39`). The experts match because
42|selection is insensitive to last-bit score differences (no captured row is a
43|near-tie at the 4th/5th place); the weights expose every last-bit difference
44|in the 4 selected scores. Section 3 below pins down, op by op, which of the
45|reference's operations the kernel reproduces exactly and which it does not:
46|**the divergence is in the scores — the router matmul's float32 accumulation
47|order (which changes with `rows`) and MLX's sigmoid formula — not in the
48|4-term weight sum, whose order the kernel already matches.**

151|### 3. Op-by-op: where the kernel's arithmetic matches the reference's, and where it does not
152|
153|#### 3.1 The router product `x.astype(f32) @ w_router.T` — DOES NOT MATCH (main cause)
154|
155|The kernel accumulates each expert's dot product **serially, in one thread,
156|in increasing `d` order**: `acc += xsh[d] * w_router[wbase + d]` for
157|`d = 0..767` (`block-0.metal:31-34`; the Metal compiler may contract each
158|mul+add to an FMA, but the grouping stays a 768-long left-to-right chain).
159|
160|The reference never does that. `Matmul::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4,
161|`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, fetched 2026-11-04) sees A = `x` [rows,768]
162|f32 (not transposed), B = `w_router.T` [768,60] (transposed view), so
163|`transpose_a=false, transpose_b=true`, M=rows, N=60, K=768:
164|
165|- **rows = 1 → GEMV.** `min(M,N)==1` routes to `gemv`
166|  (matmul.cpp, `Matmul::eval_gpu`); the `gemv_wide` shortcut is skipped
167|  because the output is float32 (`gemv_wide_config` requires float16/bfloat16
168|  out). Dispatch picks `GEMVKernel<float, BM=4, BN=1, SM=1, SN=32, TM=4,
169|  TN=4>`: each output is accumulated by one simdgroup whose 32 lanes each
170|  serially sum 24 products — lane `l` takes `d = i*128 + l*4 + (0..3)` for
171|  `i = 0..5` (`kernels/gemv.h:162-182`) — and the 32 partials are then combined
172|  by a shuffle tree, `result += simd_shuffle_down(result, sn)` for
173|  sn = 16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`). Grouping: 32 blocked partials + pairwise
174|  tree, not a serial chain.
175|- **rows = 8, 32, 127 → steel split-K GEMM.** In `steel_matmul_axpby` the
176|  split-K case fires when `_tm*_tn <= 2048` (this device's architecture string
177|  ends in `s`; brief:99 names it `applegpu_g13s`), `_tk = 768/16 = 48 >= 8`
178|  and `K >= max(M,N)` (matmul.cpp, Case 1). `steel_gemm_splitk_axpby` uses
179|  BM=16 (M<40) or 32, BN=32, BK=16, WM=WN=2 (steel/gemm split-K dispatch):
180|  partitions = min(max(2, next_pow2(48/(_tm*_tn))), 32) with
181|  `_tm=(M+31)/32, _tn=2` → **32 partitions at rows 8 and 32** (the last
182|  partition also absorbs the remaining 16 BK-iterations,
183|  `steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_splitk.h:140-155`), **8 partitions at rows
184|  127**. Each partition accumulates its K-slice with simdgroup 8×8 matrix
185|  multiply-accumulate over BK=16 chunks in order (GEMMKernel/mma in
186|  `steel/gemm/gemm.h`, `mma.h`), writes a float32 partial, and
187|  `gemm_splitk_accum` sums the partials sequentially in partition order
188|  (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`).
189|- **rows = 1,016, 2,048 → regular steel GEMM.** Split-K no longer fires
190|  (768 < M), so `steel_matmul_regular_axpby` runs with the device tile from
191|  `GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` (for an architecture ending in `s` the macro's fallback:
192|  BM=64, BN=64, BK=16, WM=2, WN=2): K is walked in BK=16 chunks staged through
193|  threadgroup memory, accumulated by simdgroup matrix ops chunk after chunk.
194|
195|So the reference has **three different float32 accumulation orders for the
196|same mathematical product, selected by `rows`** — and none of them is the
197|kernel's serial order. Every score therefore differs from the reference's in
198|the last bits with high probability, which is exactly the observed pattern:
199|~100% of decode rows and ~80–99% of prefill rows have at least one differing
200|weight, while no row picks different experts (the biased-score gaps at the
201|4th/5th place are far larger than 1-ULP score noise on these inputs).
202|The drop from ~100% (decode, GEMV/split-K regimes) to ~80% (1,016/2,048,
203|regular GEMM) is consistent with a per-regime last-bit flip rate; that last
204|step is an inference from the counts, not a measurement.
205|A scalar re-implementation cannot reproduce the steel regimes' rounding by
206|reordering a serial loop: within each 8×8 simdgroup matrix op the 8-product
207|accumulation is the hardware's. A bit-exact candidate must either reuse
208|`simdgroup_float8x8` multiply-accumulate with the same tiling/K-order per
209|regime (branching on `rows` inside the kernel, or one kernel per regime in
210|the spec), or find an accumulation that provably rounds identically — none
211|is known.
212|
213|#### 3.2 The sigmoid — DOES NOT MATCH (independent second cause)
214|
215|Kernel (`block-0.metal:35`): `1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))` — the fast
216|(non-`precise`) `exp`, applied to `-acc`, one division.
217|
218|Reference (`mx.sigmoid` → `Sigmoid` in
219|`mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`, installed headers):
220|
221|```metal
222|auto y = 1 / (1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(x)));
223|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;
224|```
225|
226|Three differences, each able to move the result by 1 ULP: (a) `precise::exp`
227|vs `metal::exp`; (b) the argument is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0`
228|the result is `1 - y` (a subtraction that rounds) instead of the direct
229|division the kernel computes for all signs. Even a kernel whose matmul
230|matched bit for bit would still fail G2 on sigmoid alone for a large share
231|of scores. The fix is free in time: copy this formula verbatim.
232|
233|#### 3.3 Selection, gather, and the weight normalisation — MATCH
234|
235|- `scores + bias`: one f32 add in both (`block-0.metal:45`;
236|  `binary_ops.h:10-15`).
237|- Selection: the kernel's strictly-greater insertion scan emits descending
238|  biased order, earliest index winning ties (`block-0.metal:44-61`). The
239|  reference's argpartition is a full sort of `-(scores+bias)`
240|  (round-1 note, `ineff-runs-2.md:94-98`); on all six graded sizes the emitted
241|  sets *and* order agree (`rows_other_experts` 0, and the grader's worst-row
242|  examples show identical expert lists, grade-exact-routing.json). This is
243|  the part of Claude's round-1 reading ("the reference's order of
244|  operations … differ", round-2 README:39) that does **not** need fixing —
245|  but a builder must preserve the exact tie behaviour, since G2 now also
246|  compares order (`check_candidate.py:120`).
247|- The 4-term sum: the reference's `w.sum(axis=-1)` on a [rows,4] f32 array
248|  takes `row_reduce_small` (row_size 4 <= 64, MLX v0.32.4
249|  `mlx/backend/metal/reduce.cpp`, `row_reduce_general_dispatch` Case 1) in its
250|  per-thread branch (`non_row_reductions=1 < 32 && row_size <= 8`,
251|  `row_reduce_small` dispatch), i.e. `thread_reduce` with `N_READS=4`
252|  (`defines.h:12`): `total = (((0 + w0) + w1) + w2) + w3` in memory order —
253|  and `w`'s memory order is the `inds` order from argpartition, the same
254|  sequence the kernel sums as `s0 + s1 + s2 + s3` (`block-0.metal:64-68`;
255|  `kernels/reduction/reduce_row.h:164-181`). The kernel then adds `1e-20f`
256|  inside the same expression (`denom = s0+s1+s2+s3 + 1e-20f`), the reference
257|  as a separate add after the reduction (`slots.py:48`) — same association,
258|  and in float32 `sum + 1e-20` equals `sum` for any sum above ~1e-27, so the
259|  epsilon cannot be the cause either. Division and ×2.5 are the same single
260|  ops (`binary_ops.h:43-48,208-213`; `block-0.metal:74-77`).
261|  **Conclusion:** once the 4 selected scores are bit-equal and in the same
262|  order, the weights are bit-equal. Builders should spend their effort on
263|  3.1 and 3.2, not on the normalisation — the opposite emphasis to round 2
264|  README:39's example list, which names "the float32 sum order of
265|  `x @ w_router.T` and of `w.sum(...)`" as co-equal suspects.

13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:31-34`)
16|computes each of the 60 router scores as one thread's serial float32 chain,
17|`acc += xsh[d] * w_router[e*768 + d]` for d = 0..767 (compiler FMA contraction
18|does not change the left-to-right grouping). The reference,
19|`mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`),
20|never accumulates that way. In MLX 0.32.4's `Matmul::eval_gpu`
21|(`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, tag v0.32.4) with M=rows, N=60, K=768,
22|A not transposed, B transposed, the accumulation order is chosen by `rows`:
23|
24|| rows | MLX kernel | float32 accumulation order |
25||---|---|---|
26|| 1 | GEMV `gemv_float32_bm4_bn1_sm1_sn32_tm4_tn4` (`min(M,N)==1` → `gemv`; `gemv_wide` skipped, f32 out) | 32 lanes × serial 24 products (lane l: d = i*128 + l*4 + 0..3, i=0..5, `kernels/gemv.h:162-182`), then shuffle tree sn=16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`) |
27|| 8, 32, 127 | steel split-K GEMM (Case 1: `_tm*_tn <= 2048` on this `…s` device, `_tk=48 >= 8`, `K >= max(M,N)`) | 32 K-partitions (8/32 rows) or 8 (127 rows); each partition: simdgroup 8×8 MMA over BK=16 chunks (BM=16/32, BN=32); partials summed sequentially in partition order (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`); last partition absorbs the remainder iterations (`splitk.h:140-155`) |

31|reordering: the 8-product accumulation inside each `simdgroup_float8x8`
32|multiply-accumulate is the hardware's. Bit-exactness therefore needs either
33|the same simdgroup matrix ops with the same tiling and K-order per regime
34|(branch on `rows`, or separate spec kernels), or a proof that another order
35|rounds identically (none known). Full derivation:
36|`territory-baseline-routing.md` section 3.1.

9|## Slot

13|## What happens
14|
15|Each row's threadgroup streams the full router weight for its own experts
16|straight from device memory (`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:30-34`):
17|60×768 float32 = 184 KB per row per layer, with no sharing across rows. The
18|reference's GEMM reads `w_router` once per layer and reuses each tile across
19|all rows in the tile (steel GEMM/GEMV dispatches, territory section 3.1).
20|Per layer the starting point therefore reads rows×184 KB where the reference
21|reads 184 KB: 0.18 MB at 1 row, 1.47 MB at 8 rows, 5.90 MB at 32 rows (and
22|377 MB at the 2,048-row prefill size, where only correctness is graded —
23|ADR 0010:42 — so that figure costs grader time, not step time).
24|
25|## Cost
26|
27|Traffic floor at the 200 GB/s peak (brief:9): candidate 0.9 / 7.4 / 29.5 µs
28|per layer at 1/8/32 rows vs the reference's 0.9 µs at every row count. At 32
29|rows the excess (5.90−0.18 MB ≈ 5.7 MB/layer ≈ 28.6 µs at peak, 0.57 ms/step
30|over 20 layers) is ~43% of the candidate's measured 68.9 µs/layer
31|(independent timing, `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:47`) — the one place
32|in this slot where bytes, not launches, are a large share. At 1 and 8 rows
33|the excess is 0 and ~6.4 µs/layer respectively.

36|
37|Bandwidth-bound at 32 rows only; overhead-bound at 1/8 rows (the slot's
38|usual regime, `ineff-runs-2`).

184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs

204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:

222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)

{"path":"muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-1/notes.md","content":"# Round-2 attempt 1 — builder-2-a, direction (a): faithful MLX-regime replica

One fused Metal kernel, 256 threads (8 simdgroups) per row, branching on
`rows` in-Metal. Baseline: none. Builds on the starting point
`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1` (kept: bf16->f32 cast, strictly-greater
insertion top-4 with earliest-index tie win, `((w0+w1)+w2)+w3 + 1e-20` then
`/ denom * 2.5` on unbiased scores).

## What changed since the starting point

- Product: serial 768-term chain replaced by the MLX regime for `rows`:
  rows==1 GEMV lane order (`d=i*128+lane*4+0..3`, i=0..5) + shuffle tree
  16,8,4,2,1; 1<rows<=768 split-K (BK=16 chunks, partitions from
  `next_pow2(48/((rows+31)/32*2))` clamped to [2,32], base `48/partitions`
  chunks, last partition to chunk 48, partials added in partition order);
  rows>768 BK=16 chunks in order. MMA regimes use `simdgroup_float8x8`
  multiply-accumulate, two 8-wide ops per BK=16 chunk; only A-tile row 0 is
  the real row, other rows staged zero, so per-element K order is steel's.
- Sigmoid: `1/(1+exp(-acc))` replaced by MLX verbatim
  `y=1/(1+precise::exp(abs(s))); (s<0)?y:1-y`, float32 throughout.
- Top-4/weights: unchanged from the starting point (see above).

## Inefficiencies removed

`ineff-baseline-routing-1` (three product accumulation orders), `-2`
(sigmoid formula), and the serial-dot part of `-3` (dots now lane- or
MMA-parallel; the serial thread-0 scan is kept deliberately to preserve
the tie rule bit for bit).

## Predicted us per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows

Starting point measured 28.5 / 23.6 / 41.8 us (its notes.md) against a
~24 us chained-harness floor; traffic per row is 184 KB (0.9 us at
200 GB/s) and body work is 92k FLOP/row. This kernel keeps one launch,
widens to 8 simdgroups/row (better 1-row occupancy) but the MMA path
stages 48 chunks x 2 barriers and wastes 7/8 of each 8x8 tile at decode
sizes, so I predict it lands near the starting point, not below the floor:
1 row ~ 24 floor + 0.9 traffic + ~2 MMA staging ~= **27 us**;
8 rows ~ 24 amortised + 7.4 traffic ~= **26 us**;
32 rows ~ 18 amortised + 29.5 traffic ~= **40 us**.
Compiled reference (starting point's run): 30.5 / 42.0 / 49.1 us, so a
chained win is plausible only if G2 passes.

## Known limits (stated before grading)

- MMA tile is 8 rows x 8 experts, not steel's BM=16/32 x BN=32 (split-K)
  or 64x64 (regular). Per-element K/chunk/partition order matches; if the
  hardware 8-product rounding depended on tile position it would still
  differ — no evidence it does, but this is the residual risk.
- GEMV per-lane products use the same `acc += x*w` form as MLX gemv.h;
  compiler FMA contraction is assumed to match MLX's build.
- The thread-0 top-4 scan remains serial (60 steps) by design for ties.

## Verdict

(not graded yet)

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write a faster MobileMoE-S decode kernel
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
12|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
13|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
14|
15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|
94|## Tools and limits
95|
96|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
97|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
98|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes; stop one that hangs.
99|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
100|
101|## Rules of this session
102|
103|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
104|
105|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
106|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
107|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**

112|

114|muse-spark/
115|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
116|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
117|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
118|    spec.json                                the launch spec

122|
123|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
124|
125|```bash
126|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
127|```
128|
129|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.

131|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
132|

134|{
135|  "targets": [
136|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
137|  ]

144|

146|{
147|  "kernels": [
148|    {
149|      "name": "fused_routing",
150|      "source_block": 0,
151|      "header_block": null,
152|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
153|      "outputs": [
154|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
155|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
156|      ],

167|
168|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
169|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
170|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
171|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
172|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
173|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.

176|
177|## How each attempt is judged
178|
179|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
182|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
183|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
184|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
185|
186|   At every size:
187|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
188|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
189|
190|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
191|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
192|3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.
193|
194|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
195|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
196|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
197|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.
198|
199|**The piece timing** runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and waits for the GPU once at the end. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.
200|
201|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and beats the compiled reference in the piece timing at all three row counts, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.
