1|# Attempt 1 — builder-2-a, single fused kernel (direction a)
2|
3|First attempt in this direction: one Metal kernel per layer fusing router
4|scores (matmul + sigmoid + bias), top-4 selection, and weight normalize/scale.
5|One threadgroup (32 threads) per row; thread t computes experts t and t+32;
6|thread 0 does the serial top-4 scan and writes the outputs.
7|
8|## Inefficiency removed
9|
10|`ineff-runs-2`: routing costs 1.02 ms/step at 1 row for ~4 MB of traffic —
11|12 tiny kernels/layer of pure launch overhead (argpartition full-sorts 60
12|elements/row; the weights-norm sum runs on 1 thread at 1 row). This attempt
13|replaces all 12 with 1 launch/layer, keeping the same traffic floor
14|(w_router 60*768 f32 = 184 KB/layer/row, read once per row).
15|
16|## Prediction (µs per layer)
17|
18|Fixed cost per tiny kernel 6.81 µs
19|(`results/runs/2026-10-30-micro/step_parts.txt:2`); peak bandwidth 200 GB/s
20|(brief:9). One launch ≈ 6.8 µs plus traffic rows*184 KB at 200 GB/s:
21|
22|- 1 row: 6.8 + 184 KB / 200 GB/s (0.9) ≈ **8 µs**
23|- 8 rows: 6.8 + 1.47 MB / 200 GB/s (7.4) ≈ **14 µs**
24|- 32 rows: 6.8 + 5.9 MB / 200 GB/s (29.5) ≈ **36 µs**
25|
26|Compute (2*60*768 = 92k FLOP/row) and the 60-element serial scan are
27|negligible. Original reference per layer ≈ 1.02 ms/20 = 51 µs at 1 row
28|(ineff-runs-2 ÷ 20 layers).
29|
30|## Verdict
31|
32|G1 pass, G2 pass, beats `mx.compile(ref_routing)` at all three row counts.
33|Grader output (µs per layer, reference / compiled / candidate):
34|
35|- 1 row: 36.1 / 30.5 / **28.5** (predicted 8)
36|- 8 rows: 48.0 / 42.0 / **23.6** (predicted 14)
37|- 32 rows: 65.4 / 49.1 / **41.8** (predicted 36)
38|
39|Correctness: 0 wrong-expert rows, 0 near-tie rows, max rel err 2.6e-6 at all
40|row counts (limit 1e-4) — the f32 dot + sigmoid + exact-op-order weights match
41|the reference with ~40x margin, and no selection flip occurred on any of the
42|41 captured rows × 20 layers.
43|
44|Per the brief's stop rule (first attempt beating compiled at all three row
45|counts), this attempt stops the slot; G3/end-to-end are the team's call.
46|
47|## Why the 1/8-row predictions missed (>20%)
48|
49|The traffic model held (32 rows: 41.8 vs 36 predicted, +16%), but the fixed
50|cost is ~24 µs, not one 6.81 µs launch. The verdict itself proves it: the
51|reference's 12 kernels measure 36.1 µs/layer at 1 row, i.e. ~3 µs each in
52|this harness — far below the 6.81 µs whole-step figure from
53|`step_parts.txt:2` that I used. So per-launch cost in the piece-timing
54|harness (20 calls enqueued, one GPU wait, ÷20) is small, and my single
55|kernel's 28.5 µs is dominated by fixed per-harness cost: one wavefront on a
56|16-core GPU (single threadgroup at 1 row), MLX `metal_kernel` dispatch +
57|command encoding per call, and the amortized eval/wait. Consistent with this,
58|8 rows (23.6 µs) is *faster* than 1 row (28.5 µs): more threadgroups amortize
59|the fixed cost better, the opposite of a traffic model.
60|
61|Consequence for the saving: piece-timing saving vs the reference at 1 row is
62|(36.1−28.5)×20 = 0.15 ms/step, not the 0.9 ms the knock-out scaling
63|predicted — the knock-out (1.02 ms) and the piece harness (0.72 ms) disagree
64|on the slot's standalone cost, and G3 decides which one the fused kernel
65|actually cashes. The compute itself (92k FLOP/row, 60-element scan) is
66|negligible either way; further work on this slot should attack the ~24 µs
67|fixed floor (e.g. fewer, larger dispatches across layers is out of scope for
68|the slot — so nothing left here), not the kernel body.

1|# Territory: baseline-routing — the routing slot's starting point under bit-exact G2
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-routing
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:20:20Z
7|- **Next:** none — checklist filled for all pieces, ineff-baseline-routing-1..4 posted, grader and g3 notes folded
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|In every decode step and every prefill chunk, each of the 20 layers runs
12|`MoE.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`): cast the
13|layer input to float32, multiply by the router weight transposed, sigmoid, add the
14|expert bias only for selection, take the top-4 experts per row, gather their
15|*unbiased* scores, normalise them (divide by their sum + 1e-20) and scale by 2.5.
16|The slot outputs `inds` [rows,4] uint32 and `weights` [rows,4] float32; `inds`
17|feeds the experts slot, `weights` feeds combine, which sums the 4 (expert,
18|weight) pairs *in the emitted order* — which is why round 2's G2 requires the
19|same experts, the same weights and the same order, bit for bit
20|(`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:25-27`,
21|`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:119-121`).
22|
23|The starting point is round 1's `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1`: one fused
24|Metal kernel per layer (`block-0.metal`, 78 lines; `spec.json`: one kernel
25|`fused_routing`, grid `rows*32`, threadgroup 32). One threadgroup per row stages
26|`x[row]` (768 bfloat16→float32) in threadgroup memory, each of the 32 threads
27|computes 1–2 experts' 768-term dot products serially, writes
28|`sigmoid(acc)` to `scores[60]`, and thread 0 alone does a serial insertion
29|top-4 scan over the biased scores and writes `inds`/`weights`
30|(`block-0.metal:10-78`).
31|
32|## The headline finding (details in ineff-baseline-routing-1 and -2)
33|
34|Under the new grader the starting point fails G2 at **every** size while the
35|experts and their order always match (`rows_other_experts` 0 everywhere):
36|rows differing 20/159/638 at decode 1/8/32 rows (of 20/160/640 rows summed over
37|20 layers — 100% / 99.4% / 99.7% of rows) and 2,518/16,187/32,743 at prefill
38|127/1,016/2,048 rows (of 2,540/20,320/40,960 — 99.1% / 79.7% / 79.9%), max
39|relative error 2.6e-06 at decode and up to 8.7e-06 in the prefill
40|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`, quoted in
41|`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/README.md:39`). The experts match because
42|selection is insensitive to last-bit score differences (no captured row is a
43|near-tie at the 4th/5th place); the weights expose every last-bit difference
44|in the 4 selected scores. Section 3 below pins down, op by op, which of the
45|reference's operations the kernel reproduces exactly and which it does not:
46|**the divergence is in the scores — the router matmul's float32 accumulation
47|order (which changes with `rows`) and MLX's sigmoid formula — not in the
48|4-term weight sum, whose order the kernel already matches.**

151|### 3. Op-by-op: where the kernel's arithmetic matches the reference's, and where it does not
152|
153|#### 3.1 The router product `x.astype(f32) @ w_router.T` — DOES NOT MATCH (main cause)
154|
155|The kernel accumulates each expert's dot product **serially, in one thread,
156|in increasing `d` order**: `acc += xsh[d] * w_router[wbase + d]` for
157|`d = 0..767` (`block-0.metal:31-34`; the Metal compiler may contract each
158|mul+add to an FMA, but the grouping stays a 768-long left-to-right chain).
159|
160|The reference never does that. `Matmul::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4,
161|`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, fetched 2026-11-04) sees A = `x` [rows,768]
162|f32 (not transposed), B = `w_router.T` [768,60] (transposed view), so
163|`transpose_a=false, transpose_b=true`, M=rows, N=60, K=768:
164|
165|- **rows = 1 → GEMV.** `min(M,N)==1` routes to `gemv`
166|  (matmul.cpp, `Matmul::eval_gpu`); the `gemv_wide` shortcut is skipped
167|  because the output is float32 (`gemv_wide_config` requires float16/bfloat16
168|  out). Dispatch picks `GEMVKernel<float, BM=4, BN=1, SM=1, SN=32, TM=4,
169|  TN=4>`: each output is accumulated by one simdgroup whose 32 lanes each
170|  serially sum 24 products — lane `l` takes `d = i*128 + l*4 + (0..3)` for
171|  `i = 0..5` (`kernels/gemv.h:162-182`) — and the 32 partials are then combined
172|  by a shuffle tree, `result += simd_shuffle_down(result, sn)` for
173|  sn = 16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`). Grouping: 32 blocked partials + pairwise
174|  tree, not a serial chain.
175|- **rows = 8, 32, 127 → steel split-K GEMM.** In `steel_matmul_axpby` the
176|  split-K case fires when `_tm*_tn <= 2048` (this device's architecture string
177|  ends in `s`; brief:99 names it `applegpu_g13s`), `_tk = 768/16 = 48 >= 8`
178|  and `K >= max(M,N)` (matmul.cpp, Case 1). `steel_gemm_splitk_axpby` uses
179|  BM=16 (M<40) or 32, BN=32, BK=16, WM=WN=2 (steel/gemm split-K dispatch):
180|  partitions = min(max(2, next_pow2(48/(_tm*_tn))), 32) with
181|  `_tm=(M+31)/32, _tn=2` → **32 partitions at rows 8 and 32** (the last
182|  partition also absorbs the remaining 16 BK-iterations,
183|  `steel/gemm/kernels/steel_gemm_splitk.h:140-155`), **8 partitions at rows
184|  127**. Each partition accumulates its K-slice with simdgroup 8×8 matrix
185|  multiply-accumulate over BK=16 chunks in order (GEMMKernel/mma in
186|  `steel/gemm/gemm.h`, `mma.h`), writes a float32 partial, and
187|  `gemm_splitk_accum` sums the partials sequentially in partition order
188|  (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`).
189|- **rows = 1,016, 2,048 → regular steel GEMM.** Split-K no longer fires
190|  (768 < M), so `steel_matmul_regular_axpby` runs with the device tile from
191|  `GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` (for an architecture ending in `s` the macro's fallback:
192|  BM=64, BN=64, BK=16, WM=2, WN=2): K is walked in BK=16 chunks staged through
193|  threadgroup memory, accumulated by simdgroup matrix ops chunk after chunk.
194|
195|So the reference has **three different float32 accumulation orders for the
196|same mathematical product, selected by `rows`** — and none of them is the
197|kernel's serial order. Every score therefore differs from the reference's in
198|the last bits with high probability, which is exactly the observed pattern:
199|~100% of decode rows and ~80–99% of prefill rows have at least one differing
200|weight, while no row picks different experts (the biased-score gaps at the
201|4th/5th place are far larger than 1-ULP score noise on these inputs).
202|The drop from ~100% (decode, GEMV/split-K regimes) to ~80% (1,016/2,048,
203|regular GEMM) is consistent with a per-regime last-bit flip rate; that last
204|step is an inference from the counts, not a measurement.
205|A scalar re-implementation cannot reproduce the steel regimes' rounding by
206|reordering a serial loop: within each 8×8 simdgroup matrix op the 8-product
207|accumulation is the hardware's. A bit-exact candidate must either reuse
208|`simdgroup_float8x8` multiply-accumulate with the same tiling/K-order per
209|regime (branching on `rows` inside the kernel, or one kernel per regime in
210|the spec), or find an accumulation that provably rounds identically — none
211|is known.
212|
213|#### 3.2 The sigmoid — DOES NOT MATCH (independent second cause)
214|
215|Kernel (`block-0.metal:35`): `1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))` — the fast
216|(non-`precise`) `exp`, applied to `-acc`, one division.
217|
218|Reference (`mx.sigmoid` → `Sigmoid` in
219|`mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`, installed headers):
220|
221|```metal
222|auto y = 1 / (1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(x)));
223|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;
224|```
225|
226|Three differences, each able to move the result by 1 ULP: (a) `precise::exp`
227|vs `metal::exp`; (b) the argument is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0`
228|the result is `1 - y` (a subtraction that rounds) instead of the direct
229|division the kernel computes for all signs. Even a kernel whose matmul
230|matched bit for bit would still fail G2 on sigmoid alone for a large share
231|of scores. The fix is free in time: copy this formula verbatim.
232|
233|#### 3.3 Selection, gather, and the weight normalisation — MATCH
234|
235|- `scores + bias`: one f32 add in both (`block-0.metal:45`;
236|  `binary_ops.h:10-15`).
237|- Selection: the kernel's strictly-greater insertion scan emits descending
238|  biased order, earliest index winning ties (`block-0.metal:44-61`). The
239|  reference's argpartition is a full sort of `-(scores+bias)`
240|  (round-1 note, `ineff-runs-2.md:94-98`); on all six graded sizes the emitted
241|  sets *and* order agree (`rows_other_experts` 0, and the grader's worst-row
242|  examples show identical expert lists, grade-exact-routing.json). This is
243|  the part of Claude's round-1 reading ("the reference's order of
244|  operations … differ", round-2 README:39) that does **not** need fixing —
245|  but a builder must preserve the exact tie behaviour, since G2 now also
246|  compares order (`check_candidate.py:120`).
247|- The 4-term sum: the reference's `w.sum(axis=-1)` on a [rows,4] f32 array
248|  takes `row_reduce_small` (row_size 4 <= 64, MLX v0.32.4
249|  `mlx/backend/metal/reduce.cpp`, `row_reduce_general_dispatch` Case 1) in its
250|  per-thread branch (`non_row_reductions=1 < 32 && row_size <= 8`,
251|  `row_reduce_small` dispatch), i.e. `thread_reduce` with `N_READS=4`
252|  (`defines.h:12`): `total = (((0 + w0) + w1) + w2) + w3` in memory order —
253|  and `w`'s memory order is the `inds` order from argpartition, the same
254|  sequence the kernel sums as `s0 + s1 + s2 + s3` (`block-0.metal:64-68`;
255|  `kernels/reduction/reduce_row.h:164-181`). The kernel then adds `1e-20f`
256|  inside the same expression (`denom = s0+s1+s2+s3 + 1e-20f`), the reference
257|  as a separate add after the reduction (`slots.py:48`) — same association,
258|  and in float32 `sum + 1e-20` equals `sum` for any sum above ~1e-27, so the
259|  epsilon cannot be the cause either. Division and ×2.5 are the same single
260|  ops (`binary_ops.h:43-48,208-213`; `block-0.metal:74-77`).
261|  **Conclusion:** once the 4 selected scores are bit-equal and in the same
262|  order, the weights are bit-equal. Builders should spend their effort on
263|  3.1 and 3.2, not on the normalisation — the opposite emphasis to round 2
264|  README:39's example list, which names "the float32 sum order of
265|  `x @ w_router.T` and of `w.sum(...)`" as co-equal suspects.

1|# Inefficiency: the router product's float32 accumulation order matches MLX at no row count
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-routing
4|- **Status:** confirmed
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:23:45Z
7|- **Next:** verifier to confirm the three dispatch regimes against MLX v0.32.4 `matmul.cpp`
8|
9|## Slot
10|
11|`routing`
12|
13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:31-34`)
16|computes each of the 60 router scores as one thread's serial float32 chain,
17|`acc += xsh[d] * w_router[e*768 + d]` for d = 0..767 (compiler FMA contraction
18|does not change the left-to-right grouping). The reference,
19|`mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`),
20|never accumulates that way. In MLX 0.32.4's `Matmul::eval_gpu`
21|(`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, tag v0.32.4) with M=rows, N=60, K=768,
22|A not transposed, B transposed, the accumulation order is chosen by `rows`:
23|
24|| rows | MLX kernel | float32 accumulation order |
25||---|---|---|
26|| 1 | GEMV `gemv_float32_bm4_bn1_sm1_sn32_tm4_tn4` (`min(M,N)==1` → `gemv`; `gemv_wide` skipped, f32 out) | 32 lanes × serial 24 products (lane l: d = i*128 + l*4 + 0..3, i=0..5, `kernels/gemv.h:162-182`), then shuffle tree sn=16,8,4,2,1 (`gemv.h:202-208`) |
27|| 8, 32, 127 | steel split-K GEMM (Case 1: `_tm*_tn <= 2048` on this `…s` device, `_tk=48 >= 8`, `K >= max(M,N)`) | 32 K-partitions (8/32 rows) or 8 (127 rows); each partition: simdgroup 8×8 MMA over BK=16 chunks (BM=16/32, BN=32); partials summed sequentially in partition order (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`); last partition absorbs the remainder iterations (`splitk.h:140-155`) |
28|| 1,016, 2,048 | regular steel GEMM (split-K off: 768 < M) | BM=64/BN=64/BK=16 tiles (`GEMM_TPARAM_MACRO` fallback for `…s`), K walked in BK=16 chunks, simdgroup MMA accumulation chunk after chunk |
29|
30|A serial scalar loop cannot reproduce the two MMA regimes' rounding by
31|reordering: the 8-product accumulation inside each `simdgroup_float8x8`
32|multiply-accumulate is the hardware's. Bit-exactness therefore needs either
33|the same simdgroup matrix ops with the same tiling and K-order per regime
34|(branch on `rows`, or separate spec kernels), or a proof that another order
35|rounds identically (none known). Full derivation:
36|`territory-baseline-routing.md` section 3.1.
37|
38|## Cost
39|
40|This is a correctness gate, not a speed cost: it makes G2 fail at every size,
41|so the slot's fused-kernel saving can never be banked. Measured
42|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`): rows
43|differing 20/159/638 at decode 1/8/32 rows (100%/99.4%/99.7% of the
44|20/160/640 rows over 20 layers) and 2,518/16,187/32,743 at prefill
45|127/1,016/2,048 (99.1%/79.7%/79.9% of 2,540/20,320/40,960); experts and
46|order always match (`rows_other_experts` 0); max relative error 2.6e-06
47|decode, 8.7e-06 prefill. In time terms the blocked amount is the whole
48|fused-vs-compiled headroom below.
49|
50|## Kind
51|
52|Overhead-bound slot blocked by a correctness (rounding-order) cause; in the
53|terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md` the slot itself is overhead-bound (1.02 ms/step
54|at 1 row for ~4 MB, `ineff-runs-2` confirmed).
55|
56|## Spans
57|
58|`baseline-routing`; feeds `baseline-experts` and `baseline-combine` (both
59|consume this slot's outputs in the model).
60|
61|## Predicted saving
62|
63|Removing this cause (an exact product at the starting point's speed) unlocks
64|the fused kernel's measured gap to the compiled reference. Independent piece
65|timing (Claude re-grade, `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:47`): candidate
66|25.3/24.3/68.9 vs compiled 31.5/42.7/87.6 µs/layer → 6.2/18.4/18.7 µs/layer ×
67|20 layers = **0.12 / 0.37 / 0.37 ms per step at 1/8/32 rows**. Caveats, both
68|measured: the round-2 bar is the *chained* timing, for which no routing
69|figure exists yet (round-2 README:36), and end-to-end the starting point is
70|~0.41 ms/step *slower* than the compiled reference at 1 request (G3:
71|+0.185 vs −0.220 ms, `muse-round-1.md:85-86`), so at 1 row exactness alone
72|banks nothing — it must arrive with the occupancy fix in
73|`ineff-baseline-routing-3`. The exact product itself may cost more than the
74|serial loop (MMA tiling at decode sizes has little work to amortise); the
75|saving above is the headroom it makes claimable, not a promise.
76|

78|

1|# Inefficiency: the kernel's sigmoid rounds differently from MLX's at every score
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-routing
4|- **Status:** confirmed
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:24:18Z
7|- **Next:** verifier to confirm against installed `unary_ops.h:308-314`
8|
9|## Slot
10|
11|`routing`
12|
13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point computes `scores[e] = 1.0f / (1.0f + metal::exp(-acc))`
16|(`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/block-0.metal:35`): the fast
17|(non-`precise`) Metal `exp` of `-acc`, then one division, for all signs.
18|The reference's `mx.sigmoid` (`bench/grader/slots.py:45`) is MLX's unary
19|`Sigmoid` (`mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/unary_ops.h:308-314`,
20|installed MLX 0.32.4):
21|
22|```metal
23|auto y = 1 / (1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(x)));
24|return (x < 0) ? y : 1 - y;
25|```
26|
27|Three rounding differences, each independently able to move a score by
28|1 ULP: (a) `metal::precise::exp` vs `metal::exp`; (b) the exponent argument
29|is `|x|`, never negative; (c) for `x >= 0` the result is the subtraction
30|`1 - y` rather than a direct division. With 60 scores per row and 4 selected,
31|even a bit-exact matmul behind this sigmoid would still leave most rows
32|differing — this cause is independent of `ineff-baseline-routing-1`, and
33|both must be fixed for G2. (That the 4-term weight sum is *not* a third
34|cause is shown in `territory-baseline-routing.md` section 3.3.)
35|
36|## Cost
37|
38|Correctness only; no time cost. It contributes to the same measured failure
39|as ineff-baseline-routing-1: rows differing 20/159/638 (decode) and
40|2,518/16,187/32,743 (prefill), max relative error up to 8.7e-06
41|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-routing.json`). The split
42|of blame between this entry and the matmul order cannot be measured without
43|a candidate that fixes one of them; the grader's worst-row examples show
44|individual selected weights alternately equal and 1-ULP-off within one row
45|(e.g. prefill 127, layer 0 row 0: three weights equal, the fourth off by
46|3e-08 relative), consistent with per-score last-bit flips from either cause.
47|
48|## Kind
49|
50|Overhead-bound slot blocked by a correctness (rounding-formula) cause.
51|
52|## Spans
53|
54|`baseline-routing`
55|
56|## Predicted saving
57|
58|Zero µs directly — copying MLX's formula verbatim is the same instruction
59|count class (one `exp`, one division, one conditional subtract). Its value
60|is that it is a *necessary* half of unlocking the fused-vs-compiled headroom
61|quantified in `ineff-baseline-routing-1` (0.12/0.37/0.37 ms per step at
62|1/8/32 rows on the independent timing): with the matmul fixed and this left
63|in place, G2 still fails at essentially every row and the saving stays 0.
64|

66|

{"path":"muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-2/notes.md","content":"# Attempt 2 (round 2) — builder-2-b, direction (b): minimal-change scalar exact fix

Starting point: `muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1` (single kernel, one
32-thread threadgroup per row). That starting point fails G2 at every size
under round 2's bit-exact grader (product accumulation order +
sigmoid formula; see `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-routing.md`
§3.1–3.2). Baseline for this slot: `none`, so there is no `beats_baseline`
bar; the bar is the compiled reference.

## What changed (only the scores)

Kept exactly as attempt-1: one kernel, grid `rows*32`, threadgroup 32, one
threadgroup per row, `x` staged in threadgroup memory, thread `t` computes
experts `t` and `t+32`, thread 0's serial strictly-greater top-4 insertion
scan (same tie rule), and the weights sum `s0+s1+s2+s3 + 1e-20f`, divide,
×2.5 in `inds` order. Changed only how each expert's score is computed:

1. **Sigmoid, MLX verbatim** (`unary_ops.h:308-314`):
   `y = 1/(1 + metal::precise::exp(metal::abs(acc)))`,
   `scores[e] = (acc < 0) ? y : 1 - y`. Removes `ineff-baseline-routing-2`.
2. **Product accumulation reordered scalar-wise, no MMA intrinsics:**
   - `rows == 1` (GEMV regime): 32 lane partials, lane `l` serially sums
     `d = i*128 + l*4 + 0..3` for `i = 0..5` (`gemv.h:162-182`), then the
     shuffle tree `sn = 16,8,4,2,1` (`gemv.h:202-208`) emulated in place on
     the partial array (ascending `l` reads `lane_part[l+sn]` before it is
     overwritten in that round).
   - `rows > 1` (split-K regime): 32 partitions of BK=16 chunks —
     partitions 0..30 cover 16 elements each, partition 31 covers the
     remaining 272 (steel split-K at 8/32 rows: `gemm_k_iterations =
     (768/16)/32 = 1`, `split_k_partition_size = 16`, last partition absorbs
     the rest, `steel_gemm_splitk.h:140-155`). Each partial is summed
     scalar-wise in increasing `d`; partials are summed sequentially in
     partition order from 0, as in `gemm_splitk_accum`
     (`steel_gemm_splitk.h:186-189`).

This is the controlled test of whether scalar reordering can be bit-exact:
at 1 row the GEMV grouping is fully scalar (lane serial sums + shuffle
tree), so it should reproduce the reference if FMA contraction matches;
at 8/32 rows the partition boundaries and sequential partial sum are exact,
but each partition's internal accumulation in MLX is an 8×8 simdgroup MMA
whose 8-product hardware accumulation a scalar loop may not reproduce
(`ineff-baseline-routing-1`). Note this attempt deliberately does **not**
reproduce MLX's partition count at 127 rows (8 partitions) or the regular
steel GEMM at 1,016/2,048 rows — direction (b) fixes 32 partitions at all
larger rows, so those sizes test the same scalar question less cleanly.

## Inefficiency removed

`ineff-baseline-routing-2` (sigmoid, fully) and, if scalar reordering
rounds identically, `ineff-baseline-routing-1` (product order). It does not
touch `ineff-baseline-routing-3` (one simdgroup per row + serial scan) or
`-4` (`w_router` re-read per row) — minimal change by design.

## Prediction (µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows)

Same flop count as attempt-1 (768 multiply-adds per expert) and same
traffic (`rows × 184 KB` of `w_router`). Extra work per expert: 32 partial
stores + 31 tree/partition adds (≈8% more adds) and one `precise::exp`
instead of fast `exp` (60 per row, negligible). Attempt-1 measured
28.5 / 23.6 / 41.8 µs per layer in its own (round-1, unchained) grader run
(`muse-spark/kernels/routing/attempt-1/notes.md:35-37`), so ×1.08:

- 1 row: **≈31 µs** (compiled reference 30.5 in that run)
- 8 rows: **≈25 µs** (compiled 42.0)
- 32 rows: **≈45 µs** (compiled 49.1)

Round 2's chained timing may shift all figures; the prediction is against
attempt-1's harness numbers. G2 prediction: pass at 1 row; fail at 8/32 if
(and only if) the MMA internal accumulation differs from a scalar serial
sum within each partition.

## Verdict

*(pending grader run)*

62|
63|Neighbour code is unchanged: post-attention layernorm → `x`; router →
64|`inds`, `weights`; `experts(x, inds)` → `y`; `shared_expert(x)` independent;
65|combine pairs `y[r,j]` with `weights[r,j]` positionally → residual
66|(`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`;
67|`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119,105-118`). What changed is the invocation
68|domain: the same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill first chunk, so the slot
69|is now called at the prefill row counts above with the same expectations —
70|`inds` any order, values in [0,60); `y` exact shape/dtype, positional
71|(`bench/grader/slots.py:217-218,231-254`;

74|### What must stay identical — changed: bit-exact, with two arithmetics
75|
76|- **Tolerance removed.** Round 1 allowed every element within 2 bfloat16
77|  ULP; now every element must equal the reference bit for bit
78|  (`differ == 0` in every layer at all six sizes;
79|  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:186-188`;
80|  `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:90-99,153-169,172-175,308`).
81|  `max_ulp` is diagnostic only (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`).
82|- **Summation order and dequantization are no longer free.** Round 1
83|  allowed any fp32 summation/dequantization order; that line is superseded.
84|  The reference itself changes kernel at `rows >= 60` — dispatch
85|  `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4` with `B = rows*4`, `E = 60`,
86|  i.e. `B >= 240` (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`
87|  §A; `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:22-32`).
88|  Sorting from `inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16 is a distinct, earlier
89|  threshold and does not switch the kernel: decode 32 rows is sorted and
90|  still `gather_qvm` (`bench/grader/slots.py:62`;
91|  `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:181`).
92|
93|  | Rows | Reference kernel | Weight value | K accumulation |
94|  |---|---|---|---|
95|  | < 60 (all decode) | `gather_qvm` | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 through the product (`qouter`) | strided lanes `k≡lane (mod 32)` serial, then `simd_sum` tree |
96|  | ≥ 60 (all tested prefill) | `gather_qmm_rhs` | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup `Ws` before the multiply (`dequantize`: `static_cast<bfloat16>(s·q+b)`) | contiguous 8-wide frag dots, sequential over `BK=32` tiles (`BlockMMA`, `AccumType=float`) |
97|
98|  Sources: `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`
99|  §D (dequant rounding), §E (MMA order), §F (side-by-side table);
100|  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md` §F.
101|  Either difference alone breaks bit-equality (down outputs near
102|  cancellation amplify a 1-ULP hidden flip, round-1 boundary builders'
103|  notes; measured 62.4–62.6% differ, max 43/65/110.5 ULP at prefill,
104|  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:62-71`).
105|  A size branch is therefore required — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
106|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic at/above — branched on `rows >= 60` from the
107|  dispatch source, not on the grader's bracketing sizes 32/127; rows
108|  33–59 in the real model still run `qvm`
109|  (`territory-quantized-kernels.md` §F conclusion). Row *grouping* inside
110|  the prefill branch is free (padded rows occupy separate accumulators
111|  and are discarded); per-row K order is not
112|  (`territory-quantized-kernels.md` §C invariant, §E invariant).
113|- **Unchanged in kind, now exact:** each gate/up/down product still
114|  accumulates in float32 and rounds once to bfloat16; `silu(gate)*up` is
115|  still computed on those bfloat16 values and rounded to bfloat16 before
116|  down (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`; `bench/grader/slots.py:67-79`).

118|  reference paths, so it is not the divergence
119|  (`ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:56-58`). At prefill the gate/up values
120|  arriving at `swiglu` already differ by the two rows above.
121|- **Tie rule and pair order — unchanged, restated because G2 is exact:**
122|  this slot makes no 4th/5th-expert tie choice; it inherits routing's
123|  output as given and must accept any 4 valid ids per row in any order,
124|  including either side of a near-tie. The order of the 4 pairs is not
125|  free: `y[r,j]` must stay the output of expert `inds[r,j]`, because
126|  combine sums `y[...,j,:] * weights[...,j]` positionally
127|  (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52,116`;
128|  `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:230-232`). Routing's own
129|  ordered tie-exactness is the `routing` slot's contract
130|  (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:187`), not this slot's.
131|- **Starting point against this boundary:** attempt-4 replicates only
132|  `gather_qvm` — strided-lane `qvm_block` + `simd_sum`, float32 dequant
133|  `x·(s·q+bias)` (`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/block-1.metal:20-40`),
134|  full-bfloat16 silu (`block-0.metal:53-64`), one kernel with grid
135|  `rows*4` groups at every row count (`spec.json`; `block-0.metal:6`).
136|  Decode 1/8/32 therefore passes bit-exact and every prefill size fails
137|  (`ineff-baseline-experts-1.md:62-71`); closing that gap without losing
138|  the decode bits is this hypothesis's correctness work.
139|
140|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see — changed
141|
142|Checks (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): G1 is true only after the
143|whole six-size correctness loop completes without exception (`:306`);
144|per-layer shape/dtype faults fail G2 with G1 true (`:158-159,288-304`).

146|layers at decode 1/8/32 and prefill 127/1,016/2,048 (`:153-169,272-308`).

149|(`:178-213,309-337`); `beats_compiled` needs chained candidate <

153|exists this round (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md` §5).
154|What it still can't see (checked by hand later — *check an attempt*):
155|row counts between the six tested ones (2–7, 9–31, 33–126, 128–1,015,
156|1,017–2,047, >2,048), with both thresholds (sort 16, kernel switch 60)
157|only bracketed by tested sizes; prefill beyond the first chunk of seeded
158|128-token random prompts (later chunks, other lengths/distributions);
159|reads of unwritten threadgroup memory, thread-timing dependence, and
160|the 32 KB limit below; NaN-vs-NaN counts as equal (`:93`)
161|(`territory-grader.md`, *What the grader still cannot see* 1–6).

163|### The GPU limits — unchanged
164|
165|At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup (count enforced,
166|`bench/grader/slots.py:327-328`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:98`) and
167|32 KB of threadgroup memory (not enforced by `build` — verify by hand
168|from the Metal source; `territory-grader.md` §3). Starting point for
169|scale: 256 threads/group and 3,840 B threadgroup memory
170|(`muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4/spec.json`;
171|`block-0.metal:13-16`), valid at every row count including 8,192
172|threadgroups at 2,048 rows
173|(`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md` §C).
174|Any prefill branch must stay inside both limits at all six sizes.

176|## Builders

178|### builder-1-b — direction (b): branched single kernel, 512 threads/pair
179|
180|- Attempt: `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-1` (starting
181|  point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4`, copied qvm path).

183|  starting point's qvm arithmetic unchanged per block, widened to 512
184|  threads/pair (gate/up 1 wave, down 2 waves); at/above, per-pair

193|  scalar BK=32 mimic). `beats_compiled` false: wins 8/32 rows, loses
194|  1 row (104.3 vs compiled 77.6). Baseline `none` — no
195|  `wins_vs_baseline`/`beats_baseline`.
196|- Learned: threads-per-pair widening is nearly exhausted at 1 row
197|  (256→512 bought ~29 µs chained; prediction missed +23%). The binding
198|  limit is 4 threadgroups per call on 16 cores, which a fused per-pair
199|  kernel cannot raise; and territory §E's frag-tree warning did not
200|  bite — serial BK-order adds matched BlockMMA bitwise on all tested
201|  layers (see attempt notes).

203|### builder-1-a — direction (a): size-branched kernels, decode block-split
204|

206|  point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4`). Two kernels, each
207|  branched in-Metal on `rows >= 60`: gate/up kernel with one

211|  per-pair `qmm_block` (bfloat16-rounded dequantized weights,
212|  BK=32 sequential 8-wide `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` steps).

214|  (grader, this run): **103.6 / 326.8 / 887.6**, vs reference

216|  run. Starting point chained (other harness): 132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6.
217|- **G1 pass; G2 pass — differ 0, max_ulp 0.0 at all six sizes**

1|# attempt-1 (round 2): branched fused experts, 512 threads/pair (builder-1-b)
2|
3|Direction (b) on starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4`
4|(baseline `none` — no earlier attempt passes the current G2). One fused
5|kernel, one threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair, branched in-Metal
6|on `rows >= 60` (`x_shape[0]`, the `gather_qmm_rhs` dispatch threshold,
7|not the grader's bracketing sizes):
8|
9|- **Decode (`rows < 60`):** attempt-4's qvm arithmetic unchanged —
10|  `qvm_block` copied verbatim (strided lanes `k ≡ lane (mod 32)`,
11|  float32 dequant `x·(scale·q+bias)`, `simd_sum`), so every block's
12|  accumulation order is identical. The one change is width: 512
13|  threads/pair (16 simdgroups) instead of 256, so gate/up run their 12
14|  blocks in 1 wave (was 2) and down its 24 blocks in 2 waves (was 3):
15|  4 simd waves instead of 7, more blocks in flight per call. This is
16|  the ineff-baseline-experts-2 fix (1-row chained latency): at 1 row
17|  the call still has only 4 threadgroups, but each now keeps up to 16
18|  blocks in flight instead of 8.
19|- **Prefill (`rows >= 60`):** per-pair path with `gather_qmm_rhs`
20|  arithmetic — each weight dequantized to bfloat16 first
21|  (`bfloat(scale·q+bias)`, `qmm_accum` in block-1) and K accumulated
22|  contiguously in BK=32 tile order by a single thread per output (one
23|  output per lane, no `simd_sum`), mimicking BlockMMA's sequential
24|  tile order. Same silu (full-bfloat16, attempt-4's) and the same four
25|  bfloat16 rounding points (gate, up, hidden, down).
26|
27|Removes: ineff-baseline-experts-1 (the G2 gate — the branch supplies
28|the prefill arithmetic attempt-4 lacks) and attacks
29|ineff-baseline-experts-2 (1-row latency) without touching any block's
30|`simd_sum` order. ineff-baseline-experts-3 (per-pair re-reads) is
31|deliberately kept — round-1 evidence says grouped reads lose at this
32|duty cycle; per-pair reads at/above 60 rows are correctness-only cost
33|(prefill is untimed).
34|
35|Limits: 512 threads/group ≤ 1,024; threadgroup memory unchanged at
36|3,840 B (tg_x 768 + tg_gate/up/h 384×3 bfloat16) ≤ 32 KB. Valid at
37|every `rows` (grid `rows*2048` threads = `rows*4` groups of 512; the
38|branch is on the same `rows` the grid is built from).
39|
40|## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (chained, grader timing)
41|
42|Starting point chained (console-chain.txt, via ineff-baseline-experts-2):
43|132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6; reference chained 80.3 / 239.6 / 797.6. Bytes per
44|pair 552,960 B → 2.21 / 17.69 / 70.78 MB per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows.
45|
46|- **1 row: 85.** Latency-bound: attempt-4's 132.9 ≈ ~20 µs fixed
47|  (launch/link, x load, silu, barriers) + ~113 µs wave-serial; waves
48|  7 → 4 scale the serial part: 20 + 113×4/7 ≈ 85. Roughly the
49|  reference's 80.3 — closing most of the +52.6 gap.
50|- **8 rows: 165.** Streaming: 17.69 MB at ~107 GB/s (attempt-4 chained
51|  ran 100.6 GB/s; 16 in-flight blocks/group should add a little
52|  memory-level parallelism) → ~165.
53|- **32 rows: 565.** 70.78 MB at ~125 GB/s (attempt-4: 120.5 GB/s) →
54|  ~566. Risk noted: 512-thread groups halve resident groups per core;
55|  if occupancy binds instead, this lands nearer 590.
56|
57|G2 prediction: decode bit-exact (identical per-block math). Prefill
58|bit-exact only if BlockMMA's 8-wide fragment dots round like serial
59|float adds in BK order — territory-quantized-kernels §E warns they may
60|not; the dequant rounding (the larger of the two divergences) is
61|matched exactly either way.
62|
63|## Verdict
64|
65|G1 pass; **G2 pass at all six sizes, differ 0 / max_ulp 0.0 everywhere**
66|(decode 1/8/32 and prefill 127/1,016/2,048) — the branch works: decode
67|keeps attempt-4's bits, and the scalar prefill path (bfloat16 dequant +
68|serial BK=32 tile order) matched `gather_qmm_rhs` bit for bit on every
69|tested layer. Chained timing µs/layer (this run; candidate vs reference
70|vs compiled): **1 row 104.3 / 87.6 / 77.6 (loses both)**; 8 rows
71|193.3 / 231.2 / 235.7 (wins); 32 rows 535.7 / 820.6 / 791.6 (wins).
72|`beats_compiled` false — only the 1-row size misses. No baseline this
73|round (`none`), so no `wins_vs_baseline`/`beats_baseline`.
74|
75|Against the starting point's chained numbers (132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6,
76|different harness — indicative only): −22% at 1 row, +10% at 8 rows,
77|−9% at 32 rows.
78|
79|## Miss analysis (prediction 85 / 165 / 565, measured 104.3 / 193.3 / 535.7)
80|
81|1 row missed by +23% (over the 20% bar); 8 rows +17%; 32 rows −5%
82|(fast side). The wave-count model was wrong about what dominates at
83|1 row. Cutting waves 7 → 4 did help (132.9 → 104.3 vs the starting
84|point), but the residual is not wave-serial: with 4 pairs there are
85|only 4 threadgroups, so at most 4 of the 16 GPU cores can hold work no
86|matter how wide each group gets — the reference spreads 1 row over
87|24+24+48 small groups. The fixed remainder (launch/link on the chain,
88|tg_x load, 512-thread barriers, lane-0's serial 32-output stores per
89|block) also does not shrink with waves. Conclusion: threads-per-pair
90|widening is nearly exhausted as the 1-row lever (256 → 512 bought
91|~29 µs chained); the binding limit is threadgroups per call, which a
92|single fused per-pair kernel cannot raise — down needs the pair's full
93|hidden vector, so blocks cannot be split across groups without a
94|device-memory intermediate. The 8-row +17% miss has the same shape in
95|milder form: 512-thread groups halve resident groups per core vs
96|256-thread groups, costing more at 32 groups than the extra in-flight
97|blocks repay; at 128 groups (32 rows) the trade turns positive again.

9|## What it does
10|
11|This territory is MLX's `mx.gather_qmm` Metal kernels behind the `experts`
12|slot (`quantized.h`, `quantized_utils.h`, `utils.h` in the installed
13|0.32.4 headers, dispatch in MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp`). Round 1 mapped
14|it as decode-only: `affine_gather_qvm` runs at every decode size and
15|`affine_gather_qmm_rhs` was listed as never run
16|([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`](../../exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md)
17|§A/§C, frozen). Round 2 reopens it because the new G2 is bit-exact at
18|prefill sizes too: from 60 rows the reference switches to
19|`gather_qmm_rhs`, whose rounding is now on the correctness path at
20|prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows. This entry writes only what is new: the
21|prefill dispatch, the `qmm_rhs` arithmetic, and exactly how it diverges
22|from `qvm`. Decode facts that still hold are cited, not rewritten.

24|## The checklist
25|
26|### A. Dispatch — `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` (which kernel runs at each size)
27|

29|  served twin `SwitchGLU.__call__`
30|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:176-199`) both call
31|  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4,
32|  mode="affine", sorted_indices=do_sort)` three times per layer (gate,
33|  up, down), with `do_sort = inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16
34|  (`slots.py:62`, `switch_layers.py:181`). MLX is 0.32.4
35|  (`.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; print(mx.__version__)"`).
36|  Served weights are `[E, in, out]` via `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear`
37|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:142-184`), hence
38|  `transpose=False`; the `transpose=True` twin in `switch_layers.py:75-90`
39|  is not the served path.
40|- **Callees:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu`
41|  ([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1980-2094](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1980-L2094)).
42|  It shapes `K = x.shape(-1)`, `M = x.shape(-2)`,
43|  `N = out.shape(-1)`, `B = out.size()/M/N`,
44|  `E = w.size()/w.shape(-1)/w.shape(-2) = 60`,
45|  `vector_limit = 4` for `transpose=False` (`:2000-2005`). Branch order:
46|  (1) rhs fast path iff `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4`
47|  (`:2012-2031`); (2) else `gather_qmm` iff `M >= vector_limit`
48|  (`:2034-2054`); (3) else `gather_qmv` iff `transpose_` (`:2056-2075`);
49|  (4) else `gather_qvm` (`:2077-2094`). With `M=1` always (below),
50|  branch (2) never fires in this model.
51|- **Data / shapes at every grader size.** `x` reaching `gather_qmm` is
52|  `[B, 1, K]` with `B = rows*4`: `xx = expand_dims(x, (-2,-3))` then,
53|  when sorting, `_gather_sort` gathers to one row per pair
54|  (`slots.py:61-65`, `switch_layers.py:12-17`); hence `M = 1` and the
55|  `M` argument later passed to `gather_qmm_rhs` is `x.size()/K = B`
56|  (`:2013-2027`). Gate/up: `K=768, N=384`; down (input is the
57|  bfloat16 `silu*up` hidden): `K=384, N=768`.
58|
59|  | rows | B = rows·4 | B/E | sorted (`inds.size≥64`) | MLX kernel |
60|  |---|---|---|---|---|

62|  | 8 (decode) | 32 | 0.53 | no | `gather_qvm` |

150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive

163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =

165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows

171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).

177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,

182|  uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are random tokens, so this is
183|  the expected case, not a bound): useful row tiles
184|  `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` ≈ 60 / 300 / 540 at B = 508 / 4,064 /
185|  8,192, against dispatched `grid_y` 91 / 313 / 571 (§B). Weight

199|  a valid row's arithmetic (§E) — so a bit-exact replacement may

203|### D. Dequantization — `QuantizedBlockLoader` + `dequantize` (rounding point 1)
204|
205|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` with
206|  `QuantizedBlockLoader<T=bfloat16, BROWS=BK=32, BCOLS=BN=32,
207|  dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=0, tgp_size=64, group_size=32, bits=4>`
208|  (`quantized.h:2613-2621`); same loader family as `qmm_n`/`qmm_t`
209|  (§G).
210|- **Callees:** `load_unsafe`/`load_safe` (`quantized.h:736-770`) call
211|  `dequantize<T, pack_factor=2, bits=4>` (`quantized.h:557-663`,
212|  bits=4 at `:617-623`) per packed byte: with `s = float(scale)`,
213|  `b = float(bias)` it writes
214|  `w_local[2i] = (bfloat16)(s * (w[i] & 0x0f) + b)` and
215|  `w_local[2i+1] = (bfloat16)((s/16) * (w[i] & 0xf0) + b)` into
216|  threadgroup `Ws`. Scales: one `scale`/`bias` pair per thread from
217|  `scales + bi * N/32` (`:733-734`); `group_steps = 32/32 = 1`, so
218|  `next()` advances `scales/biases` by `32*N/32 = N` per K tile
219|  (`:772-790`) — exactly one scale group per `BN=32` output tile and
220|  per `BK=32` row of `K`, matching the `[E, K, N/32]` layout.
221|- **Data:** packed uint32 weights are viewed as bytes (`(device
222|  uint8_t*)w`); each byte yields 2 outputs (low/high nibble), each
223|  `BK×BN = 1,024`-element weight tile dequantized once per
224|  (row tile, K tile) visit into `Ws`, then read by the MMA (§E).
225|  `x` tiles by contrast are copied verbatim (bfloat16 → bfloat16,
226|  exact) by `BlockLoader` (`steel/gemm/loader.h:74-80`).
227|- **Neighbours:** this is the first of the two divergence points
228|  vs `qvm` (§F): the dequantized weight is **rounded to bfloat16
229|  before any multiply**. In `qvm` the same `scale*q + bias` value
230|  stays in float32 registers through the product.
231|- **Cost:** dequant element-ops per product per layer =
232|  `T × K × N` = `T × 294,912` (both products have `K·N = 294,912`):
233|  17.7M / 88.5M / 159.2M at the three prefill sizes (balanced `T`
234|  from §C), each a float mul+add, a float→bfloat round, and a
235|  threadgroup store+reload. This recompute-per-row-tile is the
236|  loader's design (no dequantized-weight cache exists; the full
237|  dequantized expert is 294,912 × 2 B = 590 KB, far above the
238|  32 KB threadgroup limit, so cross-tile reuse would need a device
239|  buffer and an extra kernel — not a free fix).
240|- **Invariants:** `scale`/`bias` themselves are bfloat16 values
241|  upcast to float exactly (bfloat→float is exact), identical to
242|  `qvm`'s inputs; the *only* added rounding is
243|  `static_cast<bfloat16>(s*q + b)`. Relative error up to half a
244|  bfloat ULP (≈2⁻⁹ ≈ 0.2%) per weight element, deterministic per
245|  `(expert, k, n)` — the same rounded weight is reused for all
246|  ≤16 rows of the tile, so errors are correlated across rows
247|  sharing an expert, unlike per-pair float weights.

249|### E. Accumulation — `BlockLoader` + `BlockMMA` (rounding point 2)
250|
251|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` instantiates
252|  `BlockMMA<bfloat16, bfloat16, BM=16, BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2,
253|  false, transpose=false, ...>` (`quantized.h:2599-2610`) and
254|  `BlockLoader<bfloat16, BM=16, BK=32, dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=1,
255|  tgp_size=64>` for `x` (`:2611-2612`).
256|- **Callees:** `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:439-537`) with
257|  `AccumType = float` by default (`mma.h:451`): accumulator
258|  fragments `Ctile` are `float` 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` tiles
259|  (`TM = 16/(8·1) = 2`, `TN = 32/(8·2) = 2` frags per simdgroup).
260|  `mma()` (`mma.h:513-537`) steps `kk` over `BK` in 8-wide frags
261|  (4 steps per tile), each `tile_matmad` issuing
262|  `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` (`mma.h:181-206, 406-427`).
263|  Operand fragments are loaded from threadgroup bfloat16 and
264|  widened to float (`BaseMMAFrag::load` casts, `mma.h:57-67`), so
265|  the multiply is float×float with float accumulate — but the
266|  weight operand is the already-bfloat-rounded value of §D, and
267|  the 8-term dot inside each frag is the hardware's tree order,
268|  not a serial FMA chain. `gemm_loop_*` then adds tile results
269|  sequentially over the 24/12 K tiles. Store:
270|  `store_result`/`store_result_safe` cast float → bfloat16 once
271|  (`mma.h:100-112, 540-592`; `quantized.h:2683, 2694`) — the same

274|  (rows zero-padded by `load_safe` when `tgp_bm < 16`,
275|  `loader.h:83-128`); `Ws` holds the §D dequantized tile. Partial-row
276|  tiles take the `gemm_loop_unaligned<false, true, ...>` branch
277|  (`quantized.h:2687-2695`) — full MMA work on padded rows, results
278|  discarded.
279|- **Neighbours:** identical bfloat16 store boundary as `qvm`, so
280|  the downstream `swiglu` (gate/up) and down product see the same
281|  *kind* of rounding point — only the float value arriving at the
282|  cast differs.
283|- **Cost:** per product, MMA flops are `2·B_padded·K·N` with
284|  `B_padded = T·16` = 960 / 4,800 / 8,640 vs useful `B` = 508 /
285|  4,064 / 8,192 (padded fractions in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
286|  At 5.2 TFLOPS peak (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:14`) the useful MMA
287|  floors at `2·B·K·N/5.2 TFLOPS` = 57.6 / 461.0 / 929.2 µs per
288|  layer-product (B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192) if it ran at peak — it
289|  cannot, at `BM=16` tiles with two barriers per 32-K step
290|  (`quantized_utils.h:14-29`), so the path is
291|  overhead/latency-bound, not compute-bound; no measured prefill
292|  time exists to check this against (§A).
293|- **Invariants:** per-output accumulation grouping is
294|  **[contiguous 8-wide frag dots] sequentially over BK=32 tiles**,
295|  in increasing K. This is the second divergence from `qvm` (§F):
296|  even with bit-identical weight operands, regrouping a 768-term
297|  float sum this way rounds differently on generic data. Reproducing
298|  it with scalar FMAs is not bit-safe; reproducing it requires the
299|  same 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` fragmentation (same `BK`, same
300|  frag step order) or a proof the hardware order coincides — none
301|  exists in the sources. Warp tiling `WM/WN` only partitions frags
302|  across simdgroups; it does not change a single output's add order.

304|### F. Comparator — `qvm_impl` + `qouter` (what decode runs; delta only)
305|
306|Round 1 §A mapped this kernel fully; only the contrast is new.
307|
308|- **Callers/Callees:** `gather_qvm` host (`quantized.cpp:1462-1529`)
309|  → `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`) → `qvm_impl`
310|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid `(1, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of
311|  64 threads; gate/up `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. Each lane owns
312|  one strided `K` element per 32-step (`x += block_size` with
313|  `block_size = 32`, `:1275-1287`) and accumulates 32 outputs in
314|  float registers via `qouter` (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 at
315|  `:503-509`): `result += x * (scale*q + bias)` with
316|  `scale`/`bias`/`x` all float, **no bfloat16 rounding of the
317|  weight**, serial per-lane adds in strided-K order
318|  (`k = lane, lane+32, ...`), then one `simd_sum` tree over the 32
319|  lane partials (`:1317-1321`) and a single float→bfloat16 store
320|  (`:1324-1329`).
321|- **The two divergences, side by side:**
322|
323|  | aspect | `gather_qvm` (decode, rows < 60) | `gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill, rows ≥ 60) |
324|  |---|---|---|
325|  | weight value | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup (§D) |
326|  | K grouping | strided lanes: lane `l` sums `k≡l (mod 32)` serially, then `simd_sum` tree | contiguous: 8-wide frag dots, sequential over BK=32 tiles (§E) |
327|  | rows sharing work | none: one grid slice per pair | ≤16 sorted rows share each weight tile |
328|  | final rounding | float → bfloat16 once after `simd_sum` | float → bfloat16 once after MMA — identical point |
329|
330|  Either divergence alone breaks bit-equality (measured: 62.4–62.6%
331|  of experts outputs differ at all three prefill sizes, max
332|  43/65/110.5 ULP, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-experts.json`;
333|  full statement in `ineff-baseline-experts-1`). A single arithmetic
334|  cannot match both kernels on generic inputs: pick any weight with
335|  `float(scale·q+bias)` not representable in bfloat16 and any
336|  `x ≠ 0` — the two references already disagree on that product
337|  before accumulation even starts. **Conclusion for builders: a
338|  size branch is required** — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
339|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic (bfloat-rounded dequant tiles + 8-wide frag
340|  accumulation) at/above 60 rows — or a proof of coincidence that
341|  the 62% differ rate rules out empirically. The branch threshold
342|  must be the dispatch rule `rows >= 60` (pairs `>= 240`, `E=60`),
343|  not the grader's nearest tested sizes 32/127: rows 33–59 in the
344|  real model still run `qvm` (§A). Row *grouping* inside the
345|  prefill branch is free (§C invariant); per-row accumulation is
346|  not.
347|- **Cost:** decode cost is round 1's confirmed entry
348|  (`muse-spark/exploration/ineff-quantized-kernels-1`, confirmed;
349|  round-2 restatement `ineff-baseline-experts-3`): 51 MB read in
350|  0.92 ms at 1 row (55 GB/s), 908 MB in 14.67 ms at 32 rows
351|  (62 GB/s, 31% of peak). Not re-posted here.
352|- **Invariants:** both paths accumulate in float32 and round to
353|  bfloat16 exactly once per product; `silu(gate)·up` is computed on
354|  those bfloat16 values and rounded again before down (brief:
355|  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). Any candidate must keep all
356|  four bfloat16 points (gate, up, hidden, down) — matching only the
357|  final `y` rounding is insufficient, since 1-ULP hidden flips
358|  amplify through down (round 1
359|  `muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md:103-108`).

389|
390|- **Feeds from:** switch-layers territory (sorted `idx`, `x` gathered
391|  to `[B, 1, K]`, the `right_sorted_` flag), model territory (router
392|  `inds` before that).
393|- **Feeds to:** other-kernels territory (compiled `swiglu` between
394|  the products), switch-layers (`_scatter_unsort`), then combine.
395|- **Slot view:** `baseline-experts` territory owns the starting
396|  point kernel that must branch (§F conclusion);
397|  `ineff-baseline-experts-1` owns the G2-failure statement. This
398|  territory owns why the two MLX arithmetics differ and what the
399|  reference itself wastes at prefill (§C, inefficiencies below).

401|## Inefficiencies
402|
403|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (open): `BM=16` row-tile quantization
404|  in `gather_qmm_rhs` — dispatched empty tiles plus zero-padded
405|  rows waste 47% / 15% / 5% of row work at prefill 127 / 1,016 /
406|  2,048 rows. Prefill-only; 0 µs at decode sizes.
407|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-2` (open): `gather_mm_offsets` recomputed

9|## What it does
10|
11|The `experts` slot of one MoE layer: for each row `r` and slot `j`, with
12|`e = inds[r, j]`, compute
13|`y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]`
14|(`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:84-88`; reference `bench/grader/slots.py:55-82`).
15|The starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4` is now the code in
16|the slot: one fused per-pair Metal kernel
17|(`block-0.metal` + header `block-1.metal`, launched by `spec.json`) that
18|replicates MLX `affine_gather_qvm` bitwise. It is bit-exact at decode sizes
19|and fails the new G2 at every prefill size, and it loses chained at 1 row
20|while winning chained at 8/32 rows. Round 1 mapped the same code path in
21|`muse-spark/exploration/territory-switch-layers.md` and
22|`territory-quantized-kernels.md`; this entry cites them where they still
23|hold and writes only what is new: the starting point as slot code, the
24|chained-timing reversal at 1 row, and the prefill kernel switch.

1|# attempt-2: size-branched block-split experts (builder-1-a, direction a)
2|
3|First attempt in direction (a) for `hyp-1-experts-exact`. Builds on the
4|starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4` (baseline: none;
5|attempt-4 fails the current G2 at every prefill size). One spec, two
6|kernels in list order, each branching on `rows` read from
7|`inds_shape[0]` (the dispatch threshold `rows >= 60`, pairs >= 240,
8|from `territory-quantized-kernels` §A/§F, not the tested sizes):
9|
10|- `experts_gate_up` (block-0): one 32-thread threadgroup per
11|  (pair, 32-output block) — grid `rows*1536` threads = `rows*4*12`
12|  groups. Computes gate and up for its block, applies the silu-mul,
13|  writes `hidden[pair, block*32 + lane]`.
14|- `experts_down` (block-1): one 32-thread threadgroup per
15|  (pair, 32-output block) — grid `rows*3072` threads = `rows*4*24`
16|  groups. Reads `hidden`, writes its 32 outputs of `y`.
17|
18|Shared header (block-2): `qvm_block` copied byte-identically from
19|attempt-4, a new `qmm_block`, and attempt-4's full-bfloat16 silu.
20|
21|## What changed since attempt-4, and which inefficiency it removes
22|
23|1. **Prefill arithmetic (`ineff-baseline-experts-1`, the G2 gate).**
24|   Below 60 rows both kernels keep attempt-4's bit-exact `gather_qvm`
25|   arithmetic (float32 dequant through the product, strided lanes
26|   `k == lane (mod 32)` + `simd_sum`, full-bf16 silu). At 60 rows and
27|   above, `qmm_block` replicates `gather_qmm_rhs`: dequantized
28|   weights rounded to bfloat16 before the multiply
29|   (`dequantize` bits=4, `s` / `s/16` nibble form), then BK=32 tiles
30|   in increasing K order, each four sequential 8-wide
31|   `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` steps on float fragments — the
32|   `BlockMMA` order. Row grouping is per-pair (fragment row 0, seven
33|   zero-padded rows in separate accumulators), which the boundary
34|   allows; per-row K order is unchanged. Gate/up/down each still
35|   round once from float32 to bfloat16, and the silu is shared.
36|2. **Chained 1-row latency (`ineff-baseline-experts-2`).** Attempt-4
37|   exposes 4 threadgroups per call at 1 row (one per pair) with
38|   barrier-serialised waves. Here a 1-row call exposes 48 (gate/up)
39|   + 96 (down) threadgroups, each computing exactly one 32-output
40|   block with the identical strided-lane + `simd_sum` order, so the
41|   GPU's 16 cores all have work while no block's bits change. Cost:
42|   a second launch per layer and one `hidden` round-trip (3 KB per
43|   pair); `x` is re-read from cache once per block (12x per pair,
44|   18 KB vs 369 KB of gate/up weights per pair).
45|3. `ineff-baseline-experts-3` (per-pair weight re-reads) is **not**
46|   removed: weight bytes per pair stay 552,960 B, as in attempt-4.
47|   The 8/32-row chained wins must therefore be kept by occupancy,
48|   not by fewer bytes.
49|
50|Boundary kept: bit-exact accumulation order per size regime as
51|above; all four bfloat16 rounding points (gate, up, hidden, down);
52|positional `y[r,j]` for any `inds` order; valid at every `rows`
53|(grid and block counts scale with `rows*4` pairs, branch only on
54|the 60-row dispatch threshold); 32 threads/group <= 1024;
55|threadgroup memory by hand (grader does not check 32 KB): GU
56|1536 + 128 + (256+1024+256)*4 = 7,808 B; Down 768 + 6,144 =
57|6,912 B.
58|
59|## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (chained, this grader)
60|
61|Weight bytes per layer (552,960 B/pair): 2.21 / 17.7 / 70.8 MB at
62|4 / 32 / 128 pairs. Attempt-4 chained (round-2 exploration,
63|`console-chain.txt`): 132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6; reference chained
64|80.3 / 239.6 / 797.6.
65|
66|- 1 row: 144 small groups fill 16 cores; gate/up 1.47 MB + down
67|  0.74 MB at an assumed ~55 GB/s effective for 32-thread groups
68|  gives ~40 µs including the extra launch → **40 µs**
69|  (attempt-4 chained 132.9; reference 80.3).
70|- 8 rows: 384 + 768 groups, streaming regime; 17.7 MB at
71|  ~110 GB/s ≈ 160 µs → **165 µs** (attempt-4 175.9).
72|- 32 rows: 1,536 + 3,072 groups; 70.8 MB at ~115 GB/s ≈ 615 µs
73|  → **610 µs** (attempt-4 587.6; the 4% block-split tax is the
74|  risk to the kept win).
75|
76|G2: expect `differ == 0` at all six sizes. Decode reuses
77|attempt-4's proven per-block math unchanged; prefill depends on
78|the hardware's 8-wide fragment dot matching `BlockMMA`'s when fed
79|the same bfloat16-rounded operands in the same tile order.
80|
81|## Verdict
82|
83|G1 pass; **G2 pass — `differ` 0, `max_ulp` 0.0 at all six sizes**
84|(decode 1/8/32 and prefill 127/1,016/2,048). The prefill branch is
85|bit-exact: bfloat16-rounded dequantized weights plus BK=32 tiles of
86|four sequential 8-wide `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` steps, fed a
87|single row per threadgroup, reproduce `gather_qmm_rhs` bit for bit
88|on every tested layer. `beats_compiled` false. Chained
89|µs/layer (candidate vs reference vs compiled, same run):
90|**103.6 / 326.8 / 887.6** vs 76.1 / 244.6 / 797.1 and
91|73.1 / 232.0 / 804.5. Baseline `none` — no
92|`wins_vs_baseline`/`beats_baseline`. The attempt is correct at
93|every size but slower than the compiled reference at all three
94|decode sizes, and slower than the starting point's chained times
95|(132.9 / 175.9 / 587.6, other harness) at 8/32 rows.
96|
97|## Miss analysis (prediction 40 / 165 / 610; all misses > 20%)
98|
99|Measured is 2.6x / 2.0x / 1.5x the prediction. Effective bandwidth
100|from 552,960 B/pair: 21 / 54 / 80 GB/s chained, against attempt-4's
101|chained 17 / 101 / 121 GB/s. The split helped exactly where group
102|count was the binding limit (1 row: 103.6 vs 132.9) and hurt
103|wherever streaming mattered. Two causes, both in the split shape,
104|not the arithmetic:
105|
106|1. **One simdgroup per group has too little memory parallelism.**
107|   Each 32-thread group runs its block's 24-step strided K loop
108|   alone; attempt-4 runs 8 such blocks concurrently per group, so
109|   one stalled load hides behind seven others. More groups only
110|   partly compensate: at 8/32 rows the GPU was already saturated
111|   with groups, and the per-group latency chain became the limit.
112|2. **Threadgroup memory caps residency in the decode branch too.**
113|   The qmm tiles (6,144 B of floats) are allocated in both kernels
114|   at every size, so a decode gate/up group carries 7,808 B where
115|   attempt-4 carries 3,840 B. Resident groups per core fall, and
116|   with 32-thread groups the resident thread count falls with
117|   them — the opposite of the occupancy the split was meant to add.
118|
119|Lesson for `ineff-baseline-experts-2`: exposing threadgroups is
120|not sufficient; a block-split kernel must keep several blocks in
121|flight per group (or per core) and keep decode threadgroup memory
122|near attempt-4's, e.g. 128-thread groups of 4 simdgroups each
123|owning one block (12 + 24 groups at 1 row), with the prefill tiles
124|overlaid on the decode buffers instead of added to them.
125|
126|**Next change:** rebuild the decode branch as 4-simdgroup groups
127|(4 blocks per group, qvm_block unchanged), overlay the qmm tile
128|memory on the decode threadgroup buffers, keep `qmm_block` as is.

32|}

35|]

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE

51|def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
53|

55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)

90|    return {

92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.

105|    def moe_call(self, x):

303|def build(spec, sources, slot):
304|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
305|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
306|    kernels = []

309|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
310|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
311|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
312|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
313|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
314|            header=header,
315|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
316|        )
317|        kernels.append((k, fn))
318|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
319|    if missing:
320|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")

323|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
324|        env = dict(inputs)
325|        for k, fn in kernels:
326|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
327|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
328|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
329|            outs = fn(
330|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
331|                template=[
332|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
333|                ],
334|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
335|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
336|                output_shapes=[
337|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
338|                ],
339|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
340|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
341|            )
342|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
343|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}

2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing chains the 20 layers, so
9|each call waits for the one before, as in a decode step. The grader prints
10|its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when given. It never writes into
11|the attempt folder, which holds only the Muse agent's files.

13|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
14|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
15|
16|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run as the
17|candidate, and adds `beats_baseline`. From round 2 on, the bar is the previous
18|round's final attempt for the slot (claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md).
19|The two are timed in alternating repeats, so drift in the GPU's clocks reaches
20|both alike, and the candidate beats the baseline at a row count only if it is
21|faster in at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats: a one-sided sign

25|routing+combine attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.

184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs

204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:
221|            call()
222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
228|    return times

143|### C. Metal kernel — `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` + `schedule_row_tile`
144|
145|- **Callers:** §B only. Instantiated for this model as
146|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs<bfloat16, group_size=32, bits=4, BM=16,
147|  BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2, transpose=false>`
148|  (`quantized.h:2570-2593`).
149|- **Callees:** `schedule_row_tile<BM=16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) maps
150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive
159|  `BlockMMA::mma` over `K_it = K/BK` tiles (24 gate/up, 12 down),
160|  with an extra `gemm_loop_finalize` only when `!align_K` — never
161|  here, since `K % 32 == 0` (`quantized.h:2631, 2676-2717`).
162|- **Data:** threadgroup memory `Xs[16 × 40]` + `Ws[32 × 40]` bfloat16
163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =
164|  40`, `quantized.h:2596-2597, 2623-2624`; padding is the usual
165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows
170|  `y_row .. y_row+tgp_bm-1` of the already-gathered `[B, K]` matrix;
171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).
175|- **Neighbours:** consumes the sorter's output order directly; this
176|  is the only gather kernel whose addressing depends on pair order
177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,
179|  so `_scatter_unsort` after the down product is load-bearing for
180|  position, not for bits.
181|- **Cost (arithmetic):** balanced-expert model (counts near the
182|  uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are random tokens, so this is
183|  the expected case, not a bound): useful row tiles
184|  `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` ≈ 60 / 300 / 540 at B = 508 / 4,064 /
185|  8,192, against dispatched `grid_y` 91 / 313 / 571 (§B). Weight
