9|## Slot
10|
11|`combine`.
12|
13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal:20-25`)
16|writes the 4-term f32 sum as one expression,
17|`float(y0)·w0 + float(y1)·w1 + float(y2)·w2 + float(y3)·w3`, then
18|`bfloat(acc) + shared`. Compiled as a single Metal kernel, the compiler
19|FP-contracts the mul+add pairs into FMAs, keeping each product unrounded
20|into its add. The reference can never do this: `ref_combine`
21|(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`) runs eagerly as separate kernels —
22|`binary_g` multiply (`Multiply` is plain `x * y`, product rounded once
23|to f32), then `col_reduce_small` (`Sum` is plain `a + b`, init 0) folding
24|((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ with a rounding after every add, then `copy_v` bf16
25|round, then `binary_vv` bf16 add (headers under
26|`.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`;
27|full mapping in `territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist B–D). The
28|candidate's `acc` therefore differs from the reference fold by ~1 f32
29|ULP on some elements; the bf16 rounding absorbs it except when `acc`
30|sits at a rounding midpoint, and the following `+ shared` can magnify
31|the reported gap when it cancels toward zero (ULP floored at
32|`|r| = 0.001`, `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`).
33|
34|This is contraction, not association: the candidate's written order is
35|already the reference's left fold, and round 1's CPU emulation showed
36|all 120 pure association trees give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches
37|to the grader fingerprint while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it
38|exactly (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The
39|2.0-ULP touch*). Attempt-2's explicit `acc += …` loop has the identical
40|fingerprint, so neither loop form nor staging avoids contraction — the
41|fix must suppress it (the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary
42|named there) while keeping the ((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ fold and both bf16
43|rounding points.
44|
45|Under round 2's bit-exact G2 (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md`)
46|the kernel fails at five of six sizes
47|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-combine.json`, summed
48|over 20 layers): decode 1 row 0 differ (pass), 8 rows **2** (max
49|2.0 ULP), 32 rows **2** (max 1.0 ULP); prefill 127 rows **6** (1.0),
50|1,016 rows **50** (16.0), 2,048 rows **130** (32.0). The count grows at
51|a roughly constant 3–16 ppm of rows·768·20 elements — the same lottery
52|sampled more times, not a prefill kernel switch (combine's kernels are
53|row-count-invariant; the 60-row experts switch cannot enter through
54|captured `y`). In the model, these differences changed 7 of 32 vLLM
55|sequences from token 0 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §2), which is
56|why the new G2 admits none.
57|
58|## Cost
59|
60|This inefficiency costs correctness, not time — FMA contraction is the
61|faster evaluation. Its cost is the slot's entire bankable saving: while
62|G2 fails, the grader never times the attempt
63|(`check_candidate.py:308-337`) and the kernel cannot be used at any
64|size. The forfeited saving against the compiled reference (old
65|independent piece timing, the only same-run basis available; Claude
66|re-grade, `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §1):
67|
68|| Rows | Compiled ref | Candidate | Gap ×20 layers |
69||---|---|---|---|
70|| 1 | 23.8 µs/layer | 18.6 µs/layer | 5.2 × 20 = **0.104 ms/step** |
71|| 8 | 26.1 µs/layer | 17.0 µs/layer | 9.1 × 20 = **0.182 ms/step** |
72|| 32 | 32.0 µs/layer | 18.9 µs/layer | 13.1 × 20 = **0.262 ms/step** |

74|End to end, combine attempt-1 alone saved 0.51 / 0.71 / 0.39 ms in vLLM

81|Overhead-bound slot (see `ineff-baseline-combine-2`); this entry is the
82|correctness gate on that saving, in the terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md`
83|an exactness blocker rather than a bandwidth/compute loss.

86|
87|`baseline-combine` (candidate arithmetic), `grader` (bit-exact G2 at
88|six sizes). Explicitly not `baseline-experts` or `baseline-routing`:
89|the combine part is graded on captured `y` and reference `weights`.

94|kernel otherwise unchanged — is predicted to cost <0.5 µs/layer (the

128|### C. The reference sum's association (`col_reduce_small`, size-4 axis)
129|
130|Per output element (fixed row, fixed column `d`), `reduce_col.h` runs:
131|`totals[i]` (4 column lanes per thread) start at `Sum::init = 0`; the loop
132|over the reduction (`r = lid.y; r < rows·4; r += lsize.y`, `lsize.y = 4`)
133|gives each `lid.y` lane exactly one product, so lane `j` holds
134|`0 + p_j = p_j` exactly; then, if `lsize.y > 1`, the threadgroup fold on
135|`lid.y == 0` computes `t = p_0; t = p_1 + t; t = p_2 + t; t = p_3 + t`,
136|each `op(a,b) = a + b` rounded once to f32. IEEE addition commutes, so the
137|reference association is exactly the left fold **((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃** with a
138|rounding after every add. That association does **not** change with rows:
139|the reduced axis is always size 4; more rows only add threadgroups /
140|non-column reductions. Round 1's boundary emulation already proved the
141|point from the candidate side: all 120 pure association trees of the four
142|products give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches to the grader
143|fingerprint, while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it exactly
144|(`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The 2.0-ULP touch*).

146|### D. The candidate's arithmetic (`block-0.metal:20-25`)
147|
148|The source writes the same left fold, `p₀ + p₁ + p₂ + p₃` as one f32
149|expression, then `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]`. Compiled as a single
150|Metal kernel (MLX `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, `slots.py:309-316`; no compiler
151|flags are expressible in `spec.json`), the mul+adds are FP-contracted
152|into FMAs: `fma(y_j, w_j, partial)` keeps the product unrounded, so `acc`
153|can differ from the reference fold by ~1 f32 ULP. The bf16 rounding of
154|`acc` absorbs that almost always; it flips only when `acc` lies within
155|the delta of a bf16 rounding midpoint, yielding a 1-ULP-different sum,
156|which the bf16 `+ shared` then preserves — or magnifies in ULP terms
157|when `shared ≈ −sum` cancels toward zero (the grader floors the ULP at
158|`|r| = 0.001`, `check_candidate.py:84-99`, so near-zero results report
159|large ULP gaps from tiny absolute differences). Attempt-2's explicit
160|`acc += product` loop shows the identical fingerprint (0.0 / 2.0 / 1.0),
161|so loop form and staging are exonerated too: only suppressing
162|contraction (e.g. the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary named)
163|while keeping the ((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ fold can close it. Counts under the
164|new grader (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-combine.json`,
165|summed over 20 layers; totals = rows·768·20 elements):
166|
167|| Size | Differ | Max ULP | Elements | Rate |
168||---|---|---|---|---|
169|| decode 1 row | 0 | 0.0 | 15,360 | 0 |
170|| decode 8 rows | 2 | 2.0 | 122,880 | 16 ppm |
171|| decode 32 rows | 2 | 1.0 | 491,520 | 4 ppm |
172|| prefill 127 rows | 6 | 1.0 | 1,950,720 | 3 ppm |
173|| prefill 1,016 rows | 50 | 16.0 | 15,605,760 | 3 ppm |
174|| prefill 2,048 rows | 130 | 32.0 | 31,457,280 | 4 ppm |
175|
176|The count grows with the element count at a roughly constant few-ppm
177|rate — more samples of the same rounding-boundary lottery, **not** a
178|kernel switch at prefill sizes (combine's MLX kernels are identical at
179|every row count; the 60-row `gather_qvm → gather_qmm_rhs` switch belongs
180|to the experts slot and cannot enter here, since the grader feeds
181|captured `y`). The larger max ULP at prefill is the tail of the same
182|lottery plus near-zero cancellation after `+ shared`. It fails G2 at
183|five of six sizes; in the model the round-1 kernel changed 7 of 32
184|vLLM sequences from token 0 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §2).
185|Folded in from explorer-grader's note below: the fix must hold at
186|2,048 rows, not only at decode sizes (the per-element sum is

282|def dim(expr, rows):

284|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")

303|def build(spec, sources, slot):
304|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks."""
305|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
306|    kernels = []
307|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
308|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
309|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
310|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
311|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
312|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
313|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
314|            header=header,
315|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
316|        )
317|        kernels.append((k, fn))
318|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
319|    if missing:
320|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
321|
322|    def run(**inputs):
323|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
324|        env = dict(inputs)
325|        for k, fn in kernels:
326|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
327|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
328|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
329|            outs = fn(
330|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
331|                template=[
332|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
333|                ],
334|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
335|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
336|                output_shapes=[
337|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
338|                ],
339|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
340|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
341|            )
342|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
343|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
344|
345|    return run

3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step

184|def chained(fn, layers, names):
185|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
186|
187|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
188|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
189|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
190|    """
191|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
192|    outs = []
193|    for layer in layers:
194|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
195|        if outs:
196|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
197|        out = fn(**args)
198|        if isinstance(out, dict):
199|            out = list(out.values())
200|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
201|    return outs

204|def timed(fn, layers, names):
205|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
206|    for _ in range(3):
207|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
208|    times = []
209|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
210|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
211|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
212|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
213|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

216|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
217|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
218|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        for call in calls:
221|            call()
222|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
223|    for i in range(REPEATS):
224|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
225|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
226|            calls[j]()
227|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
228|    return times

5|# From round 2, a kernel must be bit-exact at every size it runs at, prefill included, and the piece timing chains the layers
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's measurement of round 1 ([findings](../findings/muse-round-1.md)) found that round 1's final attempts, which passed the grader, broke the brief's end-to-end rule in the model, and that one of them slowed the decode step it was meant to speed up. The grader missed three things:
10|
11|1. **Sizes.** It tested a slot on a decode step's inputs only, at 1, 8 and 32 rows. The same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill, at 127 to 2,048 rows with 128-token prompts. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes, from `gather_qvm` to `gather_qmm_rhs`, and so does its rounding. Round 1's experts kernel copied `gather_qvm` bit for bit, and differed in 62% of its outputs at each prefill size.
12|2. **Exactness.** G2 allowed small differences: 2 bfloat16 units in the last place, and 10⁻⁴ for routing weights. End to end, the brief asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. Round 1's routing weights, within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences in 24 tokens.
13|3. **Latency.** The piece timing ran 20 layers' calls with no data between them, so the GPU could overlap them. At 1 row, round 1's experts kernel was 29% faster than the reference on overlapped calls and 66% slower on chained ones (`bench/micro/chain_timing.py`). In the model it slowed the decode step by 1.2 ms (22% in vLLM, 25% in plain MLX).
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose, before round 2:
16|- **every call:** the kernels run wherever `MoE.__call__` runs, the prefill included;
17|- **bit-exact** outputs;
18|- **chained** piece timing.
19|
20|## How it works
21|
22|- **G2 at two kinds of size.** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` checks every layer at:
23|  - the captured decode inputs, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
24|  - the first prefill chunk at 1, 8 and 32 requests (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows), recorded while it runs (`slots.capture_prefill`), with the prompts `time_candidates.py` uses.
25|- **Bit-exact.** An output passes only if it equals the reference's:
26|  - for routing, the 4 experts and their weights, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order;
27|  - for combine and experts, every element.
28|
29|  The grader still reports the largest gap, in units in the last place, to help find the cause. The reference checked against itself shows no difference at any size.
30|- **Chained timing.** Each layer's call takes one input through `link`, a single fused kernel that adds 0 × one value of the previous call's output, so the call can't start before the previous one finishes. Every function timed (reference, compiled, candidate and baseline) gets the same link. The chained times match those of a real data chain within 10%.
31|  - **Why not `mx.depends`:** it orders only the graph. In a test on 2026-11-04, round 1's experts kernel took 46 µs per layer with it at 1 row, as fast as with no dependency, against 133 to 195 µs with a real data dependency in three runs.
32|- **The end-to-end check and G3 are unchanged.**
33|  - `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` now takes several `SLOT=FOLDER` attempts.
34|  - It times each slot alone, against its own compiled reference, and all of them together.
35|
36|## Consequences
37|
38|- **No round-1 attempt passes the new G2,** so round 2 has no baseline in any slot. Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's final attempts are its starting points, named in Claude's findings.
39|- **The experts slot needs a kernel exact at prefill sizes,** matching `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding from 60 rows on, or a single design whose rounding matches both of MLX's kernels.
40|- **A grader run takes longer.** It loads the model (760 MB) for every slot and runs three prefill chunks.
41|- **The piece timing now includes one small link kernel per layer** for every function timed. That brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs.
42|- **Not covered:** prefill speed. G3 times decode steps only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token.
43|
44|## Considered options
45|
46|- **Decode calls only,** with MLX's code in the prefill. The kernels would need to be exact only at decode sizes, but they would no longer replace the whole MoE block. Not chosen: surucuonur asked for every call.
47|- **Keep the tolerances, and relax the token rule** to counting the sequences that differ. Simpler kernels, but the claim would become "the same model up to rounding", with a threshold to pick.
48|- **Keep independent timing,** and rely on G3 to catch latency. Round 2's builders would again rank attempts by a number that hid a 22% slowdown.
49|- **`mx.depends` for the chain.** No extra kernel, but it doesn't make the GPU wait.

1|// Fused combine: weight the 4 experts' bf16 outputs by fp32 weights, sum in
2|// fp32, round once to bf16, add shared — one kernel launch per layer, one
3|// thread per output element. Grid is (rows*768, 1, 1), threadgroup (256, 1, 1).
4|//
5|// Reference (slots.py:51-52): (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2)
6|//   .astype(bf16) + shared. y is [rows,4,768] bf16 row-contiguous, weights
7|//   [rows,4] f32, shared [rows,768] bf16, out [rows,768] bf16. The bfloat
8|//   conversion and the + shared use the same single-rounding ops as MLX's
9|//   copy_v/binary_vv kernels, and the 4-term fp32 sum order is free per the
10|//   hyp-3 boundary.
11|
12|uint idx = thread_position_in_grid.x;
13|uint row = idx / 768u;
14|uint d = idx - row * 768u;
15|
16|uint wbase = row * 4u;
17|uint ybase = row * 3072u + d; // 4*768
18|uint sbase = row * 768u + d;
19|
20|float acc = float(y[ybase]) * weights[wbase]
21|    + float(y[ybase + 768u]) * weights[wbase + 1u]
22|    + float(y[ybase + 1536u]) * weights[wbase + 2u]
23|    + float(y[ybase + 2304u]) * weights[wbase + 3u];
24|
25|out[sbase] = bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase];

23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.

66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

Diagnostics: `rows_other_experts` (rows whose expert *set* differs) and `max_rel_err`, the latter computed only over same-order rows ([check_candidate.py:122-128](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — a permuted row's weight error is invisible in the diagnostic, though the row still fails the gate. `passes` requires `rows_differ == 0` ([check_candidate.py:172-175](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). **Gone vs round 1:** the set-match pass, the 1e-6 near-tie exemption that skipped the weight check, and the 1e-4 relative tolerance (round-1 entry item 4). The reference's own tie choice between the 4th and 5th expert, and its order, must now be reproduced exactly ([brief:187](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md)).
42|- **G2 combine/experts** (`differences`, [check_candidate.py:90-99](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)): both sides cast bf16 → f32 and compared elementwise, `differ = (g != r) & ~(isnan(g) & isnan(r))` — NaN-vs-NaN counts as equal, everything else must be the same bits. `max_ulp` is **diagnostic only**: largest `|g−r| / ulp_bf16(r)` with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 ([check_candidate.py:84-99](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); overflow/NaN gaps clamp to 1e9. `check_combine` reports the first worst element as `row i column j` ([check_candidate.py:139-150](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); `check_experts` reshapes to `(rows, −1)` and decodes the flat index into row / expert slot / column ([check_candidate.py:153-169](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). `passes` requires `differ == 0`. **Gone vs round 1:** the 2-ULP pass ([brief:186-188](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md)); a single differing element in any layer at any of the six sizes fails G2, since global `g2 = all(s.get("pass"))` over every part+size ([check_candidate.py:308](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
43|- **`routing+combine` independence (unchanged, still biting):** parts are loaded, checked and timed separately ([check_candidate.py:53-64](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); the combine part is fed the captured/candidate-independent `y/weights/shared` of each size, never the candidate routing part's output — so the piece G2 cannot see a routing+combine interaction, and passing both parts is sufficient only because each part is now bit-exact.
44|
45|### 5. `check_candidate.py` — chained piece timing and the two bars (check_candidate.py:44-50, 178-228, 309-339)
46|
47|- **Callers:** runs only if `g2` passes ([check_candidate.py:309](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), and only at the three *decode* sizes (`ROWS = (1, 8, 32)`, [check_candidate.py:44](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) on the captured decode inputs ([check_candidate.py:311-312](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — prefill sizes are correctness-only.
48|- **The chain:** `link(a, prev) = a + (prev.reshape(-1)[:1] * 0)` as one `@mx.compile` fused kernel ([check_candidate.py:178-181](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). `chained` picks each part's smallest input (`min` by `size`: routing → `bias` [60], combine → `weights` [rows×4], experts → `inds` [rows×4]) and replaces it, from the second layer on, with `link(small, previous call's last output)`, so every call waits for the one before "as in a decode step" ([check_candidate.py:184-201](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Every timed function — reference, compiled, candidate, baseline — gets the identical link; `mx.depends` was rejected because it orders only the graph ([ADR 0010:31](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)). All 20 layers' outputs are kept alive until the single `mx.eval` (one GPU wait per repeat).
49|- **`timed`:** 3 warmup chained evals, then median of `REPEATS = 30` wall-clock (`perf_counter` around `mx.eval(chained(...))`) ÷ 20 → µs/layer ([check_candidate.py:204-213](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). This is the estimator for `reference` and `compiled` in all runs, and for `candidate` when no `--baseline` is given ([check_candidate.py:321-328](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); with several parts, per-part medians are summed into `row["candidate"]` etc.
50|- **`paired_times` (only with `--baseline`):** 3 warmups of each function, then per repeat the functions run in rotating order `[(i+k) % len]` so clock drift reaches both alike, each repeat a full chained 20-layer eval; per-repeat µs/layer per function ([check_candidate.py:216-228](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per row count, candidate and baseline times are accumulated *summed over parts per repeat* first ([check_candidate.py:323-326](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so for `routing+combine` the wins are counted on the summed time, not per part. Verdict adds `baseline`, per-row `wins_vs_baseline`, and `wins_needed` ([check_candidate.py:261-266, 329-334](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
51|- **What `beats_compiled` requires:** median `candidate < compiled` at **all three** row counts, strict, on the summed-over-parts medians ([check_candidate.py:334-335](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). No significance test — unlike the baseline rule, this compares medians alone, the practice ADR 0009 measured as noisy (same kernel vs itself: up to 5% between medians).
52|- **What `beats_baseline` requires:** candidate faster than baseline in at least `WINS_NEEDED` of the 30 paired repeats at **every** row count ([check_candidate.py:332-333](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). `WINS_NEEDED` is computed, not hardcoded: the smallest k with P(Bin(30, ½) ≥ k) < 0.01 → **22 of 30**, a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01 ([check_candidate.py:46-50](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Both bars must hold for a slot to stop (brief's rule, [brief:201](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md)); the verdict reports them independently (`beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, [check_candidate.py:337-339](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
53|- **Baseline loading:** `--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER` (repeatable; for `routing+combine` one combined attempt or `routing=` + `combine=`) must cover exactly the slot's parts or the run exits ([check_candidate.py:67-81](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). **Round-2 state:** no slot has a baseline — no round-1 attempt passes the new G2 ([ADR 0010:38](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md); round-2 README *Starting point*) — so the operative bar this round is `beats_compiled` only; the paired machinery is the next rounds' bar.
54|- **Neighbours / what did not change:** end-to-end greedy-token equality (24 tokens, 1 and 32 requests, plain + vLLM) and G3 (median of 3 shuffled repeats, must beat base and compiled beyond spread) still live in `time_candidates.py` / the brief ([brief:191-192](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md); [ADR 0010:32-34](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); `check_candidate` is explicitly "a guide; G3 decides" ([brief:199](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md)).
55|
56|### 6. Verdict shape (check_candidate.py:260, 336-345)
57|
58|`{slot, g1, g2, beats_compiled, correctness: {"<part> <kind> <rows>": {…stats, pass, worst_example?}}, timing_us_per_layer: {"rows N": {reference, compiled, candidate[, baseline, wins_vs_baseline]}}, error?}` plus, with `--baseline`, `{baseline, beats_baseline, wins_needed: "22 of 30 paired repeats"}`; printed as JSON and written to `--out` when given ([check_candidate.py:260-266, 336-345](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). On G2 failure there is **no timing at all** — correctness stats are the whole verdict.
59|
60|## What the grader still cannot see
61|
62|1. **Row counts between the six tested ones.** Correctness sizes are exactly {1, 8, 32, 127, 1016, 2048} ([check_candidate.py:44, 272-276](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); [slots.py:211](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Untested: 2–7, 9–31, 33–126, 128–1015, 1017–2047, >2048. Both internal thresholds are only *bracketed*, never pinpointed: the reference's sort at 16 rows sits between tested 8 and 32; MLX's `gather_qvm`→`gather_qmm_rhs` switch at 60 rows ([ADR 0010:11](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)) sits between tested 32 and 127. A kernel that branches on `rows` (readable via `*_shape` in Metal) can be exact at all six sizes and wrong in between; the correct branch threshold must come from MLX's dispatch source (quantized-kernels territory), not from the grader.
63|2. **Prefill beyond the first chunk of 128-token random prompts.** `capture_prefill` records only `ids[:, :chunk]` of seeded random ids ([slots.py:240-246](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Later chunks (KV cache already filled), other prompt lengths, real-token distributions, and mixed prefill+decode batches are never presented to a candidate. Expert-popularity and tie distributions at the tested sizes are those of random tokens, not of real prompts.
64|3. **Prefill speed.** Timing loops over decode `ROWS` only ([check_candidate.py:311](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); a kernel slower at 127–2048 rows passes `beats_compiled` unnoticed apart from time-to-first-token ([ADR 0010:42](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)). The 2048-row correctness run does exercise large grids, so gross grid/threadgroup breakage at scale is caught — slowness is not.
65|4. **Threadgroup memory.** Only the ≤1024-thread product is validated ([slots.py:327](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); the 32 KB limit ([brief:98](../../../claude/muse-agent-brief.md)) is enforced, if at all, by Metal itself and reported only as an opaque G1 exception. Declared threadgroup arrays in the source are never measured by the grader.
66|5. **Timing dependence.** (a) Every timed eval includes 20 `link` kernels (one per layer) for every function alike — a fixed additive cost that "brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs" ([ADR 0010:41](../../../claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); percentage gaps in the piece timing understate the kernel-only gap. (b) The link hangs the chain on a single scalar of the previous call's *last* output through the *smallest* input; ADR 0010 reports this matches a real data chain within 10%, but the grader itself never verifies that figure. (c) `beats_compiled` is a median-only strict `<` ([check_candidate.py:335](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) while the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between medians and the compiled reference varied up to 2× at 1 row between runs (ADR 0009) — a marginal `beats_compiled` can be noise in a way `beats_baseline` (sign test) cannot. (d) The measurement is host wall time around `mx.eval`, so CPU dispatch is inside the number; the GPU lock serialises runs but does not pin clocks. (e) Piece timing ≠ G3: round 1's experts starting point won overlapped, lost chained at 1 row, and the three slots together lost time each saved alone (round-2 README *Starting point*) — the chained timing fixes the overlap blindness, not the composition question (territory `g3`).
67|6. **Input diversity within a size.** Decode inputs are one captured step (step 8 of seeded 128-token random prompts, [slots.py:158-168](../../../bench/grader/slots.py) via round-1 item 2) and prefill inputs one seeded draw per request count. All 20 layers are covered at every size, but value-dependent behaviour (tie frequency, NaN/Inf paths, denormals) is sampled once; `differences` treats NaN-vs-NaN as equal ([check_candidate.py:93](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so a kernel producing NaN exactly where the reference does passes — correctly, since the reference is the contract.
68|
69|## Relations
70|
71|- **Fed by:** model territory (`MoE.__call__`, the code `make_moe_call` mirrors, [slots.py:97-119](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); `bench/micro/breakdown.py` (`MODEL`, `PREFILL_TOKENS = 2048`, prefill chunking); `time_candidates.py`'s prompts for `capture_prefill`; quantized-kernels territory (the 60-row kernel switch the prefill sizes expose); `models/muse-inputs/rows{1,8,32}.npz` (captured decode inputs, round-1 item 2).
72|- **Feeds:** builders (verdict JSON, the six-size exactness gate, chained-timing bars); the boundary agent (ordered routing equality, per-element equality, the two-kernel rounding problem for experts); the three `baseline-*` explorers (grader-side notes appended to their entries, see below); territory `g3` (piece-vs-end-to-end gap, §5 item 5e).
73|- **Change vs round 1 in one line per slot:** routing — set/tolerance/tie-exempt → ordered bitwise at 6 sizes; combine/experts — 2 ULP at 3 sizes → 0 differing elements at 6 sizes; timing — overlapped medians → chained medians, plus an optional paired sign-test bar that no slot can use yet.

77|None posted from this territory: the grader runs no decode-step kernels, and its blind spots (§ above) are contract limits, not lost decode time — per tracking.md (*Adapting to the others' work*) they are delivered as grader-side notes on the entries that own the cost instead of duplicate `ineff-grader-N` entries:

*written by boundary-3, 2026-11-04T03:54:22Z — delta to round 1's boundary. Only what changed is written here; every round-1 line not listed below still holds verbatim.*

Round 1's boundary is [hyp-3-fused-combine.md](../../implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md) *Boundary* (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md:19-62`: inputs/outputs table, before/after in `MoE.__call__`, identical-math, grader, GPU limits). I checked each of its lines against the starting point `muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (`spec.json`; `block-0.metal:12-25`) and against the current G2 (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:179,182-188`; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:22-29`; `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:90-99,139-150,172-175,277-308`). Still holding, not rewritten below: input/output names, dtypes and layouts at decode sizes; neighbour contracts (positional `weights[r,j]` ↔ `y[r,j,:]` pairing, shared expert outside the slots, residual-add consumer); the two bfloat16 rounding points in kind; the launch-spec surface; GPU limits. Baseline is `none` — no earlier attempt passes the current G2 (this entry, *Inefficiency*; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:38`). Three round-1 conclusions are retired: the 2-bfloat16-ULP tolerance, "the summation order of the 4 products is free within the 2-ULP tolerance", and "merging the astype and the `+ shared` roundings is acceptable if within 2 ULP" (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md:50-52`). Only what changed follows.

### Inputs and outputs — extended to the prefill sizes (changed)

Sources: the brief's combine table (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:49-62`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-32,51-52`. All arrays stay row-contiguous (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:24`); the harness flattens the port's lead dims, so the slot sees flat rows (`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119,105-118`). Unchanged shapes now also run at prefill sizes. `rows` is still read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` (`bench/grader/slots.py:323`); the grader adds prefill `127 / 1,016 / 2,048` rows (1/8/32 requests × 128-token prompts, first chunk; `bench/grader/slots.py:211,214-254`; `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:272-276`):

| | Name | Shape at decode 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Shape at prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| input | `y` | [1,4,768] / [8,4,768] / [32,4,768] | [127,4,768] / [1016,4,768] / [2048,4,768] | bfloat16, the 4 experts' outputs in `inds` order (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:53`) |
| input | `weights` | [1,4] / [8,4] / [32,4] | [127,4] / [1016,4] / [2048,4] | float32; `weights[r,j]` belongs to `y[r,j,:]` |
| input | `shared` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | [127,768] / [1016,768] / [2048,768] | bfloat16, the shared expert's output |
| output | `out` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | [127,768] / [1016,768] / [2048,768] | bfloat16; `(y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bfloat16) + shared` (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`) |

A decode step can still have any 1–32 rows and a prefill chunk other sizes again (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:24`); the kernel must be valid at every `rows`, not only the six tested ones (see *can't see*).

### Before and after — same neighbours, now also in prefill (domain changed)

Neighbour code is unchanged: experts' `y = self.experts(x, inds)` in `inds` order, routing's normalised ( `+1e-20` guard) and ×2.5-scaled float32 `weights`, shared expert's `shared = self.shared_expert(x)` outside all slots, then combine, then the residual add `h + feed_forward(...)` in `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232,258`; `bench/grader/slots.py:97-119,105-118`). What changed is the invocation domain: the same `MoE.__call__` runs the prefill first chunk, so the slot is now called at the prefill row counts above with the same expectations — `y[...,j,:]` always corresponds to `weights[...,j]` positionally, whatever per-row order routing emitted and whatever `SwitchGLU` sorts internally from rows ≥ 16 (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:181`; round-1 boundary, *Before (1)*). Checklist delta (per `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md` *The checklist*): producer `SwitchGLU` — holds; producer routing-weights chain — holds, and its values are now the exact reference weights at all six sizes (see *What the grader checks*); producer shared-expert MLP — holds; consumer residual add — holds, but now expects `out` bit-identical to the reference (see below), not within 2 ULP. Callers, callees, data and costs are as in round 1, with `rows` extended as above.

### What must stay identical — bit for bit, contraction-free (changed)

- **Tolerance removed.** Round 1 allowed every element within 2 bfloat16 ULP (ULP floored at `|r| = 0.001`); now every element must equal the reference bit for bit (`differ == 0` in every layer at all six sizes; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:186-188`; `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:90-99,139-150,172-175,308`). `max_ulp` is diagnostic only (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`). Combining the two bfloat16 roundings — e.g. adding `shared` in float32 and rounding once — is therefore no longer acceptable: it changes the reference arithmetic and fails on any element where the intermediate rounding mattered (retires round-1 boundary line 50's allowance).
- **The exact evaluation sequence (new, load-bearing).** The reference (`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`) runs eagerly as separate kernels, and a replacement must reproduce that sequence bit for bit (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist B–D; `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-1.md:20-43`):
  1. cast `y` bfloat16→float32 exactly (bf16 ⊂ f32; `copy_v`);
  2. each product `p_j = float(y[r,j,d]) · weights[r,j]` rounded **once** to float32 (the `binary_g` multiply kernel, `Multiply` is plain `x * y` — the product may not stay unrounded into the next add);
  3. fold the 4 products as **((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃** with a rounding after **every** add (the `col_reduce_small` sum: `Sum` is plain `a + b`, init 0, folded `t = p₀; t = p₁+t; t = p₂+t; t = p₃+t`; IEEE addition commutes, so this is exactly the left fold);
  4. round the sum **once** to bfloat16 (the `.astype`, `copy_v`, RNE);
  5. add `shared` in bfloat16 with a single rounding (`binary_vv` add).
  No reassociation (no pairwise/tree fold such as `(p₀+p₂)+(p₁+p₃)`), no fused multiply-add contraction at any step, and no other reordering is free any more. The fix the design names — suppress contraction, e.g. `metal::precise` operations or explicit rounding barriers, kernel otherwise unchanged (this entry, *Inefficiency*: "each product rounded once to float32, folded `((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃` with a rounding after every add, one bfloat16 round, then the bfloat16 add of `shared`") — is the only arithmetic change allowed; thread/layout decomposition stays free.
- **The reference's kernels do not change with the row count (new).** Unlike the experts slot, combine has no 60-row switch: its 5 eager kernels (`copy_v`, broadcast `binary_g` multiply, strided-small `col_reduce_small` sum, `copy_v`, `binary_vv` add; `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist B) are identical at every row count, the reduced axis is always size 4 (more rows only add threadgroups / non-column reductions), and the association in step 3 therefore does not change with `rows` (territory checklist C). The 60-row `gather_qvm → gather_qmm_rhs` switch belongs to the experts slot and cannot enter here, since the grader feeds captured `y` (territory checklist D; `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:277-304`). No `rows`-branched arithmetic is required — or permitted to differ: one evaluation sequence must hold at decode and prefill sizes alike, and a fix exact only at decode sizes fails at 2,048 rows (territory checklist D, folded grader note).
- **Tie rule and the order of the 4 pairs (kind unchanged, now exact).** No selection happens in this slot, so the 4th/5th-expert tie choice still belongs to routing only (round-1 boundary). What changed is that it is no longer insulated by tolerance: the `weights` this slot receives already embody the reference's tie choice, and combine must pair `weights[r,j]` with `y[r,j,:]` strictly positionally at every size — no re-sorting, re-picking or re-normalising experts, and no reordering of the 4 pairs beyond the fold in step 3. `weights` must still be treated as arbitrary finite float32: reference values are non-negative and sum to 2.5 per row, but a fused end-to-end model may feed anything finite (round-1 boundary, *Before (2)*).
- **Starting point against this boundary.** Checked line by line, `muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` keeps the shape/dtype/layout contract and both bfloat16 rounding points (`spec.json`: grid `rows*768`, threadgroup [256,1,1], inputs `y, weights, shared`, output `out` [rows,768] bfloat16; `block-0.metal:25`: `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]`), pairs positionally (`block-0.metal:16-23`), and writes the sum in the reference's left-fold order (`block-0.metal:20-23`). It fails this boundary on contraction only: compiled as a single Metal kernel, the compiler FP-contracts the mul+add chain into FMAs, keeping each product unrounded into its add, so `acc` can differ from the reference fold by ~1 float32 ULP and flip the bfloat16 rounding at a midpoint (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-1.md:15-43`). - **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.

Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.

17|512 threads per (row, expert-slot) pair, same grid `rows*2048`
18|threads = `rows*4` groups, same branch on `rows >= 60`, same
19|threadgroup buffers — and interleave gate and up in the decode
20|branch only:
21|
22|- **Before (attempt-1):** simdgroup `b` (`b < 12`) ran
23|  `qvm_block(gate, block b)` to completion (24 strided K steps per
24|  lane: `k = lane, lane+32, ..., lane+744`; each step loads 4 weight
25|  words + scale/bias for that `k`, then accumulates 32 outputs),
26|  stored `tg_gate`, then ran `qvm_block(up, block b)` the same way
27|  and stored `tg_up`. The two blocks' K loops were fully sequential:
28|  up's first load waited for gate's last accumulate.
29|- **Now:** simdgroup `b` runs one merged loop,
30|  `qvm_gate_up_pair` (block-1). For each strided `k`, both blocks'
31|  loads are issued first — gate's 4 weight words, scale and bias,
32|  then up's 4 weight words, scale and bias (plus the shared
33|  `tg_x[k]`, read once) — and only then do the two accumulation
34|  passes run, gate's 32 terms then up's 32 terms, into separate
35|  accumulators `pg`/`pu`. The next `k`'s loads therefore sit behind
36|  twice the issued load traffic per step, and each block's load
37|  latency has the other block's loads/compute to hide behind
38|  (double-buffering the two blocks' weight/scale/x loads within
39|  the step). Lane 0 then stores both blocks in one loop:
40|  `tg_gate[b*32+j] = (bfloat)pg[j]`, `tg_up[b*32+j] = (bfloat)pu[j]`.
41|
42|Everything else is copied, not redesigned:
43|
44|- **Per-block bits unchanged.** In `qvm_gate_up_pair`, each block's
45|  adds run in exactly `qvm_block`'s order: the same strided `k`
46|  sequence, the same float32 dequant terms
47|  `x * (s0 * (by & 0x0f) + bias)` /
48|  `x * (s1 * (by & 0xf0) + bias)` with `s1 = scale/16`, in the same
49|  per-output sequence; `pg` and `pu` are independent accumulators,
50|  so interleaving the two blocks cannot reorder either block's own
51|  adds. Each accumulator then gets the identical
52|  `#pragma clang loop unroll(full)` `simd_sum` tree as `qvm_block`.
53|  Down still calls `qvm_block` verbatim (verified by diff against
54|  attempt-1: `qvm_block` and `qmm_accum` bodies byte-identical;
55|  block-0 differs only in the header comment and the decode
56|  gate/up call site).
57|- **Prefill (`rows >= 60`) unchanged.** Attempt-1's scalar
58|  `qmm_accum` (weight rounded to bfloat16 first,
59|  `float(bfloat(scale·q+bias))`, then K accumulated contiguously in
60|  `BK=32` tile order, one output per lane) is copied byte-identical
61|  for gate, up and down, and block-0's prefill branch is untouched —
62|  the interleaving does not touch the prefill arithmetic.
63|- Same four bfloat16 rounding points (gate, up, hidden via the
64|  shared full-bfloat16 silu-mul, down — silu code byte-identical),
65|  fp32 accumulation, positional `y[r,j]` (`pair = r*4 + j`), and
66|  the same `rows >= 60` dispatch threshold from `x_shape[0]`, not
67|  the grader's bracketing sizes. No kernel split, no threadgroup
68|  count change, no new device-memory intermediate.
69|
70|## Which inefficiency it removes, and how
71|
72|- `ineff-baseline-experts-2` (chained 1-row latency): attempts 1–3
73|  all plateau at 103.6–109.5 µs/layer at 1 row despite 4, 12+24 and
74|  48+96 threadgroups per call, so the binding cost past 4 groups is
75|  each block's serial K chain (24 + 24 + 12 strided
76|  load-accumulate steps, gate→up→down ordered by the hidden
77|  dependency) executed with only one block's loads in flight per
78|  simdgroup at a time. Interleaving gate and up — the two
79|  independent, equal-length (24-step) chains — puts both blocks'
80|  loads in flight in every step without touching any block's
81|  `simd_sum` order, the only lever attempt-3's analysis left inside
82|  the fused kernel. Down (12 steps) is left sequential: it cannot
83|  start before the silu barrier in any case.
84|- `ineff-baseline-experts-1` (prefill G2 gate): already removed by
85|  attempt-1's branch; kept by reusing its scalar `qmm_accum`
86|  verbatim.
87|- `ineff-baseline-experts-3` (per-pair re-reads): deliberately
88|  kept, as in attempts 1–3 — weight bytes per pair stay
89|  552,960 B; the interleaving changes load scheduling, not bytes.
90|
91|## Limits (by hand; the grader does not check the 32 KB cap)
92|
93|512 threads/group ≤ 1,024 (spec unchanged, verified identical).
94|Threadgroup memory unchanged from attempt-1: `tg_x[768] +
95|tg_gate[384] + tg_up[384] + tg_h[384]` bfloat16 = **3,840 B** of
96|32,768 B, rows-independent. The only new state is register-local:
97|a second 32-float accumulator `pu[32]` beside `p[32]` and a second
98|4-word load buffer inside `qvm_gate_up_pair` — the register cost
99|is the risk noted below. Grid scales as `rows*4` groups, so the
100|kernel is valid at every `rows ≥ 1`, on both sides of 60.
101|
102|## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (chained, grader timing)
103|
104|Weight bytes per layer (552,960 B/pair, of which gate+up are
105|368,640 B = 2/3): 2.21 / 17.69 / 70.78 MB at 4 / 32 / 128 pairs.
106|Attempt-1 chained (this round's grader): 104.3 / 193.3 / 535.7
107|µs/layer = effective 21.2 / 91.5 / 132.1 GB/s; compiled (same run)
108|77.6 / 235.7 / 791.6.
109|
110|- **1 row: 90.** Latency-bound (floor 2.21 MB ÷ 200 GB/s =
111|  11.1 µs). Gate+up are 48 of the 60 serial product steps and 2/3
112|  of the pair bytes, so ≈ 2/3 × 104.3 ≈ 69 µs of attempt-1's time
113|  is the gate/up chains (the rest: down's 12 steps, `tg_x` load,
114|  silu, barriers, chained launch/link). Issuing both blocks' loads
115|  before accumulating doubles the loads outstanding per step; if
116|  that hides ≈ 20% of the gate/up chain's exposed latency
117|  (0.20 × 69 ≈ 14 µs), the layer lands at ≈ **90 µs** — still
118|  above the compiled 77.6, closing about half the remaining gap.
119|  Risk: the second accumulator's register pressure could spill or
120|  cut resident groups and hand the saving back.
121|- **8 rows: 178.** Streaming: 17.69 MB. Attempt-1 ran 91.5 GB/s
122|  with one block's 4 words in flight per simdgroup step; 8 words
123|  (plus two scale/bias pairs) per step should lift memory-level
124|  parallelism to ≈ 99 GB/s → 17.69 MB ÷ 99 GB/s ≈ **178 µs**,
125|  keeping attempt-1's win over compiled 235.7.
126|- **32 rows: 505.** Already near-saturated at attempt-1's
127|  132.1 GB/s; the same MLP lift, partly offset by register
128|  pressure at 128 groups, to ≈ 140 GB/s → 70.78 MB ÷ 140 GB/s ≈
129|  **505 µs**, keeping the win over compiled 791.6.
130|
131|G2 prediction: pass at all six sizes with `differ == 0` — decode
132|interleaving reorders only *between* blocks, never within a
133|block's add sequence, and the prefill path is byte-identical to
134|attempt-1's, which already matched `gather_qmm_rhs` bit for bit.
135|
136|## Verdict
137|
138|G1 pass; **G2 pass at all six sizes, differ 0 / max_ulp 0.0
139|everywhere** (decode 1/8/32 and prefill 127/1,016/2,048) — the
140|interleaving kept attempt-1's bits in both regimes: per-block
141|`qvm_block` add order unchanged by the within-step interleave, and
142|the byte-identical scalar `qmm_accum` prefill path matched
143|`gather_qmm_rhs` again. Chained timing µs/layer (this run;
144|candidate vs reference vs compiled): **1 row 94.0 / 81.2 / 73.5
145|(loses both)**; 8 rows 177.0 / 252.1 / 239.0 (wins); 32 rows
146|591.3 / 799.2 / 796.3 (wins). `beats_compiled` false — only the
147|1-row size misses, as in attempt-1. Baseline `none` — no
148|`wins_vs_baseline`/`beats_baseline`.
149|
150|Against attempt-1 (different run; compiled shifted 77.6 → 73.5
151|at 1 row between runs, so treat cross-run deltas as indicative):
152|94.0 vs 104.3 at 1 row (**−9.9%**), 177.0 vs 193.3 at 8 rows
153|(**−8.4%**), 591.3 vs 535.7 at 32 rows (**+10.4% regression**).
154|This is the first attempt to move below attempt-1's 103.6–109.5
155|µs/layer 1-row plateau (attempts 1–3) at any size, and it does so
156|at 1 and 8 rows — but it spends part of attempt-1's 32-row win.
157|
158|## Miss analysis (prediction 90 / 178 / 505, measured 94.0 / 177.0 / 591.3)
159|
160|Misses are +4.4% / −0.6% / +17.1% — all inside the 20% bar, so no
161|formal miss, but the 32-row *direction* was wrong (predicted
162|−6% vs attempt-1, measured +10.4%), and that needs explaining:
163|
164|1. **The interleave works where latency binds.** Effective
165|   bandwidth on pair bytes: 23.5 GB/s at 1 row (attempt-1: 21.2)
166|   and 99.9 GB/s at 8 rows (attempt-1: 91.5). Doubling the loads
167|   outstanding per K step (8 weight words + two scale/bias pairs
168|   issued before either accumulation) hid enough of each block's
169|   load latency to break the 103.6–109.5 plateau that three
170|   threadgroup packings could not — confirming attempt-3's
171|   diagnosis that the per-block serial chain, not group count,
172|   was the 1-row lever. The gain is real but partial: 94.0 still
173|   loses to compiled 73.5, so roughly 20 µs/layer of the 1-row
174|   cost (chained launch/link, `tg_x` load, silu, barriers, down's
175|   still-sequential 12-step chain and its two waves) remains
176|   unoverlapped.
177|2. **At 32 rows the second accumulator is the tax.** 119.7 GB/s
178|   vs attempt-1's 132.1 GB/s. Once 128 groups saturate the GPU,
179|   exposed load latency is already hidden by group-level
180|   parallelism, so the interleave buys nothing — and its cost,
181|   a second live 32-float accumulator plus a second 4-word load
182|   buffer per thread for the whole K loop, is paid in register
183|   pressure and therefore resident-group occupancy on every
184|   streaming step. The prediction's assumed MLP lift to
185|   140 GB/s double-counted parallelism the group count already
186|   provided.
187|3. **The 8-row point separates the two regimes:** same register
188|   cost as 32 rows, but only 32 groups per call, so per-group
189|   load overlap still pays (91.5 → 99.9 GB/s, prediction exact).
190|   The crossover between "latency-bound, interleave wins" and
191|   "occupancy-bound, interleave taxes" sits between 8 and 32
192|   rows in this run.
193|
194|Lesson for `ineff-baseline-experts-2`: the serial-chain lever is
195|real (first sub-plateau 1-row result: 94.0), but a uniform
196|interleave trades it against streaming occupancy. The two
197|regimes want different code, and both arithmetics are
198|bit-identical, so the choice between them is free.
199|
200|**Next change (one):** make the interleave row-conditional
201|inside the same fused kernel — `qvm_gate_up_pair` below the
202|latency/occupancy crossover (e.g. `rows <= 8`), attempt-1's
203|sequential `qvm_block` gate then up above it — keeping the
204|1/8-row wins (94.0/177.0) while restoring attempt-1's 32-row
205|register profile (535.7). Both branches keep every block's
206|add order, so G2 is unaffected by where the crossover sits.

2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

The findings name the pieces that cost the most.

11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. 14|
15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;

21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

1|# Attempt 1 — builder-3-a, single fused kernel, thread-per-output (direction a)
2|
3|First attempt in this direction: one Metal kernel per layer fusing the whole
4|combine chain (bf16→fp32 cast, multiply, sum, fp32→bf16 cast, + shared). One
5|thread per output element on a rows×768 grid, threadgroup 256 (768 = 3×256,
6|so the grid is always whole threadgroups). Each thread loads its 4 bf16
7|values, converts exactly to fp32, weights, sums in fp32, rounds once with
8|`bfloat(acc)`, and adds `shared` with the same single-rounding bf16 add as
9|MLX's `binary_vv`.
10|
11|## Inefficiency removed
12|
13|`ineff-model-2`: each layer's weighting launches 5 tiny kernels (AsType,
14|Multiply, Sum, AsType, Add) costing 0.61 ms/step at 1 row for ~6 MB of
15|activations — pure launch overhead on an overhead-bound chain. This attempt
16|replaces all 5 with 1 launch/layer, keeping both bf16 rounding points of the
17|reference (`slots.py:51-52`): the astype before `+ shared`, then the bf16
18|add. The 4-term fp32 sum order is free per the hyp-3 boundary.

27|holds 3 / 24 / 96 threadgroups, so amortization is at least as good as

31|- 8 rows: 24 + 0.4 ≈ **24 µs**

13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal:20-25`)
16|writes the 4-term f32 sum as one expression,
17|`float(y0)·w0 + float(y1)·w1 + float(y2)·w2 + float(y3)·w3`, then
18|`bfloat(acc) + shared`. Compiled as a single Metal kernel, the compiler
19|FP-contracts the mul+add pairs into FMAs, keeping each product unrounded
20|into its add. The reference can never do this: `ref_combine`
21|(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`) runs eagerly as separate kernels —
22|`binary_g` multiply (`Multiply` is plain `x * y`, product rounded once
23|to f32), then `col_reduce_small` (`Sum` is plain `a + b`, init 0) folding
24|((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ with a rounding after every add, then `copy_v` bf16
25|round, then `binary_vv` bf16 add (headers under
26|`.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`;
27|full mapping in `territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist B–D). The
28|candidate's `acc` therefore differs from the reference fold by ~1 f32
29|ULP on some elements; the bf16 rounding absorbs it except when `acc`
30|sits at a rounding midpoint, and the following `+ shared` can magnify
31|the reported gap when it cancels toward zero (ULP floored at
32|`|r| = 0.001`, `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`).

128|### C. The reference sum's association (`col_reduce_small`, size-4 axis)
129|
130|Per output element (fixed row, fixed column `d`), `reduce_col.h` runs:
131|`totals[i]` (4 column lanes per thread) start at `Sum::init = 0`; the loop
132|over the reduction (`r = lid.y; r < rows·4; r += lsize.y`, `lsize.y = 4`)
133|gives each `lid.y` lane exactly one product, so lane `j` holds
134|`0 + p_j = p_j` exactly; then, if `lsize.y > 1`, the threadgroup fold on
135|`lid.y == 0` computes `t = p_0; t = p_1 + t; t = p_2 + t; t = p_3 + t`,
136|each `op(a,b) = a + b` rounded once to f32. IEEE addition commutes, so the
137|reference association is exactly the left fold **((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃** with a
138|rounding after every add. That association does **not** change with rows:
139|the reduced axis is always size 4; more rows only add threadgroups /
140|non-column reductions. Round 1's boundary emulation already proved the
141|point from the candidate side: all 120 pure association trees of the four
142|products give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches to the grader
143|fingerprint, while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it exactly
144|(`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The 2.0-ULP touch*).

146|### D. The candidate's arithmetic (`block-0.metal:20-25`)
147|
148|The source writes the same left fold, `p₀ + p₁ + p₂ + p₃` as one f32
149|expression, then `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]`. Compiled as a single
150|Metal kernel (MLX `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, `slots.py:309-316`; no compiler
151|flags are expressible in `spec.json`), the mul+adds are FP-contracted
152|into FMAs: `fma(y_j, w_j, partial)` keeps the product unrounded, so `acc`
153|can differ from the reference fold by ~1 f32 ULP. The bf16 rounding of
154|`acc` absorbs that almost always; it flips only when `acc` lies within
155|the delta of a bf16 rounding midpoint, yielding a 1-ULP-different sum,
156|which the bf16 `+ shared` then preserves — or magnifies in ULP terms
157|when `shared ≈ −sum` cancels toward zero (the grader floors the ULP at
158|`|r| = 0.001`, `check_candidate.py:84-99`, so near-zero results report
159|large ULP gaps from tiny absolute differences). Attempt-2's explicit
160|`acc += product` loop shows the identical fingerprint (0.0 / 2.0 / 1.0),
161|so loop form and staging are exonerated too: only suppressing
162|contraction (e.g. the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary named)

164|new grader (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-combine.json`,

167|| Size | Differ | Max ULP | Elements | Rate |
168||---|---|---|---|---|
169|| decode 1 row | 0 | 0.0 | 15,360 | 0 |
170|| decode 8 rows | 2 | 2.0 | 122,880 | 16 ppm |
171|| decode 32 rows | 2 | 1.0 | 491,520 | 4 ppm |
172|| prefill 127 rows | 6 | 1.0 | 1,950,720 | 3 ppm |
173|| prefill 1,016 rows | 50 | 16.0 | 15,605,760 | 3 ppm |
174|| prefill 2,048 rows | 130 | 32.0 | 31,457,280 | 4 ppm |

# Hypothesis 3: fused combine kernel

- **Owner:** lead
- **Status:** ready
- **Version:** 4
- **Updated:** 2026-11-03T22:35:00Z
- **Next:** none — attempt-1 goes to G3

## Inefficiency

Slot `combine`. One entry:

- `ineff-model-2` (rank 5, mean 4.3% of step): each layer's weighting launches 5 kernels (bf16→fp32 cast, multiply, sum, fp32→bf16 cast, add shared) costing 0.61 ms at 1 row and 0.33 ms at 32 rows for ~6 MB of activations. Fusion to 1 kernel/layer saves 0.47 / 0.30 / 0.19 ms at 1/8/32 rows.

Design: one Metal kernel per layer that weights the 4 experts' bf16 outputs by the fp32 weights, sums in fp32, rounds once to bf16, and adds the shared expert. G2: every element within 2 bf16 ULP (floor at 0.001). Note the piece-harness lesson from hyp-2: the fused-kernel floor is ~24 µs/layer, not 6.81 µs — predict against the harness, and G3 decides the real saving.

## Boundary

### Inputs and outputs

Source: the brief's combine table (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:49-62`) and `bench/grader/slots.py:19-32,51-52`. All arrays row-contiguous (brief:24). The harness flattens the port's lead dims, so the slot sees flat rows (slots.py:107,116).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| input | `y` | [1,4,768] / [8,4,768] / [32,4,768] | bfloat16 | the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order (brief:53) |

| input | `shared` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | the shared expert's output |
| output | `out` | [1,768] / [8,768] / [32,768] | bfloat16 | `(y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bfloat16) + shared` |

### Before and after in `MoE.__call__`

Source: `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232` and the split harness `bench/grader/slots.py:105-119`.

- **Before (1), the experts call:** `y = self.experts(x, inds)` (`mobilemoe.py:230`) produces `y` in `inds` order (brief:53). From rows ≥ 16 `SwitchGLU` sorts pairs by expert internally and unscatters the result (`switch_layers.py:181`), but that is invisible here: `y[..., j, :]` always corresponds to `weights[..., j]` positionally, whatever per-row order routing emitted.
- **Before (2), routing weights:** `scores` normalized (`+1e-20` guard) and scaled × 2.5 in float32 (`mobilemoe.py:226-228`, `slots.py:48`). Reference values are non-negative and sum to 2.5 per row, but a fused end-to-end model may feed anything finite — the kernel must treat `weights` as arbitrary finite float32.
- **Before (3), the shared expert:** `self.shared_expert(x)` (`mobilemoe.py:232`), a dense int4 `MLP(dim=768, hidden=1536)` (`mobilemoe.py:215,131-139`), computed on the same `x` as the routed path, outside all slots — a slot kernel may not change it.
- **After:** the residual add `h + feed_forward(...)` in `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258`), a bf16 add on `[rows,1,768]`, then the next layer. It expects `out` exactly as the reference value below, within G2.

Checklist (per `tracking.md`) for each neighbour:

- **Producer `SwitchGLU(x, inds)`.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:230`). Callees: `gather_qmm` per product plus internal sort/unsort from rows ≥ 16 (`switch_layers.py:176-199`) — all upstream of the slot. Data: `y` [rows,4,768] bf16. Neighbours: routing before it; this slot after. Cost: the experts slot (hyp-1), untouched. Invariants: positional pairing — column `j` of `y` pairs with `weights[j]` as given; the slot must not re-sort or re-pick experts.
- **Producer routing-weights chain.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:226-228`). Callees: none into the slot — it only supplies `weights`. Data: `weights` [rows,4] f32. Neighbours: top-4 selection before (untouched). Cost: the routing slot (hyp-2, ready), untouched. Invariants: no range assumption beyond finite float32.
- **Producer shared-expert MLP.** Callers: `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:232`). Callees: 3 quantized matmuls + one fused silu-mul (`tables.md:141-144`: 4 kernels/layer, 80/step). Data: `shared` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: inside the slot boundary as input, outside all slots as computation. Cost: knock-out 0.51 ms @1, 2.90 ms @32 (`step-breakdown.md:172,213`), untouched. Invariants: bf16 values; the slot reads them as-is.
- **Consumer residual add.** Callers: `DecoderLayer.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:258`). Callees: none (plain bf16 add). Data: `out` [rows,768] bf16. Neighbours: next layer's input_norm after. Cost: outside the slot. Invariants: `out` bit-compatible with the reference within G2 — the residual add amplifies nothing, but end-to-end greedy tokens (brief:185) feel any drift.

### What must stay identical

- **Rounding points:** the reference (`slots.py:51-52`, brief:61) casts `y` bf16→fp32 (exact), multiplies by the fp32 weights and sums the 4 terms in fp32, rounds the sum once to bf16 (the `.astype`), then adds `shared` in bf16. Today that is 5 kernels/layer: `copy_v`, broadcast `binary_g` multiply, strided-small `col_reduce_small` sum, `copy_v`, `binary_vv` add (`territory-other-kernels.md` checklist G, `tables.md:140`). The two bf16 roundings — the astype and the add — are the contract: a kernel that merges them (e.g. adding `shared` in fp32 and rounding once) changes the reference arithmetic and is acceptable only if every element still lands within 2 bf16 ULP at every row count and every input. Boundary checks will probe any such move beyond the captured inputs.
- **Tie rule:** no selection happens in this slot, so the 4th/5th within-1e-6 tie freedom (brief:183) belongs to routing only. Combine must pair `weights[r,j]` with `y[r,j,:]` strictly positionally — no re-sorting, re-picking, or re-normalizing experts.
- **Allowed reorderings:** the summation order of the 4 (row, j) products per output element is free within the 2-ULP tolerance, as is any thread/layout decomposition. Nothing else may move: shapes, dtypes, the fp32 accumulation, the single astype before `+ shared`, and the positional `weights[j]` ↔ `y[j]` pairing all stay.

### What the grader checks, and what it can't see

- **G1** compiles the Metal and runs it on the captured inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows (brief:181, `check_candidate.py:206`).
- **G2 combine** checks exact shape [rows,768] and bf16 dtype, and every element within 2 bf16 ULP of the reference with the ULP floored at |r| = 0.001 (`check_candidate.py:44-47,96-109`); `pass` iff all 20 layers pass (`check_candidate.py:133-138,192-197`). Inputs are captured from all 20 layers of one real decode step per row count (`slots.py:137-171`). In a `routing+combine` candidate each part is checked on its own and combine receives the captured reference weights, never the candidate's (brief:171, `check_candidate.py:96-98,181-187`). Piece timing (median of 30 × all-20-layers eval ÷ 20) must beat `mx.compile(ref_combine)` at all three row counts to stop the slot (brief:193,195, `check_candidate.py:209-226`).
- **What it can't see:** row counts other than 1, 8 and 32 — a decode step can have any row count from 1 to 32 (brief:24); inputs other than the captured ones (other prompts, later decode steps, non-reference weights from a fused routing kernel); threadgroup-memory use near the 32 KB limit (`slots.build` enforces only the 1024-thread cap, `slots.py:275`); results that depend on thread timing; the end-to-end greedy-token check (24 tokens at 1 and 32 requests, plain MLX and vLLM) and G3 full-step timing, which the team runs after merging (brief:185-186,195). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.

### The GPU limits

At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (brief:98); `grid` counts threads, not threadgroups (brief:175). Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` available in Metal (brief:99).

  no overread (`block-0.metal:27-28,47,53`). Bit-exactness of the staging
  is corroborated by the identical G2 fingerprints (0.0/2.0/1.0) of both
  attempts: any staging error would move the touch.

### The 2.0-ULP touch (both attempts): FMA contraction, not a defect

CPU emulation (pure numpy, no GPU/model; bf16 RNE validated 0/20006 vs an
exact rational oracle) of candidate-vs-reference on all 629,760 captured
elements:

- The reference is the pure mul-then-add chain: MLX v0.32.4
  `col_reduce_small` computes `op(new, totals) = new + totals`
  (`reduce_col.h`), and with the (32,4,1) strided-small dispatch
  (`reduce.cpp`, `threadgroup_y = min(8, …, 4) = 4`) each element lands on
  its own thread, so the reference association is the linear chain —
  bit-identical to an uncontracted candidate (IEEE add commutes).
- The Metal compiler FP-contracts the candidate's mul+add chain into FMA:
  the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces the grader fingerprint **exactly**,
  (0.0, 2.0, 1.0) at 1/8/32 rows, in two contraction shapes; all 120 pure
  mul association trees give ≤1.0 on rows8 with zero fingerprint matches —
  ruling out sum order as the source.
- Realistic risk: 0 bad elements in 20M triplet-resampled captured elements
  (true y/weights/shared joint distribution) for the FMA evaluations and
  trees alike; max exactly 2.0. Exceedance needs adversarially constructed
  cancellation (`shared ≈ −acc` to <2%): max 8.0 there, a construction
  absent from real data. The brief's G2 note (brief:184) budgets exactly
  this class of difference, and the remaining gates (captured-only G2,
  greedy-token end-to-end, G3 timing) are insensitive to it.

Optional, not required: if the team wants nonzero margin at rows8, qualify
the accumulator `precise` (inhibits FMA contraction) and re-grade; both
attempts pass the gates as they stand.

## Decision

Best: `muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (builder-3-a, thread-per-output). Why: beats compiled at all three row counts by the wider relative margin (17.2 / 17.0 / 18.5 vs 22.9 / 26.2 / 28.0: −25 / −35 / −34%, against attempt-2's −14 / −30 / −35%); simpler (no threadgroup memory, fully independent threads); builder-3-b concedes it stays the pick. Both pass G1, G2 and boundary checks. No hardening round: both kernels sit on the ~17 µs/layer dispatch floor, flat across row counts with traffic ≤1.4 µs — no speed change worth making. The 8-row 2.0-ULP touch is FMA contraction, proven max exactly 2.0 on realistic inputs with zero exceedances (only adversarial `shared ≈ −acc` cancellation exceeds it); boundary-3's optional `precise`-accumulator margin-buy is noted for a later round, not worth a re-grade now. G3 should show: a faster step at all three concurrencies. First attempt in this direction (round 2, `hyp-3-combine-exact`, slot
`combine`, baseline `none`). Builds on the starting point
`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (`block-0.metal:12-25`,
`spec.json`: grid `rows*768`, threadgroup [256,1,1], no threadgroup
memory). The starting point is not a baseline: under round 2's bit-exact
G2 it fails at five of six sizes on FMA contraction alone (decode
0 / 2 / 2 differ, prefill 6 / 50 / 130; `ineff-baseline-combine-1`,
`territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist D), so it counts as the attempt
this one changes.

## What changed

Only the arithmetic. Indexing, grid, threadgroup, inputs/outputs and the
final line `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` are verbatim from the starting
point. The single-expression sum

```metal
float acc = float(y0)*w0 + float(y1)*w1 + float(y2)*w2 + float(y3)*w3;
```

which the compiler FP-contracts into FMAs (each product kept unrounded
into its add), becomes seven fma-free stepwise ops with explicit
rounding barriers:

```metal
volatile float p0 = float(y[ybase]) * weights[wbase];        // rounded to f32
volatile float p1 = float(y[ybase+768u]) * weights[wbase+1u];
volatile float p2 = float(y[ybase+1536u]) * weights[wbase+2u];
volatile float p3 = float(y[ybase+2304u]) * weights[wbase+3u];
volatile float s01 = p0 + p1;                                // rounded to f32
volatile float s012 = s01 + p2;                              // rounded to f32
volatile float acc = s012 + p3;                              // rounded to f32
out[sbase] = bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase];                    // verbatim
```

Each `volatile` store materialises its f32 value, so no product can stay
unrounded into the next add and no add can be fused with a later mul;
the fold is exactly `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3` with a rounding after every add,
then one bfloat16 round and the single-rounding bfloat16 `+ shared`,
matching the reference's separate kernels (`binary_g` multiply,
`col_reduce_small` sum, `copy_v`, `binary_vv`; `slots.py:51-52`,
Boundary steps 1–5). No reassociation, no `fma`, no threadgroup memory.

Note on spelling: the literal `precise float` qualifier does not compile
under MLX 0.32.4 (`metal::precise` is a function namespace in the MLX
header, e.g. `metal::precise::exp`; a leading `precise` is parsed as
that namespace and rejected). Volatile stepwise barriers are the
"explicit rounding barriers" the hypothesis design names as the
alternative to `metal::precise` operations, with the same semantics:
every mul rounds once to f32, every add rounds once to f32. Probes
outside the grader (random [512,4,768] inputs vs the eager MLX
reference, 3 × 393,216 elements) gave differ 3–4 for the starting
point's contracted expression and differ 0 for this kernel.

`ineff-baseline-combine-1` (confirmed, gate): FMA contraction breaks
bit-exactness and forfeits the slot's whole saving while G2 fails.
`ineff-baseline-combine-2` (confirmed, keep) is retained, not removed:
the kernel stays on the ~17 µs/layer dispatch floor (one launch/layer,
traffic + compute < 1.6 µs even at 32 rows).
